Seizures

Little signs had begun sprouting in Kalawan. On each signboard appeared a man’s name and two numbers: the length and width of his plot. These were not Kalawan men. They were newcomers, arriving to claim property. Their plots were tracts of forest, brush, or grass; all that showed of them were the little signs.

原页 46

强占

小牌子开始在卡拉万冒出来。每块牌子上出现一个男人的名字和两个数字：他那块地的长和宽。这些人不是卡拉万的男人。他们是新来者，来主张财产。他们的地块是森林、灌木或草地；能显示的只有那些小牌子。

原页 46

Yet these plots had not been unclaimed. There is no unclaimed land in Kalawan; that’s what makes it a settlement. But the technologies of “claiming” are not those recognized by the Indonesian state or regional authorities. No one, for example, had thought of Kalawan land as a series of ownable plots. In the 1980s, the village as a collective had claimed a territory in which elders must be consulted to determine rights of use. Newcomers asked for permission to move into the village; elders negotiated disagreements about land use. Personal territories were marked by the plantings and histories of old users and claimed by their descendants. Some of these territories overlapped and supported diverse kinds of claims, reflecting the variety of ways that fields, brush, and forest could be used. This was not considered a problem.

原页 46

然而这些地块并非无主。卡拉万没有无主土地；这正是它成为一个定居点的原因。但“主张”的技术不是印尼国家或地区当局所承认的那些。例如，没有人曾把卡拉万的土地想成一系列可拥有的地块。20世纪80年代，村庄作为一个集体主张了一片领土，在其中必须咨询长老来确定使用权。新来者请求允许搬入村庄；长老们协商关于土地使用分歧。个人领土由旧使用者的种植和历史标记，并由其后代主张。其中一些领土重叠，支持多种主张，反映了田地、灌木和森林可被使用的多样方式。这并不被视为问题。

原页 47

In the 1990s, the Korean Development Company (Kodeco) put a logging road through Kalawan, and the village was forced into greater regional visibility. The police began to sell plots of land to immigrants, and particularly to Javanese transmigrants brought to work on the tree plantations but eager to move off-plantation to enter the more profitable trade in natural resources. Kalawan residents protested. The land was Kalawan orchard land, tended by its owners and charted for eventual reuse as farms. They asked customary leaders to intervene. But no one dared to go against the armed forces. “ ‘State land,’ the soldiers said. If you disagree they shoot you. What could we do? Life is for a moment; death lasts until the end of time.” The land was sold out from under them.

原页 47

20世纪90年代，韩国开发公司（Kodeco）把一条伐木路修过卡拉万，村庄被迫获得更大的地区可见性。警察开始把地块卖给移民，尤其是被带来在树木种植园工作、却急于离开种植园、进入更有利可图的自然资源贸易的爪哇跨岛移民。卡拉万居民抗议。那是卡拉万的果园地，由所有者照料，并被规划最终重新用作农田。他们请求习惯法领袖介入。但没人敢对抗武装部队。“‘国有土地’，士兵们这么说。如果你不同意，他们就开枪。我们能做什么？生命只有一刻；死亡持续到时间尽头。”土地就这样从他们脚下被卖掉了。

原页 47

Kalawan became an attractive site for immigrants, and old Kalawan residents began selling land themselves before others could sell it for them. But who had the right to sell which land? The man who married in from another village sold the land of his wife’s family. The neighborhood head sold his neighborhood. Who could interfere? Meanwhile, two different plantation companies drew their property lines through the village, separating “Korea” and “Indonesia,” as residents put it. Some of my Kalawan friends worked for the survey teams, showing them the trails, and losing their lands for a few days of cigarette money.

原页 47

卡拉万成了对移民有吸引力的地方，老卡拉万居民开始赶在别人替他们卖地之前自己卖地。但谁有权卖哪块地？从另一个村庄入赘的男人卖掉了妻子家族的土地。邻里头人卖掉了所辖邻里的土地。谁能干涉？与此同时，两家不同的种植园公司把它们的财产线画过村庄，分隔了居民所说的“韩国”和“印尼”。我的一些卡拉万朋友为测量队工作，给他们指路，为了几天的香烟钱丢掉了自己的土地。

原页 47

A paroxysm of greed seized the village. Young men rushed to sell local resources, and, when they ran out, to join the army. Men in army uniforms, real or fake, ransacked the houses, stealing valuables. “If you don’t wreck and rampage, your rice pot will be empty,” someone said. “If there’s money in it, people will do it,” Uma Adang grumbled. “If they have one million, they want two million. If they have two million, they want three million. Up to tens of millions. They don’t stop to think. They just want it to multiply: gold, clothing, anything ‘modern,’ electric motors, motorcycles, motor vehicles. Kalimantan is sick.”

原页 47

一阵贪婪的抽搐攫住了村庄。年轻人争先恐后地出售本地资源，卖光之后就去参军。穿军装的男人——真的或假的——洗劫房屋，偷走贵重物品。“如果你不砸不抢，你的饭锅就会空，”有人说。“只要有钱可赚，人们就会干，”乌玛·阿当嘟囔道。“如果他们有一百万，他们想要两百万。如果他们有两百万，他们想要三百万。直到几千万。他们不停下来想。他们只想让它不断增加：金子、衣服、任何‘现代’的东西，电动机、摩托车、机动车。加里曼丹病了。”

原页 47

Sin

原页 47

罪

原页 47

Property regimes come into being with domestic realignments. In Kalawan, family values were asserted in a defensive spasm of fear. When most everything has been lost, it is easy to demand more and more control over less and less.

原页 47

财产体制随着家庭内部的重新排列而出现。在卡拉万，家庭价值在一阵防御性的恐惧抽搐中被主张。当几乎一切都已失去时，很容易要求对越来越少的东西拥有越来越多的控制。

原页 47, 48

Misah had sex with her boyfriend. I knew because everyone was talking about it. Their teacher had caught them. When they had not shown up in class, he had left the other students to their own devices. He spent the afternoon stalking the couple, following them silently to Misah’s house and peering through a window as they chatted. When they lay down, he pounced. He called an emergency village meeting in which he described in the most excruciating detail everything that he had seen. His report provoked a crisis. The couple must be married off immediately, and in acknowledgment of sin. They had disgraced their community.

In Kalawan, there are only two kinds of teachers: Muslims and Christians. Both hold themselves above the local community of pagans. Both sit in chairs and eat pastries with their coffee, while others sit on the floor. Both send the children home if they are a few minutes late to school, even if they have hiked through the jungle for an hour in a storm to get there. My friends used to make fun of them, gently and with respect for their willingness to teach the children. But in the light of krisis the villagers saw themselves in the gaze of others, and they seemed poor, backward, and without protection. Sinful and without civilization. There were no more jokes about the teachers then. “Misah is an animal,” her kin said, “she’s not even human.” Women’s sexuality has so often been posed to configure battles between kindreds and communities. But here the teacher’s accusation had turned the battle into a defensive siege. Either Dayaks were capable of moral standards or they were not. There would be no kin supporting Misah; she must be an icon of disrespect. My friends raged about her bad behavior. And I marveled: These were the same women with whom I had joked so often about sexual matters and otherwise. How had they become such small-town moralists?

原页 47, 48

米萨和男朋友发生了性关系。我知道，因为所有人都在谈论。他们的老师抓住了他们。当他们没来上课时，老师让其他学生自习。他花了一下午跟踪这对情侣，悄悄跟到米萨家，透过窗户看他们聊天。当他们躺下时，他扑了上去。他召开紧急村民会议，以最令人难堪的细节描述他所看到的一切。他的报告引发了一场危机。这对情侣必须立即结婚，以承认罪过。他们让共同体蒙羞了。

在卡拉万，只有两类教师：穆斯林与基督徒。两者都把自己置于当地异教徒共同体之上。两者都坐在椅子上，就着咖啡吃糕点，而其他人坐在地上。两者都在孩子们迟到几分钟时把他们赶回家，即便他们冒着暴风雨在丛林里走了一个小时才到。我的朋友们过去常取笑他们，温和地，并尊重他们教孩子的意愿。但在 krisis 的光照下，村民们在别人的凝视中看到自己，他们显得贫穷、落后、没有保护。有罪而没有文明。那时起，关于教师的笑话没有了。“米萨是动物，”她的亲属说，“她甚至不是人。”女性的性行为如此经常地被用来组织亲族与共同体之间的争斗。但在这里，教师的指控把战斗变成了一场防御性围困。要么达雅克人有能力遵守道德标准，要么没有。不会有亲属支持米萨；她必须成为一个不敬的象征。我的朋友们对她的坏行为暴怒。而我感到惊异：这些正是我以前经常与之拿性事和其他事情开玩笑的同一群女人。她们怎么变成了这样的小镇道德家？

原页 48

A few years before, Uma Adang had mimed how the pious at prayer peeked out from under closed eyes to see what others were doing. She demonstrated how a tone-deaf chorus sang “Hallelujah” while bemused villagers lined up for post-service refreshments. We had laughed. Now, civilizational disciplines didn’t seem so funny. Under the circumstances, everyone must learn piety. “At least she could have finished class 5,” my friends said. I wasn’t sure that the memorized inaccuracies of the school texts would have done her much good, but the sizzling atmosphere suppressed such irreverence. “Why can’t she continue school anyway?” I ask with false naivete. “Of course the teacher throws these students out,” they reprimand me with finality. “It is sin.” We would have no more parody of the teacher's discipline. If he says it is sin, it is sin. “Dayaks must have a higher standard than others,” says Uma Adang. “It’s different for [Muslims and Christians] who live in the city; they are sophisticated. Dayaks are the older sibling [of Muslims and Christians]; our law is higher. ” In the confrontation of ethics, local custom is left a role as a defensive standard of value.

原页 48

几年前，乌玛·阿当曾模仿虔诚者在祈祷时从闭着的眼睛下面偷看别人在做什么。她演示了一个五音不全的合唱团如何唱“哈利路亚”，而困惑的村民排着队等礼拜后的茶点。我们当时笑了。现在，文明的规训似乎不那么好笑了。在这种情况下，每个人都必须学会虔诚。“至少她本可以读完五年级，”我的朋友们说。我不确定学校课本里背下来的错误会对她有多大好处，但滚烫的气氛压制了这种不敬。“她为什么不能继续上学？”我故作天真地问。“老师当然会把这种学生赶出去，”他们以终结性的语气训斥我。“这是罪。”我们不会再戏仿教师的纪律了。如果他说这是罪，那就是罪。“达雅克人必须比别人有更高的标准，”乌玛·阿当说。“对住在城里的[穆斯林和基督徒]来说不一样；他们世故。达雅克人是[穆斯林和基督徒的]兄姐；我们的法律更高。”在伦理的对抗中，地方习俗被留作一种防御性的价值标准。

原页 48, 49

"There are three suku (groups],” explains Rusli, “Dayaks, Muslims, and Christians. The Javanese are Muslims. ‘Indonesia’ is the same—Muslim.” Now Dayaks have become a minority in Kalawan. Propriety is what they have. People should keep their houses clean and obey their parents. ‘Teenagers who go to school should mind their virtue. “T don’t think you'll come back,” said Uma Adang. “There is no more culture here.” Kebudayaan, the official state term for “culture,” had become a code word between us some years ago for our shared work in savoring the revitalization of customary law and the resurgence of community. But by 2000, customary law was a remnant. The spreading frontier had buried such nonproliferation regimes.

原页 48, 49

“有三个 suku（群体），”鲁斯利解释道，“达雅克人、穆斯林和基督徒。爪哇人是穆斯林。‘印尼’也一样——穆斯林。”现在达雅克人在卡拉万成了少数。体面是他们所拥有的。人们应当保持房屋干净，服从父母。上学的青少年应当注意自己的贞洁。“我觉得你不会回来了，”乌玛·阿当说。“这里不再有文化了。”Kebudayaan——国家官方的“文化”一词——几年前已在我们之间成为暗语，指我们共同品味的习惯法复兴与共同体复兴的工作。但到2000年，习惯法只剩残余。蔓延的边疆埋葬了这类非增殖体制。

原页 49

When there is nothing left, there is still the shadow of civilization, inspiring pious disciplines. And, while trouble is unlikely to come out of Kalawan, even the piety of the powerless can get fiercely out of control.

原页 49

当什么都不剩时，仍有文明的阴影，激发虔诚的规训。而且，尽管麻烦不太可能出自卡拉万，即便无权者的虔诚也可能猛烈失控。

原页 49

Body Odor

原页 49

体味

原页 49

By 2000, indeed, whiffs of pious violence could be detected across Indonesia, pitting ethnic and religious groups in new, morally inspired hatreds. Even in Kalawan, people knew that Dayaks in West Kalimantan had mobilized to protect the reputation of their women from the disrespectful gestures and violent intrusions of migrant Madurese. Dayaks were driving Madurese out, killing them if necessary.18 People in Kalawan have identified as Dayaks for a long time. But this was an exotic version of ethnicity: charismatic, passionate, and frightening.

原页 49

到2000年，确实，虔诚暴力的气息可以在整个印尼被察觉到，把族群与宗教群体投入新的、受道德启发的仇恨。即便在卡拉万，人们也知道西加里曼丹的达雅克人已经动员起来，保护他们女人的名誉，免受移民马都拉人不敬的手势与暴力侵入。达雅克人正在把马都拉人赶走，必要时杀掉他们。18卡拉万的人们长期以来认同为达雅克人。但这是族群性的一种陌生版本：有感召力、充满激情、令人恐惧。

原页 49

My closest Kalawan friends heard about the Dayak-Madurese clashes from relatives who had moved to West Kalimantan and who had come back, briefly, to visit. I heard their stories some weeks after the visitors left, but the tales were still fresh as they detailed the tellers’ sense of a breath-stopping fear—and the need for a brave response.

原页 49

我最亲近的卡拉万朋友从搬到西加里曼丹、又短暂回来探亲的亲戚那里听说了达雅克—马都拉冲突。我在访客离开几周后听到他们的故事，但故事仍然鲜活，因为他们详述了讲述者那种令人屏息的恐惧——以及对勇敢回应的需要。

原页 49

By the time I heard the stories, there was one detail that stood out, to be repeated over and over: The Dayaks of West Kalimantan, my friends said, could identify Madurese by smelling them. Madurese and Dayaks mixed in public spaces, such as transport buses. It was difficult for strangers to tell one from the other. But when buses were stopped by militants during these wars, Madurese and Dayaks were separated, despite attempts on each side to disguise their names, their clothes, and their language abilities, because they could not change their body odor. My friends showed me what it might have been like, touching me and one another with a finger and sniffing—and then laughing in amazement at the very idea. The children caught on to the game, wiping a finger on first one and then another, and smelling. They ran around giggling, giddy with the new idea, practicing. The adults were equally intrigued. Imagine, sniffing out your enemies in a literal sense!

原页 49

到我听到这些故事时，有一个细节格外突出，被一遍又一遍地重复：我的朋友们说，西加里曼丹的达雅克人能靠闻气味辨认马都拉人。马都拉人与达雅克人在公共交通巴士等公共空间混杂。陌生人很难分辨彼此。但当巴士在这些战争中被武装分子拦下时，马都拉人与达雅克人被分开，尽管双方都试图伪装自己的姓名、衣着和语言能力，因为他们无法改变自己的体味。我的朋友们向我演示那可能是什么样子，用手指触碰我和彼此，闻一闻——然后对这个想法本身惊奇地大笑。孩子们也学会了这个游戏，先用一根手指擦一个人，再擦另一个人，然后闻。他们跑来跑去咯咯笑，被这个新想法弄得晕头转向，反复练习。大人们也同样着迷。想象一下，从字面意义上嗅出你的敌人！

原页 50

Body odor as ethnicity was too powerful an idea to fade. In the mass of strangers conjured up by frontier culture and intensified by krisis, how else might one identify one’s friends and enemies? Everything else could be mimicked, or so it was said. A poor man’s DNA testing, and no authority could standardize the results. This was a technology of identity that could reach out across separate strands of fear and discontent to conjure some common ground of discomfort: It’s them.

原页 50

体味作为族群性，是一个强大得不会消退的观念。在边疆文化召唤出来、又被 krisis 强化的陌生人群体中，人还能怎样辨认朋友和敌人？别的一切都可以模仿，至少据说如此。一种穷人的DNA检测，没有任何权威能标准化结果。这是一种身份技术，能够跨越恐惧与不满的分离线索，召唤出某种共同的不适基础：就是他们。

原页 50

Body odor ethnicity reappeared in the 2001 Dayak-Madurese violence in Central Kalimantan.19 It accompanied ethnicity-making ritual and fashion: The “red bowl” of blood and feathers passed from village to village to mobilize a Dayak force; the red head scarves and rattan bracelets of Dayak combatants. All were codes to make mass ethnic conflict legible. Yet, of these, smell is the most intriguing. Smell is elusive. It is difficult to describe. It arouses inchoate emotions and carries deep and often confused memories. Smell brings emotional force to difference: Some body odors make us relax; others offend us. Yet smell is not easy to categorize. The one smell that opens the door of recognition has no cognates; it is unique. No two people offer that same smell, however closely they are related. Smell is not a good guide to social status. Smell undermines the mirage of category accuracy even as it provides it a close-to-the-body story.

原页 50

体味族群性在2001年中加里曼丹的达雅克—马都拉暴力中重现。19它伴随着制造族群性的仪式与时尚：盛着血和羽毛的“红碗”从一个村庄传到另一个村庄，以动员达雅克力量；达雅克战士的红色头巾和藤手镯。所有这些都是使大规模族群冲突变得可读的代码。然而，其中气味最耐人寻味。气味难以捉摸。它难以描述。它激起未成形的情绪，承载深刻而常常混乱的记忆。气味给差异带来情感力量：有些体味让我们放松；另一些冒犯我们。但气味不容易分类。打开识别之门的那一种气味没有对应物；它是独特的。没有两个人提供同样的气味，无论他们关系多么近。气味不是社会地位的好向导。气味削弱范畴准确性的幻象，同时给它提供一个贴近身体的故事。

原页 50

Smell, like smoke, draws our senses inside obscurity. Something is going on but we don’t know what it is. We immerse ourselves in it, engulfed in its unknowns. We steer loose from familiar distinctions and commitments, joining the flow of the frontier.

原页 50

气味，像烟一样，把我们的感官拉进隐晦之中。有什么正在发生，但我们不知道那是什么。我们沉浸其中，被它的未知吞没。我们偏离熟悉的区分与承诺，加入边疆的流动。

原页 50

From afar it is easy to see the destruction, the violence, the consolidation of property rules and ethnic boundaries, and the rise of new political disciplines. Observers wonder how people could have been induced to join this madness. I have argued here for the importance of an assault on the senses: the frontiers of capitalism, spun out of control.

原页 50

从远处很容易看到毁灭、暴力、财产规则与族群边界的巩固，以及新政治规训的兴起。观察者想知道，人们怎么会被诱导加入这种疯狂。我在这里论证了对感官的攻击的重要性：资本主义的边疆，失控地旋转。

原页 50

Still Alive, But Captured by the Enemy

原页 50

还活着，但被敌人俘虏

原页 50

Looking up from the confusion, one can only grunt, struggling to remember the precision of mathematical symbols, the numbers of the dead.

One: Natural resources are not God given but must be wrested from previous economies and ecologies in violent extractions.

从混乱中抬起头，人只能咕哝，挣扎着回忆数学符号的精确、死者的数字。

一：自然资源不是上帝赐予的，而必须在暴力采掘中从先前的经济与生态中夺取。

原页 50

‘Two: Such violence leaves none of us unscathed.

原页 50

二：这种暴力让我们无人毫发无伤。

原页 50

Three: This assault is no neighborhood storm, It gathers force from afar, entangling multiple local-to-global scales. For more on this, dear reader, please read on.

三：这场攻击并非局限于邻里的风暴。它从远方积聚力量，缠绕着多个从地方到全球的尺度。亲爱的读者，欲知更多，请继续读下去。

原页 51

“They communicate only in sign language”

原页 51

“他们只用肢体语言交流”

原页 51

[Friction in the commodity chain]

原页 51

[商品链中的摩擦]

原页 51

Everyone knows a commodity: It is the material good of capitalist production and the object of consumers’ desire. Commodities seem so familiar that we imagine them ready made for us throughout every stage of production and distribution, as they pass from hand to hand until they arrive at the consumer. Yet the closer we look at the commodity chain, the more every step—even transportation—can be seen as an arena of cultural production. Global capitalism is made in the friction in these chains as divergent cultural economies are linked, often awkwardly. Yet the commodity must emerge as if untouched by this friction.

原页 51

人人都知道商品：它是资本主义生产的物质产品，也是消费者欲望的对象。商品似乎如此熟悉，以至于我们想象它在生产和分配的每个阶段都是为我们准备好的，从一只手传到另一只手，直到抵达消费者。然而，我们越仔细看商品链，就越能发现每一步——甚至运输——都可以被视为文化生产的舞台。全球资本主义是在这些链条的摩擦中被制造的，因为彼此分歧的文化经济被连接起来，而且往往连接得很笨拙。然而，商品必须表现得仿佛未受这种摩擦触动。

原页 51

A lump of coal travels from a mine in Kalimantan to a power plant in India. Before it achieves an existence as a lump of coal, it is part of the landscape under a village field. Somehow it must be coaxed or coerced out of this landscape. Once mined, it still must travel to a warehouse and from there to a port city, where the coal ships can dock. It must be sorted and graded, and managers will have to make sure no one mixes the poor-quality coal with the good. It must meet specifications. If it sits too long in the warehouse, or in the ship at harbor, it will lose all its value to storage and docking costs. At the other end of its journey, it must convince the power plant managers that the contract has been met. All along the journey this lump is “coal.” Yet at each stage it is appraised for different properties; if it will stay in this commodity chain, it must be ready to meet these varied demands. It requires not a vague and transcendent “coalness” but rather a step-by-step negotiation of the possibilities at hand—for digging, sorting, transport, and so on. It is transformed as coal-the-diggable, coal-the-sortable, coal-the-transportable, until it eventually becomes coal-the-burnable. In these shifts the lump of coal rubs up against other participants in the chain: unhappy villagers, conveyor belts, contracts. In its shape, its cost, and its composition, coal is made in the friction of the commodity chain.

原页 51

一块煤从加里曼丹的矿井运到印度的发电厂。在它获得一块煤的存在之前，它是村庄田地之下的地景的一部分。它必须以某种方式被哄骗或强迫离开这个地景。一旦开采出来，它仍必须运到仓库，再从那里运到港口城市，煤船可以在那里停靠。它必须被分类和分级，经理必须确保没有人把劣质煤混进好煤。它必须符合规格。如果它在仓库或港口船里停留太久，仓储和停泊成本会使其失去全部价值。在旅程的另一端，它必须说服发电厂经理，合同已得到履行。在整个旅程中，这块煤都是“煤”。然而在每个阶段，它都因不同的属性而被评估；如果它要留在这条商品链中，它必须准备好满足这些多样的要求。它需要的不是模糊而超越的“煤性”，而是对手头可能性的逐步协商——用于挖掘、分类、运输等等。它被转化为可挖掘的煤、可分类的煤、可运输的煤，直到最终成为可燃的煤。在这些转变中，煤块与链条上的其他参与者摩擦：不满的村民、传送带、合同。在形状、成本和构成上，煤是在商品链的摩擦中被制造的。

原页 51, 52

The managers who facilitate this process can tell us: To produce a commodity is the work of the translator, the diplomat, and the power-crazed magician.

原页 51, 52

促成这一过程的经理们可以告诉我们：生产商品是译者、外交官和权力狂巫师的工作。

···
原页 52

2000. In Banjarmasin, I happened to meet Mr. Krishnan, a business manager from Singapore, who represents United Power, which trades in coal. Mr Krishnan, according to his business card, received his MBA in the U.K; he is the assistant manager for exports at United Power. He speaks English, Tamil (his mother tongue), and a “smattering of Malay,” on which he gets by in Indonesia. We spoke in English; later, I wrote down what he said.

原页 52

2000年。在班贾尔马辛，我碰巧遇到来自新加坡的企业经理克里希南先生，他代表从事煤炭贸易的联合电力公司（United Power）。根据他的名片，克里希南先生在英国获得MBA；他是联合电力公司的出口助理经理。他会说英语、泰米尔语（他的母语）以及“一点马来语”，靠它在印尼应付。我们用英语交谈；后来，我记下了他说的话。

原页 52

Mr. Krishnan was in Banjarmasin to supervise the loading of a coal ship. Each day the ship sits in the harbor, United Power pays U.S.$10,000 in harbor fees. He was able to reduce the time to five days; otherwise it would have been at least two weeks. In Australia, he said, loading would have taken one and a half days.

原页 52

克里希南先生来班贾尔马辛监督一艘煤船装货。船在港口停的每一天，联合电力公司要支付一万美元港口费。他成功把时间缩短到五天；否则至少需要两周。他说，在澳大利亚，装货只需一天半。

原页 52

United Power buys coal directly from the mine, which means they are responsible for trucking it to the stockpile, located three hours from Banjarmasin. From there, they transport it to the jetty, and then on to the ship. Each of these transport stages is contracted to different groups. The ship itself is on contract. Mr. Krishnan’s job is to make sure transport at each of these stages moves smoothly and efficiently. This is not a simple task: Each stage presents its own cultural, political, and technical complications.

原页 52

联合电力公司直接从矿井买煤，这意味着他们负责用卡车把煤运到距班贾尔马辛三小时路程的堆场。从那里，他们把它运到码头，再运上船。每个运输阶段都承包给不同的群体。船本身也是租用的。克里希南先生的工作是确保每个运输阶段都顺利高效地运转。这不是简单的任务：每个阶段都有自己的文化、政治与技术复杂性。

原页 52

From the mine, the coal is loaded on to trucks and brought to the stockpile. A regulation requires the trucks to take an outer ring road rather than the regular roads. But the ring road is sandy and it damages the trucks, so the drivers take the main roads anyway. Meanwhile, coal trucks have caused the deaths of several children, and people are angry.

原页 52

从矿井，煤被装上卡车，运到堆场。一项法规要求卡车走外环路而不是普通道路。但外环路是沙地，会损坏卡车，所以司机们还是走主干道。与此同时，运煤卡车已导致几名儿童死亡，人们很愤怒。

原页 52

From the stockpile, the coal is trucked to the jetty, loaded on a conveyer belt, and dumped on to barges. The barges, pushed by tugboats, take six hours to get out to the ship. There the coal is loaded into the ship’s hatches. If you put coal into standard shipping containers, it burns up, so you must use bulk loading. This job was further complicated by the fact that the buyer, in India, wanted two grades of coal, and these needed to be loaded into separate hatches.

原页 52

从堆场，煤被卡车运到码头，装上传送带，倾倒入驳船。驳船由拖船推动，需要六小时才能到达大船。在那里，煤被装进船舱。如果把煤装进标准集装箱，它会烧起来，所以必须散装。这项工作更加复杂，因为印度买家想要两个等级的煤，而它们需要装进不同的船舱。

原页 52, 53

Coal of different grades has separate uses. South Kalimantan produces a good deal of “environmentally friendly” coal, which is clean but of a low grade, less than 5.9. It causes power outages if you use it for power stations because it can’t burn long enough. Indonesia, like India, has a lot of lowgrade coal, and one must mix it with a higher grade coal, for example the 7.0 coal from China, to keep power stations running. Indian politicians always want to use Indian coal in the power stations, and as a result they always experience power outages. Low-grade coal is only good for uses such as cement plants.

原页 52, 53

不同等级的煤用途不同。南加里曼丹出产大量“环境友好”煤，它清洁但等级低，低于5.9。如果用于发电站，它会导致停电，因为燃烧时间不够长。印尼和印度一样，有很多低等级煤，必须把它与更高等级的煤混合，例如来自中国的7.0煤，才能让发电站运转。印度政客总是想在发电站使用印度煤，结果总是遭遇停电。低等级煤只适合水泥厂之类的用途。

原页 53

Different parts of a mine may produce different grades of coal. The suppliers try to mix the lower grade into shipments that are supposed to be higher grade. The differences are not actually visible, so Mr. Krishnan performs random checks at the conveyor belt. He tests the coal on the belt at least every two hours. If the grade is 6.4 or above for a 6.5 order, he lets it go; if it is below 5.9, he stops the belt.

原页 53

一个矿井的不同部分可能产出不同等级的煤。供应商试图把较低等级的煤混进本应更高等级的货里。差异实际上看不出来，所以克里希南先生在传送带旁进行随机抽查。他至少每两小时检测一次带上的煤。如果订单是6.5，而等级在6.4或以上，他就放行；如果低于5.9，他就停下传送带。

原页 53

Each coal company has a separate character. Mr. Krishnan thinks A__ is the most professional company. (I recall that the newspapers have been full of A__’s refusals to restore mining areas. Professionalism is not the same as environmental or community responsibility.) He says Indians are worse than Indonesians in requiring bribes and kickbacks. At least in Indonesia you can sit down with the company people and talk. Mr. Krishnan comes to Banjarmasin two days before the ship arrives to discuss arrangements, including the schedule. He talks particularly to the mining engineers, who can speak a little English. If he didn’t come, they would work much more slowly. For example, they would all take lunch breaks together instead of taking turns. If something breaks and no one is there, no one fixes it. Everyone waits for authorization before doing anything. Mr. Krishnan is there to make them change their attitudes.

原页 53

每家煤炭公司都有自己的性格。克里希南先生认为 A__ 是最专业的公司。（我记得报纸上满是 A__ 拒绝恢复矿区的事。专业精神并不等同于对环境或社区的责任。）他说，印度人在索要贿赂和回扣方面比印尼人更糟。至少在印尼，你可以和公司的人坐下来谈。克里希南先生在船到达前两天来班贾尔马辛讨论安排，包括时间表。他特别与能说一点英语的采矿工程师交谈。如果他不来，他们会慢得多。例如，他们会一起午休，而不是轮流。如果有什么坏了而没人在场，就没人修。每个人做任何事都要等授权。克里希南先生在那里就是让他们改变态度。

原页 53

That week, for example, he went out to the ship, where the stevedores were loading very, very slowly. He saw a barge of watermelons going by; he had it called over. He bought the load for U.S.$100 and distributed the melons to the workers. They sped up the work, and he saved two days.

原页 53

比如那一周，他去船上，装卸工装货装得非常非常慢。他看到一艘载着西瓜的驳船经过；他把它叫了过来。他用一百美元买下整船货，把西瓜分给工人。他们加快了工作，他省下了两天。

原页 53

The ships are contracted for the course of the voyage. This ship has an Indian captain and two officers, and the rest of the crew is Indonesian. They have been sailing together now for one year. The captain and his officers do not speak Indonesian, so the crew and the officers have no language in common. They communicate only in sign language. When the captain wants coffee, he puts his hand to his mouth to signal drinking. When he wants a meal cooked, he goes to the kitchen and points to each of the ingredients he wants and mimes how to cook them. They will travel that way to India.

原页 53

船按航次租用。这艘船有一位印度船长和两名高级船员，其余船员是印尼人。他们现在已经一起航行了一年。船长和他的高级船员不会说印尼语，所以船员和高级船员没有共同语言。他们只用肢体语言交流。船长想要咖啡时，把手放到嘴边表示喝。他想让人做饭时，就去厨房，指着想要的每一种配料，模仿如何烹制。他们将以这种方式航行到印度。

原页 53

United Power used to buy Australian coal. Now the rupiah is so low that Indonesian coal is irresistible. But if they don’t send a manager to make the process move smoothly, they will lose more money in delays than the coal is worth.

原页 53

联合电力公司过去买澳大利亚煤。现在印尼盾如此疲软，印尼煤令人无法抗拒。但如果他们不派经理来让流程顺利运转，他们因延误损失的钱会比煤的价值还多。

···
原页 54

What a lot of work to make sure the coal is delivered! After talking to Mr. Krishnan, I imagine myself an ethnographer on that coal ship, watching the crew go about the daily business of the ship without being able to take orders or explain difficulties to the ship’s officers. But each stage of the process is similarly plagued with recalcitrant cultural difference. Mr. Krishnan must negotiate every step of the labor process because there is little agreement about how each task must be done.

原页 54

为了确保煤被送到，要做多少工作啊！和克里希南先生谈过之后，我想象自己成为那艘煤船上的民族志学者，看着船员处理船上的日常事务，而他们却无法听懂高级船员的命令，也无法向其说明困难。但流程的每个阶段都同样受制于顽固的文化差异。克里希南先生必须协商劳动过程的每一步，因为关于每项任务该如何完成，几乎没有共识。

原页 54

In this case, indeed, there is outright conflict. I’ve heard about the coal truck drivers, described by Banjar friends as fiends who don’t care for the lives of children; meanwhile, the drivers accelerate to avoid angry residents. At the mines, things are no better. Since the army stepped back as guarantor of the coal companies, community groups, gangs, and entrepreneurs have been taking over mines by force. After all, the coal companies appropriated the land themselves only through the force of the army. Not that this does the miners much good, since then coal production proceeds without even the meager benefits the company provided. As for the engineers negotiating with Mr. Krishnan about delivery schedules, they are nice to him, I think, because they are hoping he will be a resource to leverage a better position somewhere else, out of what they imagine as a backwater assignment. Each of these little worlds forms part of the production of South Kalimantan coal. Mr. Krishnan’s job is to make this jostling work together—at least well enough to deliver something recognizable as a market load to India, and in enough quantity to make his company a profit.

原页 54

在这个案例中，确实存在公开冲突。我听说过运煤卡车司机，班贾尔朋友把他们描述为不在乎儿童生命的恶魔；与此同时，司机们加速行驶以躲避愤怒的居民。在矿井，情况也好不到哪里去。自从军队不再充当煤炭公司的担保者，社区团体、帮派和企业家一直在用武力接管矿场。毕竟，煤炭公司自己也只是通过军队的武力才占有了土地。这对矿工来说并没有什么好处，因为此后煤炭生产进行时，连公司提供的微薄福利也没有了。至于与克里希南先生协商交货时间表的工程师们，我认为他们对他很友好，因为他们希望他能成为一种资源，帮助他们在别处谋得更好的职位，离开这份在他们看来位于穷乡僻壤的工作。这些小世界中的每一个都构成南加里曼丹煤炭生产的一部分。克里希南先生的工作就是让这些相互碰撞的环节协同运作——至少足以把某种可辨认的市场货物送到印度，并且数量足够让公司盈利。

原页 55

scale. Relative or proportionate size or extent.1

原页 55

尺度（scale）：相对的或成比例的大小或范围。1

原页 55

Indonesia’s profile in the international imagination changed completely at the end of the 1990s. From the top of what was called a “miracle,” Indonesia fell to the bottom of a “crisis.” In the middle of what was portrayed as a timeless political regime, students demonstrated, and, suddenly, the regime was gone. So recently an exemplar of the promise of globalization, overnight Indonesia became the case study of globalization’s failures.

原页 55

20世纪90年代末，印尼在国际想象中的地位彻底改变。印尼从一个所谓“奇迹”的顶端跌入“危机”的底部。在一个被描绘为永恒政治体制的中间，学生们示威，突然间，政权消失了。如此近期还是全球化承诺的典范，印尼一夜之间成了全球化失败的案例研究。

原页 55

The speed of these changes takes one’s breath away—and raises important questions about globalization. Under what circumstances are boom and bust intimately related to each other? Might deregulation and cronyism sometimes name the same thing—but from different moments of investor confidence? Such questions run against the grain of economic expertise about globalization, with its discrimination between good and bad kinds of economic policy. Yet the whiggish acrobatics necessary to show how those very economies celebrated as miracles were simultaneously lurking crises hardly seem to tell the whole story. A less pious attitude toward the market may be necessary to consider the specificities of those political economies, like that of New Order Indonesia, brought into being together with international finance.2

原页 55

这些变化的速度令人屏息——也提出了关于全球化的重要问题。在什么情况下，繁荣与萧条会密切相连？去管制与裙带关系有时是否指同一件事——只是出自投资者信心的不同时刻？这样的问题与经济专家关于全球化的论述相悖，后者要区分好的和坏的经济政策。然而，要说明那些被奉为奇迹的经济体如何同时潜伏着危机，所需的那种辉格史式杂技，似乎很难讲述完整的故事。也许需要对市场采取一种不那么虔诚的态度，才能理解那些政治经济体的特殊性，例如新秩序印尼，它们是与国际金融一起被创造出来的。2

原页 55, 56

This chapter brings us back to the months just before Indonesia so drastically changed, to canoe at the running edge of what turned out to be a waterfall. It concerns a set of incidents that can be imagined as a rehearsal for the Asian financial crisis as well as a minor participant in the international disillusion that led to the Suharto regime’s downfall. In 1994, a small Canadian gold prospecting company announced a major find in the forests of Kalimantan. Over the months, the find got bigger and bigger, until it was the biggest gold strike in the world, conjuring memories of the Alaskan Klondike and South Africa’s Witwatersrand. Thousands of North American investors put their savings in the company called Bre-X. First-time investors and retired people joined financial wizards. Whole towns in western Canada invested (Eisler 1997). The new world of Internet investment blossomed with Bre-X. Meanwhile, Bre-X received continuous coverage in North American newspapers, especially after huge Canadian mining companies and Indonesian officials entered the fray, fighting over the rights to mine Busang, Bre-X’s find.3 The scandal of Indonesian business-as-usual, opened to public scrutiny as corruption, heightened international attention and garnered support for Bre-X. But, in 1997, just when expectation had reached a fevered pitch, Busang was exposed as barren: There was nothing there. Gasps, cries, and lawsuits rose from every corner. The Toronto Stock Exchange changed its rules to avoid more Bre-Xs.4 Bre-X lawsuits set new international standards.5 Several years later, Bre-X investors still hoped and complained across the Internet, as they peddled the remains of their experiences: jokes, songs, and stock certificates (as wallpaper, historical document, or irreplaceable art, ready to hang).6 Meanwhile, Indonesian mining officials and copycat prospecting companies scrambled to free themselves from the Bre-X story, even as they reenacted its scenes, hoping to revive its investor enthusiasm.7

校注9
原页 55, 56

本章把我们带回印尼发生剧变前的几个月，乘独木舟在急流边缘划行——后来才知道前方是瀑布。它涉及一系列事件，这些事件可以被想象为亚洲金融危机的彩排，也是导致苏哈托政权倒台的国际幻灭的一个小参与者。1994年，一家小型加拿大金矿勘探公司宣布在加里曼丹森林有重大发现。几个月间，这个发现越来越大，直到成为世界上最大的金矿发现，唤起人们对阿拉斯加克朗代克和南非威特沃特斯兰德的记忆。成千上万北美投资者把积蓄投入一家叫布雷-X（Bre-X）的公司。初次投资者和退休者与金融巫师一起加入。加拿大西部整座整座的城镇都投资了（Eisler 1997）。互联网投资的新世界随布雷-X一同绽放。与此同时，布雷-X在北美报纸上得到持续报道，尤其是在大型加拿大矿业公司和印尼官员加入争夺、争夺布雷-X发现地布桑（Busang）采矿权之后。3印尼照常营业的丑闻作为腐败向公众审视开放，提高了国际关注，并为布雷-X赢得了支持。但在1997年，就在期待达到狂热顶点时，布桑被揭穿为贫矿：那里什么都没有。各地传来倒抽冷气声、哭喊与诉讼。多伦多证券交易所修改规则，以避免更多布雷-X事件。4布雷-X诉讼设立了新的国际标准。5几年后，布雷-X投资者仍在互联网上希望和抱怨，兜售他们经历的残余：笑话、歌曲和股票凭证（作为墙纸、历史文件或不可替代的艺术品，随时可以挂起来）。6与此同时，印尼矿业官员和跟风勘探公司争先恐后地摆脱布雷-X故事，即便他们重演其场景，希望重燃投资者的热情。7

校注9
原页 56

The Bre-X story exemplifies popular thinking about the pleasures and dangers of international finance and associated dreams of globalization. The story dramatizes north-south inequalities in the new capitalisms; it celebrates the north’s excitement about international investment, and the blight of the south’s so-called crony capitalisms: business imagined not quite/not white. Depicting southern leaders as rats fighting for garbage, the story also promises new genres of justice for the northern investor who dares to sue. Finance looks like democracy: The Internet, they say, opens foreign investment to the North American everyman. But the Bre-X story also narrates the perils of the downsized, overcompetitive economy: the sad entrepreneurship of selling worthless stock certificates. As one writer put it, mixing metaphors, “The Bre-X saga will come to be known as the demarcation of the Internet as the weapon of choice for investors” (Zgodzinski 1997).

原页 56

布雷-X的故事例示了大众对国际金融的快乐与危险以及相关全球化梦想的思考。这个故事戏剧化了新资本主义中的南北不平等；它颂扬北方对国际投资的兴奋，以及南方所谓裙带资本主义的祸害：被想象为“不够正统／不够白人”的商业（not quite/not white）。这个故事把南方领导人描绘成争夺垃圾的老鼠，同时也承诺为敢于起诉的北方投资者提供新的正义类型。金融看起来像民主：他们说，互联网向北美普通人开放外国投资。但布雷-X故事也叙述了规模缩减、过度竞争经济的危险：出售毫无价值股票凭证的悲哀企业家精神。正如一位作家混合隐喻所写，“布雷-X传奇将作为互联网成为投资者首选武器的分界线而为人所知”（Zgodzinski 1997）。

原页 56, 57

Most salient to my concerns about the working of global capitalism is the genre convention with which Bre-X started its own story, and by which it was finished off. Bre-X was always a performance, a drama, a conjuring trick, an illusion, whether real gold or only the dream of gold ever existed at Busang. Journalists compared Busang, with its lines of false drilling samples, to a Hollywood set.8 But it was not just Busang; it was the whole investment process. No one would ever have invested in Bre-X if it had not created a performance, a dramatic exposition of the possibilities of gold.

原页 56, 57

对我关于全球资本主义运作的关切而言，最突出的是布雷-X开启自身故事、又被其终结的体裁惯例。布雷-X始终是一场表演、一出戏剧、一个戏法、一种幻象，无论布桑是否存在真金，还是只有黄金之梦。记者们把布桑及其一排排虚假钻探样本比作好莱坞布景。8但不只是布桑；整个投资过程都是如此。如果布雷-X没有创造一场表演、一次对黄金可能性的戏剧性展示，就不会有人投资它。

原页 57

Performance here is simultaneously economic performance and dramatic performance. The “economy of appearances” I describe depends on the relevance of this pun; the self-conscious making of a spectacle is a necessary aid to gathering investment funds. The dependence on spectacle has not been peculiar to Bre-X and other mining scams: It is a regular feature of the search for financial capital. Start-up companies must dramatize their dreams in order to attract the capital they need to operate and expand. Junior prospecting companies must exaggerate the possibilities of their mineral finds in order to attract investors so that they might, at some point, find something. This is a requirement of investment-oriented entrepreneurship, and it takes the limelight in those historical moments when capital seeks creativity rather than stable reproduction. In speculative enterprises, profit must be imagined before it can be extracted; the possibility of economic performance must be conjured like a spirit to draw an audience of potential investors. The more spectacular the conjuring, the more possible an investment frenzy. Drama itself can be worth summoning forth.9 Nor are companies alone in the conjuring business in these times. In order to attract companies, countries, regions, and towns must dramatize their potential as places for investment. Dramatic performance is the prerequisite of their economic performance.

原页 57

这里的 performance 同时指经济表现与戏剧表演。我所描述的“表象经济”正是建立在这层双关之上；自觉制造奇观是聚集投资资金的必要辅助。对奇观的依赖并非布雷-X和其他采矿骗局所独有：它是寻求金融资本的常规特征。初创公司必须戏剧化它们的梦想，以吸引运营和扩张所需的资本。初级勘探公司必须夸大其矿藏发现的可能性，以吸引投资者，使它们有可能在某个时候真的找到东西。这是以投资为导向的企业家精神的要求，在资本寻求创造力而非稳定再生产的那些历史时刻占据舞台中心。在投机性企业中，利润必须在被提取之前被想象；取得经济表现的可能性必须像精灵一样被召唤出来，以吸引潜在投资者的观众。召唤越壮观，投资狂潮就越可能。戏剧本身就可能值得召唤出来。9在这些时代，公司也不是唯一从事召唤的。为了吸引公司，国家、地区和城镇必须戏剧化它们作为投资地的潜力。戏剧表演是它们取得经济表现的前提。

原页 57

Yet conjuring is always culturally specific, creating a magic show of peculiar meanings, symbols, and practices. The conjuring aspect of finance interrupts our expectations that finance can and has spread everywhere, for it can only spread as far as its own magic. In its dramatic performances, circulating finance reveals itself as both empowered and limited by its cultural specificity.

原页 57

然而，召唤总是文化特定的，创造出具有特殊意义、符号与实践的魔术表演。金融的召唤面向打断了我们的期待——期待金融能够、且已经传播到各处，因为它只能传播到其自身魔法的范围。在其戏剧表演中，流动的金融显示出自己既被其文化特殊性赋能，也被其文化特殊性限制。

原页 57, 58

Contemporary masters of finance claim not only universal appeal but also a global scale of deployment. What are we to make of these globalist claims, with their millennial whispers of a more total and hegemonic world-making than we have ever known? Neither false ideology nor obvious truth, it seems to me that the globalist claims of finance are also a kind of conjuring, a dramatic performance. In these times of heightened attention to the space and scale of human undertakings, economic projects cannot limit themselves to conjuring at different scales—they must conjure the scales themselves. In this sense, a project that makes us imagine globality in order to see how it might succeed is one kind of “scale-making project”; similarly, projects that make us imagine locality, or the space of regions or nations, in order to see their success are also scale-making projects. The scales they conjure come into being in part through the contingent articulations into which they are pushed or stumble. In a world of multiple, divergent claims about scales, including multiple, divergent globalisms, those global worlds that most affect us are those that manage tentatively productive linkages with other scalemaking projects.

原页 57, 58

当代金融大师不仅声称具有普遍吸引力，还声称具有全球尺度的部署。我们该如何理解这些全球主义主张，及其关于一个比我们所知的更总体、更具霸权的世界制造的千禧年式的低语？在我看来，金融的全球主义主张既不是虚假意识形态，也不是显而易见的真理，而同样是一种召唤、一种戏剧表演。在这个对人类事业的空间与尺度给予高度关注的时代，经济项目不能局限于在不同尺度上召唤——它们必须召唤尺度本身。在这个意义上，一个让我们想象全球性以看到它可能如何成功的项目，是一种“尺度制造项目”；同样，让我们想象地方性、或区域与国家空间以看到其成功的项目，也是尺度制造项目。它们召唤的尺度部分通过它们被推入或偶然跌入的偶然接合而存在。在一个关于尺度有多个分歧主张的世界里，包括多个分歧的全球主义，最影响我们的全球世界，是那些与其他尺度制造项目建立暂时生产性联结的世界。

原页 58

Analytic tools with which to think about the global picture are still rudimentary. Many ethnographers find ourselves with data about how a few people somewhere react, resist, translate, consume, and from here it is an easy step to invoke distinctions between local reactions and global forces, local consumption and global circulation, local resistance and global structures of capitalism, local translations and the global imagination. I find myself doing it. Yet we know that these dichotomies are unhelpful. They draw us into an imagery in which the global is homogeneous precisely because we oppose it to the heterogeneity we identify as locality. By letting the global appear homogeneous, we open the door to its predictability and evolutionary status as the latest stage in macronarratives. We know the dichotomy between the global blob and local detail isn’t helping us. We long to find cultural specificity and contingency within the blob, but we can’t figure out how to find it without, once again, picking out locality.

原页 58

用于思考全球图景的分析工具仍然粗糙。许多民族志学者发现自己掌握着关于某地少数人如何反应、抵抗、翻译、消费的资料，从这里很容易援引地方反应与全球力量、地方消费与全球流通、地方抵抗与全球资本主义结构、地方翻译与全球想象之间的区分。我发现自己也在这么做。但我们知道这些二分法没有帮助。它们把我们拉进一种意象，在其中全球是同质的，正是因为我们把它与我们认定为地方性的异质性对立起来。让全球显得同质，我们就为它的可预测性及其作为宏大叙事最新阶段的演化地位打开了门。我们知道全球团块与地方细节之间的二分法没有帮助。我们渴望在团块内部找到文化特殊性与偶然性，却想不出如何在不再次挑选地方性的情况下找到它。

原页 58

This chapter suggests that we address these dilemmas by giving attention to the making of scale. Scale is the spatial dimensionality necessary for a particular kind of view, whether up close or from a distance, microscopic or planetary. I argue that scale is not just a neutral frame for viewing the world; scale must be brought into being: proposed, practiced, and evaded, as well as taken for granted. Scales are claimed and contested in cultural and political projects. A “globalism” is a commitment to the global, and there are multiple, overlapping, and somewhat contradictory globalisms; a “regionalism” is a commitment to the region; and so on. Not all claims and commitments about scale are particularly effective. Links among varied scale-making projects can bring each project vitality and power. The specificity of these articulations and collaborations also limits the spread and play of scale-making projects, promising them only a tentative moment in a particular history. The performative dramas of financial conjuring offer one perspective from which to appreciate the specificity and contingency of particular niches within capitalist scale-making.

原页 58

本章建议通过关注尺度的制造来处理这些困境。尺度是某种特定视角——无论是近距离还是远距离，微观还是行星——所需的空间维度性。我主张，尺度不只是观看世界的中性框架；尺度必须被带入存在：被提议、被实践、被规避，也被视为理所当然。尺度在文化与政治项目中被主张和争夺。“全球主义”是对全球的承诺，存在多个重叠且有些矛盾的全球主义；“区域主义”是对区域的承诺；如此等等。并非所有关于尺度的主张和承诺都特别有效。各种尺度制造项目之间的联结可以给每个项目带来活力与力量。这些接合与协作的特殊性也限制了尺度制造项目的传播与运作，只承诺它们在特定历史中的一个暂时时刻。金融召唤的表演性戏剧提供了一个视角，用以欣赏资本主义尺度制造中特定位置的特殊性与偶然性。

原页 58, 59

One of the chief puzzles of globalist financial conjuring is why it works. We’ve all seen ads for hamburgers, express mail, or computers bridging cultures across the globe. But it’s one thing to offer a stylish picture of diversity, and another thing to figure out how entrepreneurial projects actually manage to affect people who may not pay them any mind. Conjuring is supposed to call up a world more dreamlike and sweeter than anything that exists; magic, rather than unsparing description, calls capital. The puzzle seems deeper the more the material and social worlds to be reshaped and exploited are geographically, culturally, and politically remote from financial conjuring centers. How do the self-consciously glossy and exaggerated virtual worlds conjured by eager collectors of finance become shapers of radically different peoples and places? My frame highlights contingent articulations in which globalist financial conjuring links itself with regional and national scale-making projects, making each succeed wildly—if also partially and tentatively. It seems likely that successfully conjuring the globe is possible, at least now, only in thick collaborations with regional and national conjurings; certainly financial conjuring has been deeply implicated in promises of making regional and national dreams come true.

原页 58, 59

全球主义金融召唤的主要谜题之一是它为什么有效。我们都见过汉堡、快递或电脑跨越全球连接文化的广告。但提供一幅时髦的多样性图景是一回事，弄清创业项目实际上如何影响那些可能根本不理会它们的人是另一回事。召唤本应召唤出一个比任何存在之物都更梦幻、更甜美的世界；召唤资本的是魔法，而不是毫不留情的描述。那些将被重塑和开发的物质与社会世界在地理、文化和政治上离金融召唤中心越远，这个谜题似乎就越深。那些由急切的金融收集者自觉召唤出的、光滑而夸张的虚拟世界，如何成为截然不同的人民与地方的塑造者？我的框架强调偶然接合：全球主义金融召唤把自身与区域和国家的尺度制造项目连接起来，使每一个都取得惊人的成功——尽管也是部分地、暂时地。看来，成功召唤全球至少现在只有在与区域和国家召唤的厚实协作中才有可能；当然，金融召唤深深卷入了让区域和国家梦想成真的承诺。

原页 59, 60

Globalist conjuring sometimes supports the most bizarre and terrible of national and regional dreams. Certainly this was the case in the Bre-X story. Finance capital became linked with greedy elite dreams of an authoritarian nation-state supported by foreign funds and enterprises; this is a nationmaking project I call franchise cronyism to mark the interdependence of corruption and foreign investment. These in turn became linked with migrant dreams of a regional frontier culture in which the rights of previous rural residents could be wiped out entirely to create a Wild West scene of rapid and lawless resource extraction: quick profits, quick exits. To present this rather complicated set of links, I offer a diagram (fig. 1). Diagrams by their nature are oversimplifications, and this one is certainly no exception. To acknowledge this, I have named each of the three scale-making projects I discuss in a self-consciously joking manner. Yet the playfulness is also a serious attempt to focus attention on the specificity and process of articulation. Finance capital is a program for global hegemony; franchise cronyism is one particular nation-making project; frontier culture is an articulation of a region. Each is a scale-making project with its sights set on a different scale: global, national, and regional. The links among them cross scales and strengthen each project's ability to remake the world. At the same time, none of these three projects is predictable or ubiquitous in the world. Coming together as they did for a moment, they created a great fire. Looking back on them now, we see they didn’t create an evolutionary ladder to the stars. Isn’t this sense of engagement and contingency what scholars and social commentators most need to bring into view?

“Yes, We Are Still in Business”

Bre-X was the brainchild of a Canadian stock promoter named David Walsh. Walsh dropped out of high school at the end of tenth grade and soon joined a Montreal trust company, rising quickly to become the head of the investment department. After thirteen years, Walsh left to try to form his own trust company. Three unsuccessful years later, he agreed to start an office in Calgary for another firm, only to quit the next year. From then on, Walsh worked to set up his own companies: first, the oil-oriented Bresea Resources Ltd. (named after his sons Brett and Sean), and then, in 1985, Bre-X Minerals Ltd., which from the first aimed to find gold.10

Gold mining had become a profitable industry in the 1970s, when the United States ended the Bretton Woods standard of fixed exchange rates, and the price of gold, which had been held constant at $35 per ounce for many years, skyrocketed, hitting $850 per ounce in 1980.11 Canadian companies rushed to take advantage of the new gold prices by exploring not only in the Canadian West, but around the world. Junior mining exploration companies, whose goal is to find the minerals that can be exploited by major companies, sprouted by the dozens. Toronto became the world’s mining finance capital. In 1997, there were 1,225 publicly traded mining companies in Canada, and mining stocks represented 21.5 percent of all trades on the ‘Toronto Stock Exchange (Francis 1997: 24). In this industry, the line between various kinds of expertise is thin: geologists (with salaries supplemented by stock options) must be promoters to raise the money to finance their mineral finds, market analysts must be geologists to evaluate those finds, and stock promoters must explain their offerings in geologically convincing terms. Canadian preeminence in mining depended on both its mining history and its position as a center of mining finance.

原页 59, 60

全球主义召唤有时支持最离奇、最可怕的国家与区域梦想。布雷-X的故事确实如此。金融资本与一个威权民族国家的贪婪精英梦想连接起来，这个国家由外国资金和企业支持；我把这种建国项目称为特许经营式裙带主义（franchise cronyism），以标示腐败与外国投资的相互依赖。这些又与移民对区域边疆文化的梦想连接起来，在那里，先前乡村居民的权利可以被彻底抹除，以创造一个快速、无法无天的资源开采狂野西部场景：快速利润，快速退出。为了呈现这组相当复杂的联结，我提供一张图表（图1）。图表本质上是一种过度简化，这张当然也不例外。为了承认这一点，我以自觉开玩笑的方式命名了我所讨论的三个尺度制造项目。然而，这种游戏性也是一种严肃的尝试，要把注意力集中在接合的特殊性与过程上。金融资本是一项全球霸权纲领；特许经营式裙带主义是一个特定的建国项目；边疆文化是一个区域的接合。每一个都是尺度制造项目，各自瞄准不同的尺度：全球、国家与区域。它们之间的联结跨越尺度，并增强每个项目重塑世界的能力。与此同时，这三个项目中没有一个是可预测的或在世界上无处不在的。它们像那样短暂地汇合在一起，燃起了一场大火。现在回望，我们看到它们并没有造出一架通往星辰的演化阶梯。这种参与感与偶然感，不正是学者和社会评论者最需要带入视野的吗？

“是的，我们还在做生意”

布雷-X是加拿大股票推销员戴维·沃尔什的脑力结晶。沃尔什在十年级结束时从高中辍学，很快加入蒙特利尔一家信托公司，迅速升任投资部门主管。十三年后，沃尔什离开，试图创办自己的信托公司。三年失败后，他同意为另一家公司在卡尔加里开设办事处，结果第二年就辞职了。从那以后，沃尔什努力建立自己的公司：首先是石油导向的 Bresea Resources Ltd.（以他的儿子布雷特和肖恩命名），然后是在1985年，Bre-X Minerals Ltd.，后者从一开始就旨在寻找黄金。10

金矿开采在20世纪70年代成为有利可图的行业，当时美国结束了固定汇率的布雷顿森林体系，多年来一直保持在每盎司35美元的金价飞涨，1980年达到每盎司850美元。11加拿大公司争先恐后地利用新的金价，不仅在加拿大西部，而且在全世界勘探。初级矿业勘探公司的目标是找到可由大公司开发的矿产，它们成打地冒出来。多伦多成为世界矿业金融之都。1997年，加拿大有1,225家上市矿业公司，矿业股票占多伦多证券交易所所有交易的21.5%（Francis 1997: 24）。在这个行业中，各类专业知识之间的界线很薄：地质学家（工资由股票期权补充）必须是推销员，才能筹集资金来资助他们的矿产发现；市场分析师必须是地质学家，才能评估那些发现；股票推销员必须用地质学上令人信服的术语解释他们的发行。加拿大在矿业上的卓越地位既取决于其采矿历史，也取决于其作为矿业金融中心的地位。

原页 61

For a stock promoter like David Walsh to become president of a gold exploration company was not unusual in this climate. Consider the trajectory of the president of Barrick Gold, Canada’s biggest gold-mining company. Peter Munk is a high-flying but not always successful entrepreneur. In the 1950s, he founded a television and hi-fi company that crashed, leaving the government of Nova Scotia in deep debt; he went on to build hotels on South Sea islands funded by Saudi Arabian princes. Nothing in his background gave him expertise in minerals. In 1986, however, he bought a worked-over mine in Nevada. It turned out to be the most profitable gold mine in the world, pushing Munk’s company into a leading position (Wells 1996). Peter Munk was “a dreamer who became a king” (Newman 1996). In this context, David Walsh’s little enterprise made sense.

原页 61

在这种气候下，像戴维·沃尔什这样的股票推销员成为金矿勘探公司总裁并不罕见。想想加拿大最大的金矿公司巴里克黄金公司（Barrick Gold）总裁的轨迹。彼得·芒克是一位雄心勃勃但并非总是成功的企业家。20世纪50年代，他创办了一家电视与高保真音响公司，公司崩溃，让新斯科舍省政府深陷债务；他接着在南太平洋岛屿上建造由沙特阿拉伯王子资助的酒店。他的背景中没有任何东西给他矿产方面的专业知识。然而，1986年，他买下内华达州一座开采过的矿山。结果它成了世界上最赚钱的金矿，把芒克的公司推上领先地位（Wells 1996）。彼得·芒克是“一个成为国王的梦想家”（Newman 1996）。在这种背景下，戴维·沃尔什的小企业就说得通了。

原页 61

In 1988, Walsh listed Bre-X on the Alberta Stock Exchange at 30 Canadian cents per share. His wife Jeanette supported the household by working as a secretary. The family bought on credit, and, over C$200,000 in debt, both David and Jeanette Walsh declared personal bankruptcy in 1992. Bre-X shares sometimes fell as low as two cents; in his 1991 annual report, David Walsh wrote, “Yes, we are still in business.” In 1993, however, Walsh pulled together some money for a trip to Indonesia. There he met Dutchborn geologist John Felderhof, who had achieved some fame in identifying the Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea in 1967, but suffered hard times in the 1980s. Felderof agreed to help Walsh find gold in Kalimantan and contacted Filipino geologist Michael de Guzman for the project. Filipino geologists had been in great demand in Indonesia because of their experience, education, and regional savvy.12 De Guzman brought several Filipino associates to the team.13

原页 61

1988年，沃尔什以每股30加拿大分让布雷-X在阿尔伯塔证券交易所上市。他的妻子珍妮特当秘书养家。这家人靠信贷购物，负债超过20万加元，戴维和珍妮特·沃尔什于1992年双双宣布个人破产。布雷-X股票有时跌到两加拿大分；在1991年的年度报告中，戴维·沃尔什写道：“是的，我们还在做生意。”然而1993年，沃尔什凑了一些钱去印尼旅行。在那里，他遇到荷兰出生的地质学家约翰·费尔德霍夫，后者因1967年发现巴布亚新几内亚的奥克泰迪（Ok Tedi）铜金矿而获得一些名声，但在20世纪80年代经历艰难时期。费尔德霍夫同意帮助沃尔什在加里曼丹寻找黄金，并联系菲律宾地质学家迈克尔·德·古兹曼参与该项目。由于他们的经验、教育和区域见识，菲律宾地质学家在印尼需求很大。12德·古兹曼把几位菲律宾同事带进团队。13

原页 61, 62

Mining properties were cheap and available in Indonesia in the early 1990s because the Australians, who had come in some ten years before in their own wave of national mining speculation, were trying to get out. Felderhof had worked for some Australian companies and had witnessed the financial boom and bust in which mineral exploration was begun and then abandoned, promising or not. He convinced Walsh to form a partnership with an Indonesian entrepreneur to buy an old Australian claim around the creek called Busang in East Kalimantan, and Walsh raised the money to drill some holes. ‘The results were disappointing, and by December 1993 they were about to close the property. Then, early in 1994, de Guzman struck gold. Walsh was quick and effective in informing investor newsletters and brokerage firms. Felderhof’s estimates grew bigger and bigger. In 1993, Bre-X was trading at 51 Canadian cents a share; by May 1996, stocks were trading at C$286.50, accounting for a ten-to-one split. In April, Bre-X had been listed on the ‘Toronto Stock Exchange; in August, the stock was listed in the United States on NASDAQ; in September, it was also listed on the Montreal Stock Exchange. By then the company’s market capitalization was over C$6 billion (Goold and Willis 1997: 64-65). Awards started to roll in: Mining Man of the Year for Bre-X President David Walsh; Explorer of the Year for chief geologist John Felderhof. On March 9 and 10, 1997, Bre-X officers and geologists were feted in awards dinners and ceremonies at the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada meetings. They were at the height of their success.

原页 61, 62

20世纪90年代初，印尼的矿产地便宜且可得，因为大约十年前在自己国家矿业投机浪潮中进来的澳大利亚人正试图退出。费尔德霍夫曾为一些澳大利亚公司工作，目睹了金融繁荣与萧条的周期：矿产勘探被启动，然后被放弃，无论有没有前景。他说服沃尔什与一位印尼企业家合伙，买下东加里曼丹一条叫布桑的小溪周围一块旧的澳大利亚矿权地，沃尔什筹集资金钻了一些孔。结果令人失望，到1993年12月，他们准备关闭这块地产。然后，1994年初，德·古兹曼挖到了金矿。沃尔什迅速有效地告知投资者通讯和经纪公司。费尔德霍夫的估计越来越大。1993年，布雷-X的股价为每股51加拿大分；到1996年5月，股价达到286.50加元，计入十比一拆股。4月，布雷-X已在多伦多证券交易所上市；8月，股票在美国纳斯达克上市；9月，它又在蒙特利尔证券交易所上市。到那时，公司市值超过60亿加元（Goold and Willis 1997: 64-65）。奖项开始滚滚而来：布雷-X总裁戴维·沃尔什获年度矿业人物；首席地质学家约翰·费尔德霍夫获年度勘探者。1997年3月9日和10日，布雷-X高管和地质学家在加拿大勘探者与开发者协会会议的颁奖晚宴和仪式上受到庆贺。他们正处于成功的顶点。

原页 62

Conjuring

On March 19, 1997, Michael de Guzman fell 800 feet from a helicopter into the rainforests of Kalimantan. Although up to that point he had been considered little more than the Filipino sidekick, at the moment of his death, de Guzman became the company, his face displayed everywhere in the news media over charts of the company’s finds and stock prices. If Bre-X had been a big story before, it was truly dramatic now.

原页 62

召唤

1997年3月19日，迈克尔·德·古兹曼从直升机上坠入加里曼丹雨林，落差800英尺。尽管在此之前他几乎只被视为菲律宾跟班，但在死亡时刻，德·古兹曼成了公司本身，他的面孔在各处新闻媒体上展示，覆盖着公司发现和股价的图表。如果布雷-X以前是个大新闻，现在它就真的充满戏剧性了。

原页 62, 63

Mysteries abounded. A suicide note was found in which de Guzman wrote that he couldn’t stand the pain of hepatitis; but he was an optimistic man and in quite good health. What happened to the third man the other Filipino geologists had seen enter the helicopter? Rumors circulated like wildfire. One Philippines scholar confided to me, “When I heard about the watch found in the helicopter, I had to find out what kind it was. When they said ‘Rolex,’ I knew he was murdered. No Filipino gangster would dispose of his victim without first removing his Rolex.” A sign, a trophy. The trouble was, the scene was cluttered with signs, clues, false leads. Wives of de Guzman who knew nothing of each others’ existence cropped up everywhere: in Manila, Jakarta, Manado, Samarinda. Rumors circulated that de Guzman had parachuted into Zurich. When a corpse was finally found, the face and much of the body had been devoured by wild pigs. Multiple autopsies failed to establish the identity of the body beyond controversy: Could Bre-X have changed the fingerprint on his employee identity card? Did the dental records match? And where were his geologist friends when it was time for the funeral?14

It was at this period, too, that the gold deposit at Busang came to seem just as mysterious. Bre-X had been drilling core samples at Busang since 1993; by 1997, some sites looked like “Swiss cheese” (Hajari 1997). As Busang became famous, industry professionals came to visit. Bre-X President Walsh later complained, “Virtually every mining geologist, analyst went to the site, but I never received one letter or phone call during that whole period that something was amiss over in Indonesia” (Calgary Sun, October 12, 1997). The “analysts” Walsh refers to were mining stock analysts, and, indeed, dozens visited the site, each fueling investors’ attraction with more glowing reports. But in March 1997, the U.S. company Freeport McMoRan sent their assayors as the “due diligence” element of their agreement to become partners with Bre-X at Busang. Freeport found nothing. Furthermore, they claimed that the kind of gold in Bre-X’s samples was inappropriate for the site: It was stream-rounded alluvial gold instead of igneous gold. Bre-X’s assay methods were now open to question. Rumors flew of plots and coverups, and the price of Bre-X stocks roller-coasted. Perhaps Freeport was making false claims to take over the property. Perhaps Bob Hasan, an Indonesian partner, was buying up cheap stocks at a bargain-basement price. Why else had he taken out a bank loan to log just in this area, just at this time? Perhaps New York investors were trying to beat out Canadians. The gamble drew stock speculators into the fray and on April 2, the trading was so intense that it closed down the computer system at the Toronto Stock Exchange.15 On May 3, however, the independent test report arrived. Its finding: no economic gold deposit. ‘The ballooning stock swap immediately deflated; Bre-X stocks were officially worthless.16 Yet what are we to make of the mysteries?

原页 62, 63

谜团层出不穷。人们发现一封遗书，德·古兹曼在信中写道，他受不了肝炎的痛苦；但他是个乐观的人，身体相当好。其他菲律宾地质学家看到登上直升机的第三个人后来去了哪里？谣言像野火一样传播。一位菲律宾学者向我吐露：“当我听说直升机里发现一块手表时，我必须弄清那是什么牌子。当他们说‘劳力士’时，我就知道他被谋杀了。没有哪个菲律宾歹徒会在除掉受害者之前不先摘下他的劳力士。”一个标记，一件战利品。麻烦的是，现场满是标记、线索和错误导向。德·古兹曼那些彼此不知道对方存在的妻子们到处冒出来：马尼拉、雅加达、万鸦老、三马林达。有谣言说德·古兹曼跳伞降落到苏黎世。当终于找到一具尸体时，脸和大部分身体已被野猪吞食。多次尸检未能毫无争议地确定尸体身份：布雷-X是否可能换掉了他员工身份证上的指纹？牙科记录吻合吗？到了葬礼的时候，他的地质学家朋友们又在哪里？14

也正是在这个时期，布桑的金矿藏变得同样神秘。布雷-X自1993年以来一直在布桑钻取岩芯样本；到1997年，一些地点看起来像“瑞士奶酪”（Hajari 1997）。随着布桑出名，业界专业人士前来参观。布雷-X总裁沃尔什后来抱怨：“几乎每位矿业地质学家、分析师都去过现场，但在那整个时期，我从未收到一封信或一个电话说印尼那边有什么不对”（Calgary Sun, October 12, 1997）。沃尔什所指的“分析师”是矿业股票分析师，确实有几十人参观了现场，每个人都用更多热情洋溢的报告助长投资者的兴趣。但在1997年3月，美国公司自由港麦克莫兰（Freeport McMoRan）派出他们的化验员，作为与布雷-X在布桑合作协定中的“尽职调查”环节。自由港什么也没发现。此外，他们声称布雷-X样本中的那种黄金不适合该地：那是河流磨圆的冲积金，而不是火成岩中的金。布雷-X的化验方法现在受到质疑。关于阴谋与掩盖的谣言四起，布雷-X股价像过山车一样起伏。也许自由港在作出虚假声明以接管该地产。也许印尼合伙人鲍勃·哈桑正以跳楼价买进廉价股票。否则他为什么偏偏在这个时候、偏偏在这个地区贷款伐木？也许纽约投资者正试图击败加拿大人。这场赌博把股票投机者卷入混战，4月2日交易如此激烈，以至于多伦多证券交易所的计算机系统关闭。15然而5月3日，独立测试报告到了。其结论是：没有经济上可开采的金矿。膨胀的股票价值立刻泄了气；布雷-X股票正式变得一文不值。16然而，我们该如何理解这些谜团？

原页 63

I am not a journalist, and my concern does not involve just which gold miners and which Indonesian government officials and which stock market participants knew about or participated in various conjuring acts. I’m more interested in the art of conjuring itself, as practiced not only by Bre-X officers and employees but also by the analysts, reporters, investors, and regulators who formed their retinue. I am struck by two counterintuitive observations. First, mystery, rumor, and drama did not come to Bre-X at the tail end of its ride; these qualities marked the Bre-X story from its beginnings. Rather than closing Bre-X down, mystery and drama kept Bre-X alive and growing; it was only when an official report stopped the show that the company died. Second, Bre-X is not the only company that has required spectacle to grow. Bre-X seems typical of the junior Canadian mineral exploration companies that it has helped usher into the international spotlight—except, of course, it was more successful at first and later more despised. Junior companies don’t have the equipment or capital to take their mining ventures very far. They must make a big splash, first, to attract enough investors to keep prospecting, and, second, to bring in big mining companies to buy out their finds.

原页 63

我不是记者，我的关切并不只是哪些金矿商、哪些印尼政府官员和哪些股市参与者知道或参与了各种召唤行为。我更感兴趣的是召唤这门艺术本身，不仅由布雷-X的高管和雇员实践，也由组成其随从的分析师、记者、投资者和监管者实践。有两个反直觉的观察让我印象深刻。第一，神秘、谣言和戏剧性并不是在布雷-X之旅的尾端才出现的；这些品质从一开始就标记着布雷-X的故事。神秘与戏剧没有终结布雷-X，反而让它存活并成长；直到一份官方报告叫停演出，公司才死亡。第二，布雷-X并不是唯一需要奇观才能成长的公司。布雷-X似乎是加拿大初级矿产勘探公司的典型——它曾帮助这类公司进入国际聚光灯——当然，除了它起初更成功、后来更受鄙视。初级公司没有设备或资本把采矿事业推进很远。它们必须首先制造大轰动，以吸引足够投资者继续勘探；其次，引入大型矿业公司买下它们的发现。

原页 63, 64

One can draw the net wider. The mystery and spectacle Bre-X cultivated is representative of many kinds of companies in which finance capital is the ruling edge of accumulation. Such companies draw investments through drama. And the importance of drama guarantees that it is very difficult to discern companies that have long-term production potential from those that are merely good at being on stage. The charismatic and dramatic attraction of international finance capital was a key feature of Southeast Asian development strategies during the “economic miracle.” After the 1997 financial crisis, we were told to distinguish between the real and the fake, but does not the whole design of these accumulation strategies work against our ability to draw this line? As in a beauty contest, artistry and drama are necessary to compete; spectacle and mystery, playing equally across the line of the real and the fake, establish the winning reality of performance.17

原页 63, 64

人们可以把网撒得更宽。布雷-X培育的神秘与奇观，代表了许多由金融资本主导积累的公司。这类公司通过戏剧吸引投资。戏剧的重要性保证了很难分辨哪些公司具有长期生产潜力，哪些只是擅长登台表演。国际金融资本的感召力与戏剧性吸引力，是“经济奇迹”时期东南亚发展战略的关键特征。1997年金融危机后，我们被告知要区分真实与虚假，但这些积累策略的整个设计难道不是在妨碍我们划出这条线吗？就像选美比赛，技艺与戏剧性是竞争所必需的；奇观与神秘同样在真实与虚假的界线上发挥作用，确立表演的胜利现实。17

原页 64

Bre-X initially attracted investors because of the excitement of the reports coming out about Busang. From the very first, Bre-X was in the news, and journalists constantly wrote about Busang. The success with which Bre-X attracted investors depended on these reports, and particularly on the ways they used and elaborated tropes that brought the Bre-X find into other circulating stories of wealth, power, and fulfillment. Some of these stories were colonial adventure tales: the search for hidden, uncounted riches in remote places. Maclean’s, a Canadian magazine, wrote: “Two, four, and then maybe six million ounces will be pulled from Busang annually. There has never been an El Dorado like this” (Wells 1997c: 40). Other stories told of frontier independence and the promise of wealth “at the end of a miner’s rainbow,” as the New York Times put it, where “independent-mindedness” led miners to “forbidding jungles” in search of the “century’s greatest gold strike” (DePalma 1997: Al). There were stories of science in the service of human innovation. There were stories of war and conquest—“the battle for Busang”—recalling the French and the United States in Vietnam, and BreX became, repeatedly, a “rumble in the jungle,” and then, eventually, a “bungle” or a “jumble” in the jungle.18

原页 64

布雷-X最初吸引投资者，是因为关于布桑的报道带来的兴奋。从一开始，布雷-X就出现在新闻中，记者不断报道布桑。布雷-X吸引投资者的成功取决于这些报道，尤其取决于它们使用和铺陈那些把布雷-X发现带入其他流通故事——关于财富、权力和圆满的故事——的修辞方式。其中一些故事是殖民冒险故事：在偏远地方寻找隐藏的、未被清点的财富。加拿大杂志《麦克林》写道：“每年将从布桑开采出两百万、四百万，然后也许六百万盎司。从来没有过这样的黄金国”（Wells 1997c: 40）。其他故事讲述边疆独立和“在矿工彩虹尽头”的财富承诺，如《纽约时报》所说，在那里，“独立精神”把矿工引向“令人生畏的丛林”，寻找“世纪最大的金矿发现”（DePalma 1997: A1）。还有科学服务于人类创新的故事。还有战争与征服的故事——“布桑之战”——让人想起法国和美国在越南，布雷-X反复成为“丛林混战”（rumble in the jungle），最终变成“丛林里的烂摊子”（bungle）或“一团乱麻”（jumble）。18

原页 64, 65

There were also pervasive stories of underdog charisma. After announcing the Busang find, Bre-X had to fight for the rights to mine it. The story of little Bre-X up against the big North American mining companies and the big Indonesian establishment generated an overwhelming response, ushering in Bre-X’s greatest period of popular investment. When U.S. exPresident George Bush and Canadian ex-Prime Minister Brian Mulroney put pressure on Jakarta at the request of a big company, Bre-X’s David Walsh, with his high school education, his beer belly, and his ineptness, looked like David up against Goliath. He made such a convincing “little guy” that after the scam was exposed, many refused to imagine him responsible. As Fortune magazine’s reporter wrote, “Even now I have trouble believing that Walsh participated.... Walsh looked more like some poor schlemiel who had just won the lottery and couldn’t locate his ticket” (Behar 1997: 123).

Stockholders, too, contributed to the stories swirling around Bre-X.19 Bre-X established an Internet presence early on, with stories posted on their Web site; meanwhile, investors’ chat lines buzzed with Bre-X news.20 The more controversy swirled around Bre-X, the more investors talked and exchanged rumors, extending, too, dreams of wealth, conspiracy theories, reinterpretations of the mining geology and engineering, and romances of unexpected underdog advantage. On the Internet, dramatic presentation was often clearly the point. As one Silicon Investor contributor wrote about the Bre-X Internet thread, “The theater is open. The stage is set 24 hours a day. There is always an audience” (Zgodzinski 1997).

原页 64, 65

还有无处不在的弱者感召力故事。宣布布桑发现后，布雷-X必须争夺采矿权。小布雷-X对抗北美大型矿业公司和印尼大型权势集团的故事引发了压倒性反响，带来了布雷-X最盛大的大众投资时期。当美国前总统乔治·布什和加拿大前总理布赖恩·马尔罗尼应一家大公司要求向雅加达施压时，布雷-X的戴维·沃尔什——只有高中学历、挺着啤酒肚、笨拙无能——看起来就像对抗歌利亚的大卫。他把“小人物”演得如此令人信服，以至于骗局曝光后，许多人拒绝想象他要负责。正如《财富》杂志记者所写：“即便现在，我也很难相信沃尔什参与了……沃尔什看起来更像某个刚中了彩票、却找不到彩票的可怜家伙”（Behar 1997: 123）。

股东们也为围绕布雷-X的故事添砖加瓦。19布雷-X很早就建立了互联网存在，在网站上发布故事；与此同时，投资者的聊天热线嗡嗡作响，传播布雷-X的新闻。20围绕布雷-X的争议越多，投资者就越谈论、交换谣言，也延伸着财富梦想、阴谋论、对采矿地质学与工程学的重新解释，以及关于弱者意外优势的浪漫故事。在互联网上，戏剧性呈现往往显然就是重点。正如一位 Silicon Investor 撰稿人关于布雷-X网络讨论串所写：“剧院开门了。舞台一天24小时搭好。总有观众”（Zgodzinski 1997）。

原页 65

One Internet contributor signed herself “Ole49er,” reminding readers that the Wild West is never far from discussion of Bre-X. A Canadian shareholder with whom I spoke explained that Canadians were excited about the chance to invest in minerals in Indonesia because of the symbolic importance of mining in Canada as well as a national anxiety about the closing of the frontier. Environmental regulations in Canada, he explained, made it difficult to mine profitably in the last wide open spaces of the Canadian West. Yet those open spaces might be pursued abroad in foreign lands. As a substitute frontier, Bre-X’s Kalimantan continued the excitement of the frontier story of Canada’s development.

原页 65

一位互联网撰稿人署名“Ole49er”，提醒读者狂野西部从未远离关于布雷-X的讨论。一位与我交谈的加拿大股东解释说，加拿大人对有机会投资印尼矿产感到兴奋，既因为采矿在加拿大的象征重要性，也因为一种关于边疆关闭的民族焦虑。他解释说，加拿大的环境法规使得在加拿大西部最后的空旷地区进行有利可图的采矿变得困难。然而那些空旷空间也许可以在外国的土地上追寻。作为替代边疆，布雷-X的加里曼丹延续了加拿大发展边疆故事的兴奋。

原页 65

But what of Kalimantan in this story? In the moment of frontier making, financial conjuring runs up against the landscape, but not quite as in its dreams. At this trick in the magic show, an opportunity presents itself to ask about how the magic works, and how it doesn’t.

原页 65

但在这个故事里，加里曼丹又如何？在边疆制造的时刻，金融召唤撞上地景，但并非完全如其梦想。在魔术表演的这一招中，出现了一个机会，去追问魔法如何运作，以及如何不运作。

原页 65

Frontiers

Let me return to the beginning of the Bre-X story, or, at least, one beginning, in Kalimantan. A brave man is hacking his way through the jungle, alone and surrounded by disease and danger. There is nothing there but mud, malaria, leeches, hepatitis, and the pervasive loneliness of the jungle trek. But one day . . . he discovers gold!

原页 65

边疆

让我回到布雷-X故事的开头，或者至少是它在加里曼丹的一个开头。一个勇敢的男人在丛林中披荆斩棘，独自一人，周围是疾病与危险。那里只有泥浆、疟疾、水蛭、肝炎，以及丛林跋涉中无处不在的孤独。但有一天……他发现黄金！

原页 65

This is an old story, told not only about Borneo, but about many a jungle or lonely rock cliff. But it is also what the Bre-X miners told the press. According to the Far Eastern Economic Review (McBeth 1997: 42-43):

原页 65

这是一个古老的故事，不仅关于婆罗洲，也关于许多丛林或孤寂岩壁。但这也是布雷-X矿工告诉媒体的故事。据《远东经济评论》（McBeth 1997: 42-43）报道：

原页 65

The story of how Felderhof and de Guzman unearthed Busang’s golden secret is the stuff that fables are made of. Mostly it is a human saga—about two quiet, very ordinary men from opposite sides of the world who persevered for years in the face of tropical illnesses and some of the harshest terrain in the world....

原页 65

关于费尔德霍夫和德·古兹曼如何发掘出布桑黄金秘密的故事，是寓言的材料。它主要是一部人类传奇——关于两个来自世界两端、安静而非常普通的人，面对热带疾病和世界上最严酷的地形，坚持了多年……

原页 66

Felderhof first landed in Indonesia in 1980.... [H]e worked his way from west to east across the centre of the vast Borneo island.... Those were hard times. He lived in jungle villages, eating whatever was available, carrying what he needed on his back, and hacking his way through some of the remotest rain forest in Asia.

原页 66

费尔德霍夫1980年首次抵达印尼……他沿着广阔的婆罗洲岛中部从西向东行进……那是艰难时期。他住在丛林村庄，有什么就吃什么，把需要的东西背在背上，在亚洲最偏远的雨林中披荆斩棘。

原页 66

De Guzman has gone through similar hardships. . . . He’s had malaria 14 times since he met up with Felderhof in 1986.... Travelling alone, de Guzman took a seven-hour boat ride up the Mahakam River, then trekked 32 kilometers.... During a week of old-fashioned prospecting, he recognized a geological setting he had come to know well in the Philippines.

原页 66

德·古兹曼也经历了类似的艰辛……自1986年与费尔德霍夫相识以来，他已经得过14次疟疾……德·古兹曼独自旅行，乘船沿马哈坎河上行七小时，然后徒步32公里……在一周的老式勘探中，他认出了自己在菲律宾早已熟悉的地质环境。

原页 66

The story has come close to the moment of discovery. ‘he New York Times tells that moment succinctly: “1994. Michael de Guzman, a mining geologist, is trekking through the Busang site doing work for Bre-X when a bit of yellow rock on a river bank catches his eye. ‘Check it out,’ he writes on a plastic strip and tacks it to the rock. His assistant follows with a more detailed analysis and writes: ‘Checkmate’” (DePalma 1997: C10).

原页 66

故事已经接近发现的那一刻。《纽约时报》简洁地讲述了那一刻：“1994年。矿业地质学家迈克尔·德·古兹曼为布雷-X在布桑现场徒步勘察时，河岸上一点黄色岩石引起了他的注意。‘检查一下，’他写在一条塑料带上，钉在岩石上。他的助手随后做了更详细的分析，并写道：‘将死’”（DePalma 1997: C10）。

原页 66

One might be suspicious of this sudden appearance from nowhere of an assistant, but let’s let that pass and move on to the second act in the discovery, the scientific theory that lets the miners know that a glitter of gold might be the tip of an underground hoard. Without science, de Guzman is just a Filipino guy playing with rocks; with science, he is the translator between nature and North American industry.

原页 66

人们可能会怀疑这位助手突然从无处出现，但我们先放过这一点，进入发现的第二幕：那套让矿工知道一点金光也许只是地下宝藏尖端的科学理论。没有科学，德·古兹曼只是一个玩石头的菲律宾人；有了科学，他就是自然与北美工业之间的译者。

原页 66

Working alone at 3 o’clock one morning, it suddenly became crystal clear [to de Guzman]. Bounding upstairs, he woke Puspos [the assistant] and explained his theory: that Busang, with its dome-like geological structure, lay at a faultline crossroads. Together on that January morning, the two spent eight hours in “nonstop technical brainstorming.” (McBeth 1997: 44)

原页 66

一天凌晨三点，独自工作的[德·古兹曼]突然豁然开朗。他跳上楼，叫醒普斯波斯[助手]，解释他的理论：布桑的穹顶状地质构造位于断层线交叉处。在那个一月的早晨，两人一起花了八小时进行“不间断的技术头脑风暴”。（McBeth 1997: 44）

原页 66, 67

It is a lovely story, but it bears a very odd relationship to everything else one might want to say about mining in Kalimantan. By the time de Guzman arrived at Busang, foreign prospectors, migrant miners, and local residents had all combed the landscape for gold. Yet his “discovery” story does not reflect the interdependence of his knowledge with that of other miners. Local residents, government regulations, mining camps, churches, markets, bus schedules, army officers, village heads, property disputes: all are missing. The frontier story requires that de Guzman wander alone on an empty landscape.

The story of lonely prospectors making independent discoveries in a remote jungle moved North American investors and stimulated the capital flow that made Bre-X rich, These images are repeated in the portfolio of every North American prospecting company working in Kalimantan. Consider the exploration of a Canadian prospecting company called International Pursuit, as reported in Gold Newsletter’s Mining Share Focus. International Pursuit was prospecting in the wake of the Bre-X drama and needed to distance itself from Bre-X. Yet the frontier story is precisely the same. The company has sent its prospectors to the empty, wild landscape of Kalimantan, where, through a combination of luck and science, they stumble on precious metals. They are especially in luck because in late 1997 the devastation brought about by El Nifio drought and forest fires had given the landscape some of the wild loneliness of which they dreamed. El Nifio, they say, was a godsend because the streams dried up, revealing hidden minerals. “(I]t was as if Mother Nature had lifted a curtain, exposing the secrets below” (Lundin 1998: 4). Ignoring local residents’ hunger, fire damage, smoke inhalation, and displacement, he bragged, “International Pursuit’s exploration teams were among the relative few left on the ground” (ibid.).

原页 66, 67

这是一个可爱的故事，但它与人们可能想说的关于加里曼丹采矿的一切都保持着非常奇怪的关系。到德·古兹曼抵达布桑时，外国探矿者、移民矿工和当地居民都已经把这片地景梳过一遍寻找黄金。然而他的“发现”故事并未反映他的知识与其他矿工知识的相互依赖。当地居民、政府法规、采矿营地、教堂、市场、公交时刻表、军官、村长、财产纠纷：全都缺失了。边疆故事要求德·古兹曼独自漫步在一片空无的地景上。

孤独探矿者在偏远丛林中做出独立发现的故事打动了北美投资者，刺激了使布雷-X致富的资本流动。这些意象在每一家在加里曼丹运作的北美勘探公司的宣传册中重复。以一家名为 International Pursuit 的加拿大勘探公司的勘探为例，正如《黄金通讯》的《矿业股票焦点》所报道。International Pursuit 在布雷-X戏剧之后进行勘探，需要与布雷-X保持距离。然而边疆故事完全相同。公司把探矿者送到加里曼丹空旷、狂野的地景，在那里，靠运气与科学的结合，他们偶然发现贵金属。他们尤其幸运，因为1997年末厄尔尼诺干旱与森林大火造成的破坏，给地景带来了一些他们梦寐以求的荒凉孤独。他们说，厄尔尼诺是天赐之物，因为溪流干涸，露出了隐藏的矿物。“就好像大自然母亲拉起了一块幕布，露出下面的秘密”（Lundin 1998: 4）。他无视当地居民的饥饿、火灾损失、吸入烟雾和流离失所，夸口说：“International Pursuit 的勘探队是相对少数留在现场的队伍之一”（同上）。

原页 67

I first began to think about gold mining because of the spread of desolation and wildness across large swathes of the Kalimantan landscape. A new landscape had developed in resource extraction areas: Quiet scenes of forests, fields, and houses had become wild terrains of danger, urgency, and destruction. The mad rush for gold joined and stimulated mad rushes for logs, birds’ nests, incense woods, marble, and even sand.

原页 67

我最初开始思考金矿开采，是因为荒芜与荒野在加里曼丹大片地景上蔓延。资源开采区出现了一种新地景：森林、田野和房屋的安静场景变成了充满危险、紧迫和毁灭的狂野地形。疯狂的淘金热加入并刺激了对原木、燕窝、香木、大理石甚至沙子的疯狂争夺。

原页 67

As I discussed in chapter 1, three developments were essential to this transformation of the terrain. First, big and small entrepreneurs were interdependent. Transnational companies and transregional migrants from all over Indonesia complemented each other. In mining, big companies have official permits; independent miners are illegal. Independent miners lead company prospectors to the best spots. The companies displace them but then employ them for prospecting. The companies complain about the illegals, blaming them for environmental problems, thus protecting their own reputations. The illegals supply everyday services for the companies. The companies follow the small miners and the small miners cluster around the companies; they become codependents.

原页 67

正如我在第一章所讨论的，三个发展对这种地形转变至关重要。第一，大大小小的企业家相互依赖。跨国公司与来自印尼各地的跨区域移民相互补充。在采矿中，大公司有正式许可；独立矿工是非法的。独立矿工把公司探矿者引向最好的地点。公司把他们赶走，但随后又雇他们探矿。公司抱怨非法矿工，把环境问题归咎于他们，从而保护自己的名声。非法矿工为公司提供日常服务。公司跟随小矿工，小矿工聚集在公司周围；他们成了相互依赖者。

原页 67, 68

Second, nature had to be made into loot, free for all. In the 1980s, logging companies worked hard to extinguish local rights to resources. “This place belongs to Indonesia, not to you,” the logging bosses said when residents complained. The military followed and supported their claims, creating an authoritarian lawlessness that made resources free for those who could take them. By the mid-1990s, local residents said, “We still know our customary rights, but no one cares about them.” The roads invited migrants. Violence became key to ownership. Swarming miners escalated the terror, the risk, and the urgency of taking everything out, right away.

原页 67, 68

第二，自然必须被制造成战利品，任人争抢。20世纪80年代，伐木公司努力消灭当地人的资源权利。“这个地方属于印尼，不属于你们，”居民抱怨时伐木老板说。军队跟随并支持他们的主张，制造了一种威权的无法无天状态，使有能力夺走资源的人可以任意攫取。到20世纪90年代中期，当地居民说：“我们仍然知道自己的习惯权利，但没人在乎。”道路招来了移民。暴力成为所有权的关键。蜂拥而至的矿工升级了恐怖、风险，以及立刻把所有东西搬走的紧迫性。

原页 68

Third, frontier migrants arrived at the end of long chains of culture and capital. Small miners rarely owned the hydraulic pumps with which they removed topsoil; they contracted them from urban entrepreneurs in profitsharing arrangements. Often, they subcontracted with local residents, dividing imagined profits even further. Migrants and local residents learned to share cultural practices of entrepreneurship that reached from distant cities deep into the forest. Local residents brought mining activities up the rivers, through their familiar forests, close to home, spreading frontier standards of rapid resource extraction. They have been drawn into the competition and violence of frontier relationships, taking on even the superficial trappings of migrant-oriented subsistence. In these entrepreneurial chains, a spreading frontier culture is created. It is a culture dedicated to the obliteration of local places, local land and resource rights, and local knowledges of flora and fauna. The makeshift camps of the miners proliferate across the landscape, mixing migrants and local residents in an anti-local regionality in which commitment to the local landscape is as useless as the gravel residue left after gold has been picked out and taken away.

原页 68

第三，边疆移民抵达于漫长的文化与资本链条末端。小矿工很少拥有他们用来剥离表土的水压泵；他们以利润分成安排从城市企业家那里承包。他们常常与当地居民再分包，把想象的利润分得更细。移民与当地居民学会了共享企业家精神的文化实践，这种实践从遥远城市一直深入森林。当地居民把采矿活动带向上游，穿过他们熟悉的森林，靠近家园，传播快速资源开采的边疆标准。他们被拉入边疆关系的竞争与暴力，甚至接受了面向移民的生存方式的表面装束。在这些企业家链条中，一种蔓延的边疆文化被创造出来。这种文化致力于抹除地方场所、地方土地与资源权利，以及地方关于动植物群的知识。矿工的临时营地在地景上增殖，把移民与当地居民混合进一种反地方的区域性，在其中，对地方地景的承诺就像金子被挑走搬走后留下的砾石残渣一样无用。

原页 68

Frontier culture is a conjuring act because it creates the wild and spreading regionality of its imagination. It conjures a self-conscious translocalism, committed to the obliteration of local places. Such commitments are themselves distinctive and limited—and thus “local” from another perspective. Yet they break with past localisms in self-conscious regionalism. This is a conjuring of scale, and frontier resource extraction relies on it.

原页 68

边疆文化是一种召唤行为，因为它创造出它想象中的狂野而蔓延的区域性。它召唤一种自觉的跨地方主义，致力于抹除地方场所。这类承诺本身是独特的、有限的——因此从另一个视角看是“地方的”。然而它们在自觉的区域主义中与过去的乡土主义决裂。这是对尺度的召唤，边疆资源开采依赖它。

原页 68

A distinctive feature of this frontier regionality is its magical vision; it asks participants to see a landscape that doesn’t exist, at least not yet. It must continually erase old residents’ rights to create its wild and empty spaces where discovering resources, not stealing them, is possible. To do so, too, it must cover up the conditions of its own production. Consider the contrasts between the features of the story of the frontier that must be told and the frontier conditions I observed: The lone prospector replaces swarming migrants and residents, searching the landscape. The excitement of scientific discovery replaces the violence of expropriation as local resource rights are extinguished and armed gangs enforce their preeminence. The autonomy of the prospector’s find replaces the interdependent negotiations of big companies and illegal miners, each leading the other to new sites and trading political and material assets as they form complementary players.21

原页 68

这种边疆区域性的一个显著特征是它的魔法视觉；它要求参与者看见一片并不存在、至少尚未存在的地景。它必须不断抹除旧居民的权利，以创造其狂野而空无的空间，在其中发现资源而不是偷窃资源是可能的。为此，它还必须掩盖自身生产的条件。想想必须讲述的边疆故事特征与我观察到的边疆条件之间的对比：孤独探矿者取代蜂拥的移民与居民，在地景上搜寻。科学发现的兴奋取代了剥夺的暴力，因为当地资源权利被消灭，武装团伙强制推行其优势。探矿者发现的自主性取代了大公司与非法矿工相互依赖的谈判，他们彼此引领到新地点，并在形成互补参与者时交换政治与物质资产。21

原页 68, 69

Why does the frontier story have any power at all, considering what it erases? How can it imagine the Kalimantan landscape so wrongly? These trompe l’oeils became possible because of national discipline: the violence of the military, which spreads a regional lawlessness; the legal regulations that privileged company rights and profits yet allowed illegal migrants to accumulate in the spreading wildness; the confusion between private entrepreneurship and public office that forged the national government. This is not the only kind of nation-making that can exist. To explore its specificity, it is useful to turn our attention to CoWs.

原页 68, 69

鉴于它抹除了什么，边疆故事为什么还有任何力量？它怎么能如此错误地想象加里曼丹地景？这些错视画之所以成为可能，是因为国家纪律：军队的暴力，传播一种区域性的无法无天；法律法规赋予公司权利与利润特权，却允许非法移民在蔓延的荒野中积聚；私人企业家精神与公职之间的混淆，锻造了国家政府。这并不是唯一可能存在的建国方式。为了探讨其特殊性，把注意力转向CoW是有用的。

原页 69

CoWs

CoWs are Contracts of Work. No mining company can extract minerals in Indonesia without one. Like animals, CoWs come in generations. The first CoW was a much revered and singular ancestor, granted to Louisiana’s Freeport McMoRan to mine in West Papua.22 Succeeding generations of CoWs have become more differentiated, more limited, and more finely detailed.23 Yet as they develop, they continue to be icons, even fetishes, held up to show the relationship between the Indonesian nation and the world. Ideally, they guarantee that resource extraction activities work in the interests of the Indonesian nation as well as the mining company. They specify the conditions that create mutual benefits shared between the nation and its foreign investors.

原页 69

CoW

CoW 是采矿合同（Contracts of Work）。没有它，任何矿业公司都不能在印尼开采矿产。像动物一样，CoW 也分代。第一份 CoW 是一位备受尊崇的独特祖先，授予路易斯安那州的自由港麦克莫兰公司，在西巴布亚采矿。22随后的各代 CoW 变得更加分化、更加有限、细节更加精细。23然而在发展中，它们仍然是偶像，甚至是被崇拜的灵物，被举起来展示印尼国家与世界的关系。理想情况下，它们保证资源开采活动既服务于印尼国家的利益，也服务于矿业公司的利益。它们规定了创造国家与外国投资者互利共赢的条件。

原页 69

CoWs have been magical tools of the national elite. Although merely paper and ink, they conjured a regular income for the Indonesian nationstate. Their terms must be secure and attractive by international standards, or they will not draw capital. But if they meet these standards, they can conjure the funds that allow the nation-state to produce itself as what one might call a “miracle nation”: a nation in which foreign funds support the authoritarian rule that keeps the funds safe.
