I have called this “franchise cronyism.” In exchange for supplying the money to support the national leaders who can make the state secure, investors are offered the certainties of the contract, which ensures title to mineral deposits, fixes taxation rates, and permits export of profit.

原页 69

CoW 一直是国家精英的魔法工具。尽管只是纸和墨，它们为印尼民族国家召唤来固定收入。其条款必须按国际标准安全且有吸引力，否则就吸引不到资本。但如果符合这些标准，它们就能召唤资金，使民族国家把自己生产为一个可称为“奇迹国家”的东西：一个由外国资金支持威权统治、而威权统治又保证资金安全的国家。我称之为“特许经营式裙带主义”。作为提供资金支持能够使国家安全的国家领导人的交换，投资者获得合同的确定性，合同确保矿藏所有权、固定税率，并允许将利润汇出境外。

原页 69

The CoW guarantees that investors are not working with “dictators.” As one Canadian Bre-X investor explained to me, in investing his modest funds he always avoided the countries of dictators. This was the reason the Bre-X investment seemed reasonable. I was confused: What is a dictator? As we talked, I realized that a dictator is a foreign ruler who interferes with Canadian investment. Indonesia’s President Suharto was not a dictator, at least before Bre-X. As Bre-X president David Walsh put it, his company—like other Australian and Canadian mining companies in the 1980s and 1990s—targeted Indonesia “by virtue of its geological setting, favorable investment climate and political stability” (Wells 1997c: 42).

原页 69

CoW 保证投资者不是在和“独裁者”合作。正如一位加拿大布雷-X投资者向我解释的，他在投入自己不多的资金时总是避开独裁者国家。这就是布雷-X投资看起来合理的原因。我感到困惑：什么是独裁者？随着我们交谈，我意识到，独裁者是干涉加拿大投资的外国统治者。印尼总统苏哈托不是独裁者，至少在布雷-X之前不是。正如布雷-X总裁戴维·沃尔什所说，他的公司——像20世纪80年代和90年代其他澳大利亚与加拿大矿业公司一样——瞄准印尼是“凭借其地质环境、有利的投资气候和政治稳定”（Wells 1997c: 42）。

原页 70

Other nations could be and were imagined in Indonesia. Suharto’s New Order emerged violently in 1966 from an earlier scene of diverse and competitive programs for making the nation, and from the start the regime depended on the repression of other Indonesian national visions through censorship and militarization. Political quietude was nurtured, too, through internationally sponsored “development,” which came to refer to programs of state expansion dedicated to convincing diverse local people of the unified national standards of state power. Through “development,” the state conceived a legal framework to claim the nation’s resources and make them available for foreign expropriation, thus amassing the materials through which its version of the nation could prosper.

原页 70

在印尼，另一种国家可以被想象，也确实曾被想象。苏哈托的新秩序于1966年从早先建国方案的多样竞争场景中暴力地浮现，从一开始，该政权就依赖通过审查与军事化镇压其他关于印尼国家的愿景。政治寂静也通过国际赞助的“发展”来培育，发展逐渐指国家扩张计划，致力于说服多样的地方人民接受国家权力的统一国家标准。通过“发展”，国家构想出一个法律框架来主张国家的资源，并使其可供外国攫取，从而积聚材料，让它所构想的国家得以繁荣。

原页 70

When investment capital began to circulate wildly across national boundaries in the 1980s, the Indonesian elite was ready for it. They beckoned to the mining sector, saying: “There are still vast tracts of unexplored land in Indonesia. For those who dare to venture, Indonesia offers immense possibilities.”24 The Australians came. One Indonesian ex-mining official candidly admitted that these were “irresponsible investments” with “rubbish technology.” When the Canadian companies followed in the 1990s, it was more of the same: “It’s a repetition of history. It’s not really a gold rush. It’s rather a stock market rush.”25 Yet the government transformed the stock market rush into a gold rush by offering it regional frontiers in the making. The regime gave the companies Contracts of Work, despite their irresponsibility. The CoWs wrote away local rights. Military men deployed to enforce CoWs felt encouraged to start their own entrepreneurial schemes, creating a model of government in which administrators by definition doubled as entrepreneurs who, supported by kickbacks, freed up resources for investors, including themselves. Civil servants became franchise entrepreneurs too, learning to conjure the miracle nation locally. It was they who sanctioned the mass migration of illegal small loggers and miners that kept the regional economy afloat while bigger investors took out bigger resources and profits. In this escalating mobility and lawlessness, the mysteries of the search for buried treasure became possible. Whether there was gold or not, the economy could grow, spurred on by fabulous dreams.

原页 70

当投资资本在20世纪80年代开始疯狂跨越国界流通时，印尼精英已经准备好了。他们向矿业部门招手，说：“印尼仍有大片未勘探的土地。对于敢于冒险的人，印尼提供无限可能。”24澳大利亚人来了。一位印尼前矿业官员坦率承认，这些是“不负责任的投资”，技术是“垃圾”。当加拿大公司在20世纪90年代跟进时，情况大同小异：“这是历史的重复。这不是真正的淘金热。这更像股市热。”25然而政府通过提供正在形成中的区域边疆，把股市热变成了淘金热。政权给公司采矿合同，尽管它们不负责任。CoW 一笔勾销了地方权利。被部署执行 CoW 的军人受到鼓励，开始自己的创业计划，创造了一种政府模式：行政官员按定义兼任企业家，他们在回扣的支持下为投资者——包括他们自己——释放资源。公务员也成了特许经营企业家，学着在地方召唤奇迹国家。正是他们批准非法小伐木者和矿工的大规模迁移，使区域经济得以维持，而更大的投资者取走更大的资源和利润。在这种不断升级的流动性与无法无天中，寻找埋藏宝藏的谜团成为可能。无论有没有黄金，经济都能在神奇梦想的刺激下增长。

原页 70, 71

By the 1990s, the Suharto regime began to take for granted its domestic stability and international support. The work of disguising official kickbacks as sound investment policy seemed already complete. Perhaps this will help to explain how the set performance of the miracle nation could have been allowed to deteriorate into dramatic excess. Drama ultimately embarrassed the Suharto regime, allowing investors to label it corrupt. At the same time, it provided a moment of opportunity for investors, who could maneuver within the new embarrassments of national performance to gain a better position for themselves. No investors did better than Bre-X and its rivals in opening up those dramatic cracks and making them visible on international news screens. However unself-conscious the manipulation, it seems clear that the over-the-top drama of franchise cronyism set off around Bre-X allowed the Bre-X investment bubble to last far longer than it could have otherwise, drawing out the drama from the 1994 announcement of gold to the 1997 death of de Guzman. This drama popularized the Bre-X story, vastly enlarging investment.

原页 70, 71

到20世纪90年代，苏哈托政权开始把其国内稳定与国际支持视为理所当然。把官方回扣伪装成稳健投资政策的工作似乎已经完成。也许这有助于解释，奇迹国家的既定表演怎么会被允许恶化成戏剧性的过度。戏剧最终让苏哈托政权难堪，使投资者可以给它贴上腐败标签。与此同时，它为投资者提供了一个机会时刻，他们可以在国家表演的新尴尬中周旋，为自己谋取更好的位置。在打开这些戏剧性裂缝并使其出现在国际新闻屏幕上方面，没有投资者比布雷-X及其对手做得更好。无论这种操纵多么不自觉，看来很清楚：围绕布雷-X的特许经营式裙带主义的夸张戏剧，使布雷-X投资泡沫维持得比原本可能的长得多，把戏剧从1994年宣布黄金拉长到1997年德·古兹曼之死。这场戏剧使布雷-X故事流行起来，极大扩大了投资。

原页 71

In January 1994 Barrick Gold offered to buy a stake in Bre-X. Barrick was involved in an aggressive campaign of acquisitions in an attempt to become the world’s biggest gold mining company. As mentioned previously, Barrick’s CEO, Peter Munk, was a risk taker who had made his fortune from the lucky purchase of a Nevada mine, which turned out to be a fabulous mother lode. Furthermore, Barrick had targeted Indonesia as a possible site for high-profit, low-cost mining. Bre-X’s Busang was just Barrick’s kind of buy (Goold and Willis 1997: 99-100).

原页 71

1994年1月，巴里克黄金公司提出购买布雷-X的股份。巴里克正在参与一场激进的收购运动，试图成为世界上最大的金矿公司。如前所述，巴里克的首席执行官彼得·芒克是个冒险者，他靠幸运地买下内华达州一座矿山发财，那座矿山结果是一座惊人的主矿脉。此外，巴里克已把印尼定为一个可能进行高利润、低成本采矿的地点。布雷-X的布桑正是巴里克想买的那种（Goold and Willis 1997: 99-100）。

原页 71

When Bre-X turned him down, Barrick moved into the cracks of the Indonesian regime, working the connection between greed and vulnerability that their nation-making performances had themselves produced. The highpowered politicians on Barrick’s advisory board pressured the minister of mines and energy, and even President Suharto.26 Barrick then approached the president’s daughter Tutut, a tycoon in road construction contracts. Barrick offered her Busang’s construction contracts, and she pushed the minister of mines to negotiate a Barrick Bre-X split in which the government would control 10 percent of the mine, Barrick 70 percent, and Bre-X 20 percent. Bre-X was vulnerable because they had begun drilling without a CoW; now the ministry pulled out even their temporary exploration permit to clinch the deal (Wells 1997c).

原页 71

布雷-X拒绝后，巴里克钻进印尼政权的裂缝，利用贪婪与脆弱性之间的联系——这种联系正是印尼的建国表演所制造的。巴里克顾问委员会中的高层政客向矿业与能源部长、甚至苏哈托总统施压。26随后巴里克接触总统女儿图图特，她是一位道路建设合同大亨。巴里克向她许诺布桑的建设合同，她推动矿业部长谈判一项巴里克—布雷-X分割方案：政府控制矿山10%，巴里克70%，布雷-X 20%。布雷-X很脆弱，因为他们在没有 CoW 的情况下就开始钻探；现在矿业部甚至撤销了他们的临时勘探许可，以敲定交易（Wells 1997c）。

原页 71

Bre-X stockholders went wild with anger. In the glare of their dissatisfaction, the drama escalated. Placer Dome, another Canadian company, made a better bid.27 Meanwhile, Bre-X made a spectacular play by approaching the president’s son, Sigit, and offering him 10 percent of the mine plus an eyecatching $1 million per month to push their case. Whether naive, as read at the time, or unimaginably clever, this move took the performance of franchise cronyism to its extreme limits, offering the investment drama a new life. Now Suharto’s children were pitted against each other publicly.

原页 71

布雷-X股东们怒不可遏。在他们不满的强光下，戏剧升级了。另一家加拿大公司普莱瑟穹顶公司（Placer Dome）提出了更好的报价。27与此同时，布雷-X采取了一个惊人的举动，接近总统的儿子西吉特，向他提供矿山10%的股份，外加每月100万美元的醒目报酬，以推动他们的案子。无论当时被解读为天真，还是难以想象的聪明，这一举动把特许经营式裙带主义的表演推到了极致，为投资戏剧赋予了新的生命。现在苏哈托的孩子们被公开地相互对立。

原页 71, 72

Barrick continued to have government support until it gained a new opponent: entrepreneur Bob Hasan, the long-time friend and golfing buddy of the president, and the man who best knew how to mimic foreign investors’ ploys to enlarge his own empire. Hasan played the patriot of the miracle nation, arguing passionately that the enrichment and empowerment of national elites is the first principle of national interest. Barrick irritated him by sending in North American politicians, and he railed against their “cowboyisms,” which made Indonesia look helpless under the American thumb.28 Meanwhile, too, he managed to acquire a 50 percent share in Bre-X’s Indonesian partner.29

原页 71, 72

巴里克一直拥有政府支持，直到它赢得了一个新对手：企业家鲍勃·哈桑，总统的老朋友和高尔夫球友，也是最懂得模仿外国投资者手法以扩大自己帝国的人。哈桑扮演奇迹国家的爱国者，激烈主张，让国家精英致富和掌权是国家利益的第一原则。巴里克派北美政客游说，激怒了他，他痛斥他们的“牛仔作风”，说这让印尼在美国的拇指下显得无助。28与此同时，他还设法获得了布雷-X印尼合作伙伴50%的股份。29

原页 72

The game was almost over when President Suharto asked Bob Hasan to work out a solution for Bre-X, and yet, this too was a moment of momentous drama. Bre-X stockholders were at the edge of their seats. Activist stockholder George Chorny wrote a public letter to Hasan, reminding him that it was Bre-X that discovered the gold. “It’s not any of the guys at Barrick or Placer. It’s not the Indonesian government. All the Indonesian government did was to welcome the people of Bre-X to come into their country with open arms to explore this jungle, this desolate jungle in the middle of nowhere” (Wells 1997b). For Chorny, the frontier is always already empty. But Hasan had a different perspective; making the frontier was a national responsibility. Hasan dismissed both Barrick and Placer Dome and brought in the regime’s favorite company, Freeport McMoRan. In Hasan’s solution, Freeport McMoRan would take 15 percent of the mine and become sole operator; the Indonesian government would take 10 percent; Hasan’s companies would take 30 percent; and the remaining 45 percent would remain with Bre-X. Backed into a corner, Bre-X signed gracefully.30

原页 72

游戏几乎结束了，这时苏哈托总统请鲍勃·哈桑为布雷-X制定一个解决方案，然而，这同样是一个重大戏剧时刻。布雷-X的股东们紧张得屏息以待。维权股东乔治·乔尼写了一封公开信给哈桑，提醒他是布雷-X发现了黄金。“不是巴里克或普莱瑟的任何人。也不是印尼政府。印尼政府所做的，只是张开双臂欢迎布雷-X的人来到他们的国家，探索这片丛林，这片位于荒无人烟之中的荒凉丛林”（Wells 1997b）。对乔尼来说，边疆总是已经空无的。但哈桑有不同的视角；制造边疆是国家的责任。哈桑否决了巴里克和普莱瑟穹顶，引入了政权最喜欢的公司自由港麦克莫兰。在哈桑的方案中，自由港麦克莫兰将获得矿山15%的股份并成为唯一经营者；印尼政府将获得10%；哈桑的公司将获得30%；其余45%留给布雷-X。布雷-X被逼到角落，优雅地签了字。30

原页 72

Freeport, unlike Bre-X and even Barrick, was not in the business of spectacular accumulation, the economy of appearances. Freeport worked with its own cultural logic of investment and development, which, at least at this period, differed from that of Bre-X. Freeport was no mining junior, amassing capital to finance further exploration. Instead, it had established itself as a big, solid outpost of “American civilization” in Indonesia. As CEO Jim Bob Moffett put it, “We are thrusting a spear of economic development into the heartland of Irian Jaya [West Papua]” (Marr 1993: 71). Freeport built residential neighborhoods in West Papua reminiscent of U.S. suburbs; Moffett performed Elvis Presley imitations during Christmas visits. Freeport’s culture of business, then, offered Americanization rather than “frontier discovery” as a model of profitability.

原页 72

自由港与布雷-X甚至巴里克不同，并不从事奇观式积累的生意，即表象经济。自由港按照自己的投资与发展文化逻辑运作，至少在这一时期，这种逻辑不同于布雷-X。自由港不是初级矿业公司，不是聚拢资本来资助进一步勘探。相反，它已确立自己为印尼一个大型、稳固的“美国文明”前哨。正如首席执行官吉姆·鲍勃·莫菲特所说，“我们正向伊里安查亚[西巴布亚]腹地插入一支经济发展的长矛”（Marr 1993: 71）。自由港在西巴布亚建造了让人想起美国郊区的住宅区；莫菲特在圣诞节访问时模仿猫王。因此，自由港的商业文化提供的盈利模式是美国化，而不是“边疆发现”。

原页 72, 73

Freeport had long since gained its miracle deal from the Suharto regime. Its personal Contract of Work far exceeded the benefits of all other investors. In turn, Freeport was the largest source of investor tax revenue for the Indonesian government. It had spent an enormous amount of money developing its Grasberg mine in West Papua, where it depended on the army to keep local residents in line. In 1995, however, riots closed the mine; in 1996, West Papuan tribal leaders sued the company for environmental destruction and human rights abuses, and the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (an agency of the U.S. government) cancelled the company’s risk insurance because of its environmental policies. In 1997, then, Freeport was busy living down international accusations of environmental and social irresponsibility in West Papua. It needed a green profile and solid production results, not an economic miracle.31 In this spirit, Freeport sent in a sober team to assess the gold at Busang. There was nothing there. “It makes me sick every tme I think about it,” said Jim Bob Moffett, Freeport’s CEO (Behar 1997: 128). After a few most impressive last gasps, the spectacle wound down and collapsed. Said Bre-X President David Walsh, “Four and a half years of hard work and the pot at the end of the rainbow is a bucket of slop” (Calgary Sun, October 12, 1997).32

校注15
原页 72, 73

自由港早已从苏哈托政权那里获得其奇迹般的交易。它专属的采矿合同给予的优惠远超其他投资者所得。反过来，自由港是印尼政府最大的投资者税收来源。它花费巨资开发西巴布亚的格拉斯伯格（Grasberg）矿山，在那里，它依靠军队约束当地居民。然而1995年，骚乱使矿山关闭；1996年，西巴布亚部落领袖起诉该公司破坏环境和侵犯人权，海外私人投资公司（美国政府的一个机构）因其环境政策取消了该公司的风险保险。于是1997年，自由港正忙于摆脱国际上对其在西巴布亚的环境和社会不负责任的指控。它需要绿色形象和稳健的生产业绩，而不是经济奇迹。31本着这种精神，自由港派出了一个冷静的团队评估布桑的黄金。那里什么都没有。“每次想到这件事，我都觉得恶心，”自由港首席执行官吉姆·鲍勃·莫菲特说（Behar 1997: 128）。经过几阵最令人印象深刻的最后喘息，奇观逐渐收场并崩溃。布雷-X总裁戴维·沃尔什说：“四年半的辛苦工作，彩虹尽头的大罐不过是一桶泔水”（Calgary Sun, October 12, 1997）。32

校注15
原页 73

On Spectacular Accumulation

原页 73

论奇观式积累

原页 73

What does this story allow us to learn about transnational finance and its globalist aspirations? In the midst of their dramatic roles, the major players usefully remind us of the stage they have laid. Like Bob Hasan, I am struck by the North American character of the dreams and schemes of investment that swirled around Bre-X. With Bre-X stockholders, I marvel at the ability of Indonesian nation makers to usurp an economic process that has been imagined as so independent from national controls. And as for the Kalimantan landscape, it is hard not to mourn: The pot at the end of the rainbow is a bucket of eroding mud, damaged forests, and mercury-poisoned rivers. Slop indeed.

原页 73

这个故事让我们了解到跨国金融及其全球主义抱负的什么？在各自扮演戏剧角色的过程中，主要参与者有益地提醒我们他们铺设的舞台。像鲍勃·哈桑一样，我震惊于围绕布雷-X的投资梦想与计划具有北美特征。与布雷-X股东一样，我惊叹于印尼国家建构者篡夺一个被想象为如此独立于国家控制的经济过程的能力。至于加里曼丹地景，很难不哀悼：彩虹尽头的大罐不过是一桶被侵蚀的泥浆、受损的森林和被汞污染的河流。确实是泔水。

原页 73

It was the Canadian imagination of the combined frontier of investment and mining that made this drama possible. The mining industry has been historically important to Canada’s economy and identity. By the 1980s, its locus had shifted from mining in Canada to mining for Canada. It represented opportunity, initiative, and the potential prosperity in national character. Bre-X’s run from the bottom of the Alberta stock exchange to the top of the ‘Toronto exchange and into the world was a source of pride for many Canadians. As much as for profits, Canadians invested for reasons of national pride.33

原页 73

正是加拿大人对投资与采矿联合边疆的想象使这场戏剧成为可能。采矿业对加拿大的经济和身份认同历来重要。到20世纪80年代，其重心已从在加拿大采矿转向为加拿大采矿。它代表了民族性格中的机会、进取心和潜在繁荣。布雷-X从阿尔伯塔证券交易所的底层一路升至多伦多证券交易所的顶层，再进入世界，是许多加拿大人的骄傲来源。加拿大人投资不仅为了利润，也出于民族自豪感。33

原页 73, 74

Yet the national specificity of attraction to investments disappears in the excitement of commitments to globalism in the financial world. When one thinks about finance in the Bre-X case, there was nothing worldwide about it at all; it was Canadian and U.S. investment in Indonesia. Yet it was easy to assimilate this specific trajectory of investment to an imagined globalism to the extent that the global is defined as the opening-up process in which remote places submit to foreign finance. Every time finance finds a new site of engagement, we think that the world is getting more global. In this act of conjuring, global becomes the process of finding new sites. In the force field of this particular globalism, Canadian national dreams are reimagined as transcendent, circulating, beyond culture.

原页 73, 74

然而，在金融世界对全球主义承诺的兴奋中，吸引投资的国家特殊性消失了。想到布雷-X案例中的金融，它根本没有任何世界性；那是加拿大和美国在印尼的投资。然而，把这一特定的投资轨迹同化为一个想象的全球主义是容易的，只要全球被定义为遥远地方服从外国金融的开放过程。每当金融找到一个新的参与地点，我们就认为世界正变得更加全球。在这种召唤行为中，全球变成了寻找新地点的过程。在这个特定全球主义的力场中，加拿大的民族梦想被重新想象为超越的、流动的、超越文化的。

原页 74

Despite the enormous coercions and seductions of financiers, which aim to make the whole world ready for investment, there is great particularity not only in the reasons a Canadian might want to invest but also in places where he or she can invest. In the 1990s, when the dreams of the Indonesian elite linked with those of Canadians to jointly conjure the promise of gold, Indonesia became one of those places. Images of remote wild places that could make independent-minded Canadians rich and free touched Indonesian visions of a miracle nation, a nation that could come into being in the arms of foreign finance. Flying in the face of financiers’ fantasies of making the nation disappear for the greater mobility of capital, the magic of the miracle nation, waving its CoWs, asserted itself as the only door to North American investment. CoWs, as I have argued, are not merely mechanical adjustments of economic affairs. They are fetish objects, charged with conjuring the miracle nation in the face of competing alternative visions, which unless warded off might come to control the apparatus of the state. From investors’ perspectives, they are charged, too, with the security of profit and property. As a gift, they remake the identities of both giver and receiver, vitalizing the miracle nation and its globalist speculators.

原页 74

尽管金融家有巨大的强制与诱惑，旨在让整个世界准备好投资，但不仅加拿大人可能投资的原因具有很大的特殊性，他或她能够投资的地方也是如此。20世纪90年代，当印尼精英的梦想与加拿大人的梦想连接起来，共同召唤黄金的承诺时，印尼成了这样的地方之一。遥远荒野的形象——能让有独立精神的加拿大人致富和自由——触动了印尼人对奇迹国家的想象，一个可以在外国金融怀抱中诞生的国家。金融家幻想让国家消失以获得资本更大的流动性，奇迹国家的魔法却挥舞着它的 CoW，坚持自己是通往北美投资的唯一大门。正如我所论证的，CoW 不只是对经济事务的机械调整。它们是被崇拜的灵物，被赋予在竞争性替代愿景面前召唤奇迹国家的力量；那些替代愿景如果未被挡开，可能会控制国家机器。从投资者的角度看，它们也被赋予利润与财产的安全保证。作为礼物，它们重塑了给予者和接受者的身份，赋予奇迹国家及其全球主义投机者以生命力。

原页 74

For the aspirations of international investors and national elites to emerge as more than a moment's daydream, however, they must be made tangible on a regional landscape. They must engage people, places, and environments. The anti-local culture of Kalimantan frontier regionalism nurtured and raised up both the miracle nation and Canadian speculation. Here is a truly cosmopolitan scene, where varied dreams are jumbled together, naming and renaming creeks, valleys, routes, and towns. The dreamers jostle, fight bitterly, and patronize each other. As they make their own new places, these too are knocked away. Old residents become aliens as the familiar landscape is transformed by trauma, danger, and the anxiety of the unknown. Here mystery can flourish, and unexpected discoveries can be made. Unimagined riches can be found because the layout of wealth and poverty is unsettled, un-imagined. Impossible promises cannot be ignored. On this landscape, the economy of appearances seems so real that it must be true.

原页 74

然而，要使国际投资者和国家精英的抱负成为超越一时白日梦的东西，它们必须在区域地景上被变得可触可感。它们必须牵涉人民、地方和环境。加里曼丹边疆区域主义的反地方文化滋养并扶植了奇迹国家和加拿大投机。这是一个真正的世界主义场景，各种梦想混杂在一起，为溪流、山谷、路线和城镇命名、重新命名。梦想者们推挤、激烈争斗、互相资助。当他们创造自己的新地方时，这些地方也被撞开。旧居民变成了异类，熟悉的地景被创伤、危险和对未知的焦虑所改变。在这里，神秘可以繁盛，意想不到的发现可以被做出。未被想象的财富可以被找到，因为财富与贫困的布局尚未确定、尚未被想象。不可能的承诺不能被忽视。在这片地景上，表象经济显得如此真实，以至于它必定是真的。

原页 74, 75

When the spectacle passes on, what is left is rubble and mud, the residues of success and failure. People with other stakes and stories will have to pick up the pieces.

···

At the intersection of projects for making globes, nations, and regions, new kinds of economies can emerge. In the Bre-X drama, globalist commitments to opening up fresh sites for Canadian mining investments enabled Indonesian visions of a miracle nation at the same time as they stimulated the search for mining frontiers. The program of the miracle nation offered speculators security as it also forced potential frontier regions into lawless violence and abolished customary tenure. When Kalimantan responded by developing a wild frontier, its regional reformation confirmed the proprietary rights of the miracle nation. The Kalimantan frontier could then appeal to globalist speculation, offering a landscape where both discovery and loss were possible. Three scale-making projects came into conjunction here: the globemaking aspirations of finance capital; the nation-making coercions of franchise cronyism; and the region-making claims of frontier culture (see fig. 1). Globalist, nationalist, and regionalist dreams linked to enunciate a distinctive economic program, the program of spectacular accumulation.

原页 74, 75

当奇观过去，剩下的是瓦砾和泥浆，是成功与失败的残渣。拥有其他利害关系和故事的人们将不得不收拾残局。

···

在建构全球、国家和区域的项目交汇处，新型经济可以出现。在布雷-X戏剧中，全球主义者为加拿大采矿投资开辟新地点的承诺，既使印尼人对奇迹国家的想象成为可能，也刺激了对采矿边疆的寻找。奇迹国家的纲领为投机者提供安全，同时也迫使潜在的边疆区域陷入无法无天的暴力，并废除了习惯土地保有制。当加里曼丹以发展一个狂野边疆作为回应时，其区域重塑确认了奇迹国家的专有权利。加里曼丹边疆于是可以吸引全球主义投机，提供一片发现与损失皆有可能的地景。三个尺度制造项目在此汇合：金融资本的全球制造抱负；特许经营式裙带主义的国家建构的强制力量；以及边疆文化的区域制造主张（见图1）。全球主义者、民族主义者和区域主义者的梦想连接起来，阐明了一个独特的经济纲领，即奇观式积累的纲领。

原页 75

Spectacular accumulation occurs when investors speculate on a product that may or may not exist. Investors are looking for the appearance of success. They cannot afford to find out if the product is solid; by then their chances for profit will be gone. To invest in software development requires this kind of leap: Software developers sell their potential, not their product. Biotechnology requires a related if distinctive leap of faith to trust the processes of innovation and patenting to yield as-yet-unknown property rights and royalties. Real estate development requires an assessment of desirability and growth, not demonstrated occupancy; it sells investors attractiveness. In each of these cases, economic performance is conjured dramatically.34

I use the term spectacular accumulation mainly to argue with evolutionary assumptions in popular theories of the ever-changing world economy. According to regulation theorists, “flexible accumulation” is the latest stage of capitalism. Flexible accumulation follows Fordist production as barbarism follows savagery, that is, up a singular political-economic ladder. David Harvey’s writing (1989) has made this conceptualization influential among anthropologists, who suggest correlated changes in culture, spatiality, and scale to go along with this evolutionary progression. Thus, too, scholars imagine evolutionary changes in the making of space and time. Theories of globalization have us imagine a worldwide condensation of space and time in which spaces grow smaller and times more instantaneous and effortless. Consider, however, the space-time requirements of Bre-X’s spectacular accumulation: Space is hugely enlarged; far from miniature and easy, it becomes expansive, labored, and wild, spreading muddy, malarial frontiers.

原页 75

当投资者投机于一种可能存在也可能不存在的产品时，奇观式积累就发生了。投资者寻找的是成功的表象。他们等不起产品是否可靠得到查明：到那时，他们的获利机会就没了。投资软件开发需要这种飞跃：软件开发者出售的是潜力，不是产品。生物技术也需要一种相关但独特的信念飞跃，相信创新和专利程序能产生尚不为人知的产权和版税。房地产开发需要评估吸引力和增长，而不是已证明的入住率；它向投资者出售的是吸引力。在每一种情况下，经济表现都是通过戏剧性方式召唤出来的。34

我使用“奇观式积累”一词，主要是为了与流行理论中关于不断变化的世界经济的演化论假设争辩。根据规制理论家，“灵活积累”是资本主义的最新阶段。灵活积累紧随福特制生产，就像野蛮紧随蒙昧，也就是说，沿着单一政治经济阶梯向上爬。大卫·哈维的著作（1989）使这一概念化在人类学家中具有影响力，他们提出文化、空间性和尺度上与之相应的变化，以配合这一演化进程。学者们也因此想象空间与时间制造中的演化变化。全球化理论让我们想象一种世界性的时空压缩，空间变小，时间更瞬时、更不费力。然而，考虑一下布雷-X奇观式积累的时空要求：空间被巨大地放大了；远非微型而轻松，它变得广阔、费力而狂野，蔓延着泥泞的、疟疾横行的边疆。

原页 76

Time is quickened but into the rush of acceleration, not the efficiency of quick transfers. It is not effortless; if you can’t feel the rush and the intensity, you are missing the point, and you’ll keep your money at home. Moreover, this spectacular accumulation does not call out to be imagined as new. It is self-consciously old, drawing us back to the South Sea bubble and every gold rush in history. In contrast with flexible accumulation, its power is not its rejection of the past, but its ability to keep this old legacy untarnished.

原页 76

时间被加速，但加速成冲刺，而不是快速转移的效率。它并非不费力；如果你感受不到冲刺和强度，你就没抓住要点，就会把钱留在家里。此外，这种奇观式积累并不呼唤被想象为新事物。它自觉是老派的，把我们带回南海泡沫和历史上每一次淘金热。与灵活积累形成对比的是，它的力量不在于拒绝过去，而在于让这份古老的遗产保持不褪色。

原页 76, 77

This is more than yet another classificatory device in the annals of capitalism. My point is to show the heterogeneity of capitalism at every moment in time. Capitalist forms and processes are continually made and unmade; if we offer singular predictions we allow ourselves to be caught by them as ideologies. This seems especially pressing in considering the analysis of scale. Since the 1990s, every ambitious world-making project has wanted to show itself able to forge new scales. Nongovernmental organizations, ethnic groups and coalitions, initiatives for human rights and social justice: We all want to be creative and self-conscious about our scale-making. We want to claim the globe as ours. In this context, rather than ally myself with globalist financiers to tell of their globe, I trace how that globe comes into being both as a culturally specific set of commitments and as a set of practices. The investment drama of the Bre-X story shows how articulations among globalist, nationalist, and regionalist projects bring each project to life. In the spirit of serious but joking diagrams, I offer an acronym to refocus your attention (fig. 2). The particularity of globalist projects, I am arguing, is best seen in the contingent articulations that make them possible and bring them to life: These are “aphids,” Articulations among Partially Hegemonic Imagined Different Scales.

Often we turn to capitalism to understand how what seem to be surface developments form part of an underlying pattern of exploitation and class formation. Yet before we succumb to the capitalist monolith called up in these analyses, it is useful to look at the continual emergence of new capitalist niches, cultures, and forms of agency. For this task, Stuart Hall’s idea about the role of articulation in the formation of new political subjects is helpful (1996). New political subjects form, he argues, as pre-existing groups link and, through linking, enunciate new identities and interests. Social processes and categories also can develop in this way. I have used this insight to trace the spectacular accumulation brought into being by the articulation of finance capital, franchise cronyism, and frontier culture. While each of these linked projects achieved only a moment of partial hegemony, this was also a moment of dramatic success.

原页 76, 77

这不仅仅是资本主义编年史中的又一个分类工具。我的要点是展示资本主义在每个时刻的异质性。资本主义的形式和过程不断被制造和拆解；如果我们提供单一预测，就等于让自己被它们作为意识形态所捕获。考虑到尺度分析，这一点似乎尤其紧迫。自20世纪90年代以来，每一个雄心勃勃的造世项目都想表明自己能够锻造新的尺度。非政府组织、族群和联盟、人权与社会正义倡议：我们都想对自己的尺度制造富有创造性和自觉。我们都想宣称地球是我们的。在这种背景下，我并未与全球主义金融家结盟来讲述他们的地球，而是追踪那个地球如何作为一组文化特定的承诺、也作为一组实践而生成。布雷-X故事的投资戏剧展示了全球主义者、民族主义者和区域主义者项目之间的接合如何使每个项目活起来。本着严肃但开玩笑的图表精神，我提供一个首字母缩略词来重新聚焦你的注意力（图2）。我要论证的是，全球主义项目的特殊性最好在使它们成为可能并赋予其生命的偶然接合中来看：这就是“蚜虫”（APHIDS），即部分霸权的想象的不同尺度之间的接合（Articulations among Partially Hegemonic Imagined Different Scales）。

我们常常转向资本主义，以理解看似表面的发展如何构成剥削与阶级形成的深层模式的一部分。然而，在我们屈服于这些分析所召唤的资本主义巨石之前，看看新资本主义生态位、文化和能动性形式的持续涌现是有用的。为此，斯图尔特·霍尔关于接合在新政治主体形成中作用的想法是有帮助的（1996）。他认为，新的政治主体在既有群体连接、并通过连接阐明新的身份与利益时形成。社会过程和范畴也可以以这种方式发展。我用这一洞见追踪由金融资本、特许经营式裙带主义和边疆文化接合所产生的奇观式积累。虽然这些相互连接的项目中的每一个都只获得了部分霸权的时刻，但这同样是一个戏剧性成功的时刻。

原页 77

Soon after the story I have told, Indonesia precipitously collapsed as a celebrated site for investment; the miracle nation was discredited, and the articulation fell apart. Afterward, analysts scrambled to tell the difference between good and bad investments. They recognized that the Busang saga had contributed in a small way to the Indonesian crash. But they ignored or refused its allegorical quality: Bre-X offered a dramatic rendition of the promises and perils of the economic miracle attributed, in Indonesia and beyond, to globalization.35

原页 77

在我讲述的故事之后不久，印尼作为投资热土急剧崩溃；奇迹国家名誉扫地，接合解体了。此后，分析家们争先恐后地分辨好投资与坏投资。他们承认布桑传奇在很小程度上促成了印尼的崩溃。但他们忽视或拒绝其寓言性质：布雷-X戏剧性地呈现了在印尼及其他地方被归因于全球化的经济奇迹的承诺与危险。35

原页 77

How might scholars take on the challenge of freeing critical imaginations from the specter of neoliberal conquest—singular, universal, global? Attention to the frictions of contingent articulation can help us describe the effectiveness, and the fragility, of emergent capitalist—and globalist—forms. In this shifting heterogeneity there are new sources of hope, and, of course, new nightmares.

原页 77

学者们如何迎接挑战，把批判性想象力从新自由主义征服的幽灵——单一的、普遍的、全球的——中解放出来？关注偶然接合的摩擦可以帮助我们描述新兴资本主义——以及全球主义——形式的效果与脆弱性。在这种不断变化的异质性中，有新的希望来源，当然也有新的噩梦。

第二部　知识

全球视野，1955年

原书分部扉页展示1955年亚非会议纪念邮票，图中人群放飞鸽子，鸽子飞向地球；本版未复制邮票图像。

“Let a new Asia and a new Africa be born”

原页 81

原页 81

[Global vision]

原页 81

原页 81

Stories of the Enlightenment often pair knowledge and vision, in two senses: the privileging of the sense of sight, and the importance of planning. Vision has energized knowledge of the globe by condensing it in a friendly visual icon and normalizing its futurist aspirations. Yet global imagery is contested and tentative. Knowledge that travels today is haunted by the disappointments of past visions. Haunting disturbs our reliance on vision. Double vision gives us a headache, reminding us of our frailty. Authoritative knowledge is forced to shore up its boundaries. “Experts” are those who have trained themselves to see with a singular vision. In contrast, the public is troubled by haunting. Only by excluding the public can knowledge be kept pure.

原页 81

启蒙运动的故事常常把知识与视野（vision）相联系，其中包含两层意思：视觉感官的优先地位，以及规划愿景的重要性。视野把关于全球的知识凝聚成一个易于亲近的视觉符号，并使其面向未来的抱负显得理所当然，从而赋予这种知识以活力。然而，全球意象始终受到争议，尚未定型。今天流传的知识仍被过去愿景落空的幽影萦绕。这些幽影扰乱了我们对视野的依赖。重影让我们头痛，提醒我们自身的脆弱。权威知识被迫巩固其边界。“专家”是那些训练自己以单一视野观看的人。相比之下，公众仍受幽影困扰。只有将公众排除在外，知识才能保持纯净。

原页 81

None of this means that any knowledge is as good as any other. Continued life on earth depends on getting our knowledge into as good a shape as possible. But this can mean paying more rather than less attention to the multiplicity of knowledge claims. Both global knowledge and knowledge that travels around the globe are improved by dialogue across difference. Hauntings sometimes open the way to such dialogue: What visions have we been formed by, yet forgotten? What visions have we let shrivel, fester, or fall away?

原页 81

这并不意味着任何知识都和其他知识一样好。地球上的持续生命取决于把我们的知识塑造得尽可能好。但这可能意味着更多而非更少地关注知识主张的多样性。全球知识以及围绕全球旅行的知识，都通过跨越差异的对话而得到改善。萦绕有时为这种对话开辟道路：我们曾被哪些愿景塑造，却又将其遗忘？我们让哪些愿景枯萎、溃烂或消逝了？

原页 81

1955. On April 18, in the town of Bandung, Indonesia’s first president welcomed delegates from across Asia and Africa to what promised to be a momentous occasion: the Asia~Africa Conference. The theme of the president’s opening remarks (“Let a new Asia and a new Africa be born”) was freedom. Freedom was spreading across the globe.

原页 81

1955年。4月18日，在印尼的万隆镇，印尼首任总统欢迎来自亚洲和非洲的代表，参加一场有望意义重大的盛会：亚非会议。总统开场发言的主题（“让新的亚洲和新的非洲诞生”）是自由。自由正在全球蔓延。

原页 81, 82

Sisters and Brothers, how terrifically dynamic is our time! I recall that, several years ago, I had occasion to make a public analysis of colonialism, and that I then drew attention to what I called the “lifeline of imperialism.” This line runs from the Straits of Gibraltar, through the Mediterranean, the Suez Canal, the Red Sea, the Indian Ocean, the South China Sea and the Sea of Japan. For most of that enormous distance, the territories on both sides of this lifeline were colonies, the peoples were unfree, their futures mortgaged to an alien system. Along that lifeline, that main artery of imperialism, there was pumped the life-blood of colonialism.

原页 81, 82

兄弟姐妹们，我们的时代是多么充满活力啊！我记得，几年前，我曾有机会对殖民主义作一次公开分析，当时我提请注意我所谓的“帝国主义的生命线”。这条线从直布罗陀海峡出发，穿过地中海、苏伊士运河、红海、印度洋、南中国海和日本海。在这条漫长距离的大部分地方，生命线两侧的领土都是殖民地，人民不自由，他们的未来被抵押给一个异己的制度。沿着这条生命线，这条帝国主义的主动脉，泵送着殖民主义的生命之血。

原页 82

And today in this hall are gathered together the leaders of those same people. They are no longer the victims of colonialism. They are no longer the tools and playthings of forces they cannot influence. Today, you are representatives of free peoples, peoples [of] a different stature and standing in the world. (Sukarno 1983: 5)

而今天，正是这些人民的领袖们聚集在这个大厅里。他们不再是殖民主义的受害者。他们不再是那些自己无力影响的势力的工具和玩物。今天，你们是自由人民的代表，是在世界上具有不同地位与身份的人民。（Sukarno 1983: 5）

Yet the echoing U.S. voice was also known for its menace. The atom bomb had been unleashed, and the escalating Cold War threatened the very existence of the world. 原页 82, 83

[I]t has been made clear that the weapons of ultimate horror will certainly be used.... No task is more urgent that that of preserving peace” (1983: 8).

What can we do? We can do much! We can inject the voice of reason into world affairs. We can mobilize all the spiritual, all the moral, all the political strength of Asia and Africa on the side of peace. Yes, we! We, the peoples of Asia and Africa, 1,400,000,000 strong, far more than half the human population of the world, we can mobilize what I have called the Moral Violence of Nations in favor of peace. We can demonstrate to the minority of the world which lives on the other continents that we, the majority, are for peace, not war, and that whatever strength we have will always be thrown on to the side of peace. (1983: 8).

Thus opened what would become known as the Third World, here imagined as a nonaligned block of emerging nations whose united presence could stop the Cold War. Their unity would define them as a global force. Their freedom would sponsor global peace. Peace and freedom would work together to remake the globe.

然而，那回响的美国声音也以其威胁而闻名。原子弹已被释放，不断升级的冷战威胁着世界的存在本身。正如苏加诺所解释的：“战争不仅意味着对我们独立的威胁，还可能意味着文明的终结，甚至人类生命的终结。世界上有一种力量在游荡，无人真正知道它的邪恶[潜力]……

我们能做什么？我们能做很多！我们可以把理性的声音注入世界事务。我们可以动员亚洲和非洲一切精神的、道德的、政治的力量站在和平一边。是的，我们！我们，亚洲和非洲的人民，14亿之众，远远超过世界人口的一半，我们可以动员我所谓的各国的道德暴力来支持和平。我们可以向生活在其他大陆的少数人证明，我们这些多数人支持和平，而不是战争，我们拥有的一切力量将永远投向和平一边。（1983: 8）

第三世界由此开场，在这里被想象为一个由新兴国家组成的不结盟集团，其团结的存在可以阻止冷战。它们的团结将使它们成为一股全球力量。它们的自由将促进全球和平。和平与自由将共同重塑地球。

The guest list at Bandung was a roll call of the celebrities of post-World War II nationalism. Besides Indonesia’s leaders, the sponsors were India’s Jawaharlal Nehru, Burma’s U Nu, Pakistan’s Mohammed Ali, and Ceylon’s Sir John Kotelawala. Gamal Abdel Nasser represented Egypt; Chou En-lai represented China; Prince Sihanouk represented Cambodia; Kwame Nkrumah sent his deputy from the Gold Coast. Ministers from Afghanistan, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Syria, Turkey, and Yemen came from the Middle East. Leaders still working for independence came from sub-Saharan Africa. Two delegations represented Vietnam, North and South. In a gesture of solidarity, novelist Richard Wright and U.S. Congressman Adam Clayton Powell came as “unofficial delegates” representing African Americans. Racism was an important conference topic. As Sukarno put it, “This is the first intercontinental conference of colored peoples in the history of mankind” (1983: 3).

原页 83

万隆的宾客名单是二战后民族主义名人的点名。除了印尼领导人，发起者还有印度的贾瓦哈拉尔·尼赫鲁、缅甸的吴努、巴基斯坦的穆罕默德·阿里和锡兰的约翰·科特拉瓦拉爵士。贾迈勒·阿卜杜勒·纳赛尔代表埃及；周恩来代表中国；西哈努克亲王代表柬埔寨；夸梅·恩克鲁玛从黄金海岸派来了副手。来自中东的有阿富汗、伊朗、伊拉克、约旦、黎巴嫩、利比亚、沙特阿拉伯、苏丹、叙利亚、土耳其和也门的部长们。仍在为独立而战的领导人来自撒哈拉以南非洲。两个代表团代表越南，南北各一。作为团结的姿态，小说家理查德·赖特和美国国会议员亚当·克莱顿·鲍威尔作为代表非裔美国人的“非官方代表”前来。种族主义是会议的重要议题。正如苏加诺所说，“这是人类历史上第一次有色人种的洲际会议”（1983: 3）。

原页 83

In Bandung, national sovereignty seemed full of promise. Colonialism was on its way out; freedom was sweeping the globe. Unity among the emerging nations could be a new source of political power, thwarting racism and nuclear war. Solidarity could make peace possible, and peace could guarantee freedom. How many times the world has turned since then! How few today remember the meeting in Bandung.

原页 83

在万隆，国家主权似乎充满希望。殖民主义正在退场；自由正席卷全球。新兴国家之间的团结可以成为政治权力的新来源，挫败种族主义和核战争。团结可以使和平成为可能，和平可以保证自由。从那以后，世界转了多少圈！今天还有多少人记得万隆会议。

···
原页 83, 84

In April 2000, I visited the Museum of the Asia-Africa Conference in Bandung with an international group of scholars. The museum itself is a New Order creation, inaugurated in 1980. It trains our eyes with a “conference hall in miniature” exhibit, reducing the conference’s success to its pomp and discipline. It is careful to excise President Sukarno, who was deposed by the New Order, from too much praise. Yet the mythic world of post-World War II nationalism rushes upon us as soon as we see the black-and-white photographs of the delegates. Nasser, Nehru, U Nu: the names themselves resound with the promise of post-colonial development, ‘Third World nations on the move. How young they look—as beautiful as movie stars—how full of optimism and hope! How possible it still seemed that the nations over which these young men had come to preside would overcome colonial legacies to build new worlds of freedom and opportunity. For a moment we can taste the promise that the clasped hands of rising Third World leaders offered. A map of the world, covered with radiating lines, fills one wall: the connections among developing nations will cover the earth.

原页 83, 84

2000年4月，我和一个国际学者团体参观了万隆的亚非会议博物馆。博物馆本身是新秩序的产物，于1980年落成。它用“微型会议厅”展品训练我们的眼睛，把会议的成功简化为其盛况和纪律。它小心翼翼地避免过多赞扬被新秩序废黜的苏加诺总统。然而，一看到代表们的黑白照片，二战后民族主义的神话世界便扑面而来。纳赛尔、尼赫鲁、吴努：这些名字本身就回响着后殖民发展的承诺，行进中的第三世界国家。他们看起来多么年轻——像电影明星一样美丽——多么充满乐观与希望！这些年轻人已经开始领导的国家，似乎仍很有可能克服殖民遗产，建设自由与机会的新世界。有那么一刻，我们能尝到崛起的第三世界领导人紧握双手所提供的那种承诺。一面墙上挂满一张展开辐射线的世界地图：发展中国家之间的联系将覆盖地球。

原页 84

Meanwhile, we peer at dusty typewriters and telex machines in glass cases: these are the machines that ran the conference. How old and obsolete they seem. This dream of a rising Third World has not lasted. Instead of unity blocking the Cold War, the Cold War blocked the unity of nonaligned nations. Radical nationalists were deposed and murdered; the Cold War was exported to countries across the world. Militaries and development budgets took over. Nationalism lost its promise, as imperially mandated authoritar- ‘an rule came to define the Third World. As the future has shifted, the past contorts, confused. In one cabinet featuring conference pamphlets, the curators have included an engineering report on an airplane crash in another city. No explanation is offered.

原页 84

与此同时，我们凝视玻璃柜里满是灰尘的打字机和电传机：这些是运转会议的机器。它们看起来多么古老、多么过时。这个崛起的第三世界的梦想没有持续。团结没有阻止冷战，冷战反而阻止了不结盟国家的团结。激进的民族主义者被废黜和谋杀；冷战被出口到世界各国。军队和发展预算接管了。民族主义失去了它的承诺，帝国强加的威权统治逐渐定义了第三世界。随着未来的移动，过去扭曲、混乱。在一个陈列会议小册子的柜子里，策展人放入了一份关于另一座城市飞机失事的工程报告。没有任何解释。

原页 84

This past is ours, but through a glass, mythical, and dusty.

原页 84

这个过去是我们的，但隔着玻璃，神话般的，满是灰尘。

原页 84

In 1955, the Bandung conference was commemorated on an Indonesian postage stamp, an enlarged version of which adorns the museum wall. On the lower right side, Asians and Africans raise their hands to release scores of doves. The doves are flying to a great, round, moonlike rising globe, which forms the focus of attention of the crowd. This globe is the earth, illustrated with its Asian and African countries in prominent view.

原页 84

1955年，万隆会议被印在印尼邮票上，其放大版装饰着博物馆墙壁。在右下角，亚洲人和非洲人举起双手，放出数十只鸽子。鸽子飞向一个巨大、圆形、月亮般升起的地球，地球成为人群关注的焦点。这个球体就是地球，其中的亚洲和非洲国家处于显著位置。

原页 84

This is not the globe whose image we naturalize in the twenty-first century. The space shots of the fragile blue-green orb, wrapped in clouds, had not yet been produced. This is still a globe of international maps. Most strikingly, the people are not standing on it. They face it with admiration and hope; they send doves to it. It shines on them, offering them light, but it does not appear to trap them in its vulnerabilities and disciplines.

原页 84

这不是我们在21世纪习以为常的地球形象。那些呈现云层包裹着脆弱蓝绿色球体的太空照片尚未问世。这仍然是一张国际地图的地球。最引人注目的是，人们并不站在它上面。他们带着钦佩和希望面对它；他们把鸽子送向它。它照耀他们，给他们光，但似乎并没有把他们困在它的脆弱与规训中。

原页 84, 85

In Bandung, the globe was a symbol of what might be possible: national sovereignty and world peace. This global dream space was made possible by other mid-twentieth century uses of the globe, for example in the United Nations. The bridge to this dream space was that of universal truths, such as science, modernization, and political freedom. This was a time when science seemed more than a neutral set of truths. Science was the antidote to ignorant racial stereotypes and misguided imperial impositions. International cooperation among scientists formed a model for coexistence and respect. Similarly, modernization and development might allow each nation to fulfill its dreams while entering cooperative arrangements with others. Human rights might form a peace-loving common language. The doves set off in the Bandung commemorative stamp are universal truths, which forge a bridge to the dream space of global peace and freedom.

原页 84, 85

在万隆，地球是可能之物的象征：国家主权与世界和平。这个全球梦想空间之所以可能，是因为20世纪中叶地球的其他用途，例如在联合国。通往这个梦想空间的桥梁是普遍真理，如科学、现代化和政治自由。这是一个科学似乎不仅仅是中立真理集合的时代。科学是对无知种族刻板印象和错误帝国强加的解药。科学家之间的国际合作形成了共存与尊重的典范。同样，现代化和发展可能让每个国家在实现梦想的同时，与他国进入合作安排。人权可能形成一种爱好和平的共同语言。万隆纪念邮票上放出的鸽子是普遍真理，它们架起通往全球和平与自由梦想空间的桥梁。

原页 85

When we consider the importance of the Bandung dream of peace and freedom, the inadequacy of the bridge seems hardly a good enough reason to have abandoned the quest.

原页 85

当我们考虑万隆和平与自由梦想的重要性时，这座桥梁的不足似乎不足以成为放弃追求的理由。

···
原页 85

The universal bridge to a global dream space still beckons to us. The bridge might take us out of our imagined isolation into a space of unity and transcendence: the whole world. We find ourselves like a man looking out from his parochial island toward the vast but hazy world of the mainland. The bridge of universal truths promises to take us there. Yet we walk across that bridge, and we find ourselves, not everywhere, but somewhere in particular. Even if our bridge aims toward the most lofty universal truths—the insights of science, the freedom of individual rights, the possibility of wealth for all—we find ourselves hemmed in by the specificity of rules and practices, with their petty prejudices, unreasonable hierarchies, and cruel exclusions. We must make do, enmeshing our desires in the compromise of practical action. We become hardened, or, alternatively, we are overcome with grief and anger. The bridge we stepped off is not the bridge we stepped upon. Yet to cast away the memory of the first bridge denies desire. ‘To pretend it is the same as the second bridge is the baldest lie of power. It is only in maintaining the friction between the two subjectively experienced bridges, the friction between aspiration and practical achievement, that a critical analysis of global connection is possible.

原页 85

通往全球梦想空间的普遍桥梁仍在召唤我们。这座桥可能带我们走出想象的孤立，进入团结与超越的空间：整个世界。我们发现自己像一个从狭隘岛屿望向辽阔却朦胧的大陆世界的人。普遍真理之桥承诺带我们到那里。然而我们走过那座桥，却发现自己并非无处不在，而是在某个特定的地方。即使我们的桥指向最崇高的普遍真理——科学的洞见、个人权利的自由、所有人致富的可能性——我们仍被规则与实践的特殊性所围困，连同它们的小气偏见、不合理的等级制度和残酷的排斥。我们必须将就，把我们的欲望缠入实际行动的妥协。我们变得强硬，或者反过来，被悲伤和愤怒压倒。我们走下的桥不是我们走上的桥。然而，抛弃第一座桥的记忆就是否认欲望。假装它与第二座桥相同，是权力最赤裸的谎言。只有保持两座主观体验之桥之间的摩擦，即抱负与实际成就之间的摩擦，对全球联结的批判性分析才有可能。

原页 85

Science, modernization, and freedom were simultaneously dream bridges for the development of Third World nations and real-life programs within the contingencies of Cold War politics, elite power grabs, authoritarian regimes, religious wars, ecological disasters, and bureaucracies of expertise. Their ability to mobilize national support and their failure to deliver on their promises are intermeshed in these histories.

原页 85

科学、现代化和自由既是第三世界国家发展的梦想桥梁，也是冷战政治、精英夺权、威权政权、宗教战争、生态灾难和专家官僚制等偶然性中的现实生活纲领。它们动员国家支持的能力与未能兑现承诺，在这些历史中相互交织。

···
原页 85, 86

Since the mid-twentieth century, the global dream space has been kicked around like a football claimed first by one team and then another. Environmentalists have wanted it badly, but so have human rights activists, religious sects, and marketers. In the 1990s, corporate public relations took hold of the image of the globe and carried it away. “Globalization” came to mean corporate consolidation, the standardization of world markets, and the deference of national governments to transnational business demands. This global dream space also required a bridge of universal truths, involving neoliberal economic principles and the standardization of property law. Yet even the urgent stridency with which such standards were imposed could not keep other versions of truth from having their say. By the turn of the century, “antiglobalization” politics had begun to gel. The confrontation between demonstrators and police guarding the deliberations of the World Trade Organization in Seattle in 1999 opened a new era of globe-making politics.2 The motley demonstrators—like the national representatives at Bandung—hoped that the force of their unity might form a block against dangerous giants.

原页 85, 86

自20世纪中叶以来，全球梦想空间像足球一样被踢来踢去，先被一支球队宣称，然后被另一支。环保主义者非常想要它，但人权活动家、宗教派别和营销人员也是如此。20世纪90年代，企业公共关系抓住了地球形象并将其带走。“全球化”逐渐意味着企业整合、世界市场的标准化，以及各国政府对跨国商业要求的服从。这个全球梦想空间也需要一座普遍真理的桥梁，涉及新自由主义经济原则和财产法的标准化。然而，即使这些标准被强加时的紧迫尖锐，也无法阻止其他版本的真理发声。到世纪之交，“反全球化”政治开始成形。1999年，示威者与守卫世界贸易组织西雅图会议的警察之间的对抗，开启了一个全球制造政治的新时代。2形形色色的示威者——像万隆的国家代表一样——希望他们团结的力量可以形成一个阻挡危险巨人的集团。

原页 86

Seattle and Bandung could not be more different. Anarchists and children dressed as turtles in the street, versus negotiating heads of state. Police fomenting riot versus police on display. The refusal of the hegemony of nation-states, versus the proud assertion of nation-state autonomy. The critique of development, versus the endorsement of rights to develop. In Seattle, official representatives of Third World nations were notorious for refusing to discuss labor standards: Too many accepted that their power as nations now rested on their ability to offer the cheapest labor and the worst working conditions.

原页 86

西雅图和万隆再不同不过了。一边是街上的无政府主义者和装扮成乌龟的儿童，另一边是参加谈判的国家元首；一边是煽动骚乱的警察，另一边是列队展示的警察；一边拒绝民族国家的霸权，另一边自豪地主张民族国家的自主；一边批判发展，另一边肯定发展权。在西雅图，第三世界国家的官方代表以拒绝讨论劳工标准而臭名昭著：太多人接受，他们作为国家的权力如今取决于提供最廉价劳动力和最恶劣工作条件的能力。

原页 86

Yet both Bandung and Seattle were sites for reclaiming the dream space of the globe. Both offered a bridge of doves to make the dream of a livable globe real. The globe, however, was not the same. In Seattle, the globe could not be projected as a sphere of hope. No one would argue that the world’s problems were caused by a lack of global unity. Instead, demonstrators argued that corporate giants had seized the globe; it was up to transnational activists to take it back. The globe could not be imagined rising hopefully like the full moon; it presented itself as already divided between the discipline of military and machines, on the one hand, and the hopes of resistors, on the other.

原页 86

然而，万隆和西雅图都是夺回全球梦想空间的场所。两者都提供了一座鸽子的桥梁，使可居住地球的梦想成真。然而，这个地球并不相同。在西雅图，地球无法被投射为希望的球体。没有人会论证说，世界的问题源于缺乏全球统一。相反，示威者论证说，企业巨头攫取了地球；跨国活动家有责任把它夺回来。地球无法像满月一样充满希望地升起；它已经呈现为分裂的：一边是军事和机器的纪律，另一边是抵抗者的希望。

原页 86

The universal truths that might form a bridge to global dreams were also contested in Seattle. The momentary unity among labor activists, environmentalists, anarchists, and anti-imperialists did not disguise the lack of common principles that guided their critical assaults. Is the destruction of property a progressive or a destructive strategy? Is the problem for labor refractory countries such as China, or power-hungry ones such as the United States? Would environmental management be improved or worsened by placing its concerns integrally inside free trade? Is Christian prayer a good basis for cosmopolitan solidarity? Each position can be argued with a universal truth, but with different results.

原页 86

可能构成通往全球梦想之桥的普遍真理，在西雅图也受到争夺。劳工活动家、环保主义者、无政府主义者和反帝国主义者之间短暂的团结，并未掩盖指导他们批判性攻击的共同原则的缺失。毁坏财产是进步策略还是破坏策略？对劳工而言，问题在于中国等难以驾驭的国家，还是美国等渴求权力的国家？把环境关切整体置于自由贸易内部，会改善还是恶化环境管理？基督教祈祷是世界主义团结的良好基础吗？每一种立场都可以用普遍真理来论证，但结果不同。

原页 86, 87

These disagreements are not a reason to give up on anti-globalization politics; they are what make it lively. However, they require a new kind of attention to universal truths, our bridges to global dreams. The principles of justice are multiple and contested: Those who feel the effects of injustice continually stretch the categories through which justice is understood. The play among multiple, contested universals can be described as one kind of friction. Knowledge of the globe, and globally traveling knowledge, depend on this friction.

原页 86, 87

这类分歧不是放弃反全球化政治的理由；它们正是使这种政治活跃的原因。然而，它们要求对普遍真理——我们通往全球梦想的桥梁——给予一种新的关注。正义原则是多元且受争夺的：感受到不义后果的人不断延伸理解正义的范畴。多种彼此争议的普遍性之间的相互作用，可以被描述为一种摩擦。关于地球的知识，以及在各地旅行的知识，都依赖于这种摩擦。

原页 88

Natural Universals and the Global Scale

原页 88

自然普遍性与全球尺度

原页 88
To see a World in a Grain of Sand
And a Heaven in a Wild Flower,
Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand
And Eternity in an hour.
—from William Blake, “Auguries of Innocence”
原页 88
从一粒沙中看见一个世界，
从一朵野花中看见一个天堂，
把无限握在你的掌心，
把永恒握在一小时中。
——选自威廉·布莱克《纯真的预言》（“Auguries of Innocence”）
原页 88

Generalization. The action or process of generalizing, i.e. of forming, and expressing in words, general notions or propositions obtained from the observation and comparison of individual facts or appearances; also, an instance of this.1

原页 88

概括（Generalization）：概括的行动或过程，即从对个别事实或现象的观察与比较中形成并用词语表达一般概念或命题；也指这一过程的一个实例。1

原页 88

Many things are said to be universal: freedom, money, love. But the two most historically successful universal claims—which continue to form exemplars for all universality—are still God and Nature. The universality of God and the universality of Nature are historically connected; in the European Renaissance, the stirrings of modern science conceived the latter on the model of the former. Only because God was known to be universal could Nature be depicted that way. The connection between God and Nature has continued to inspire the musings of theologians, scientists, and naturalists, reminding us of the importance of reason and mystery in appreciating each domain. Yet readers interested in how God came to be universal will have to consult other texts. This chapter enters the story midway to ask about the universality of capital-N Nature, that is, the awe-inspiring, lawlike systematicity of the cosmos and of life on earth.

原页 88

许多东西被说成普遍的：自由、金钱、爱。但历史上最成功的两个普遍性主张——它们继续成为一切普遍性的典范——仍然是上帝与自然。上帝的普遍性与自然的普遍性在历史上相连；在欧洲文艺复兴中，现代科学的萌芽以前者为模型构想后者。只有因为上帝被认知为普遍的，自然才能被那样描绘。上帝与自然之间的联系继续激发神学家、科学家和博物学家的沉思，提醒我们理性与神秘在欣赏各自领域时的重要性。然而，对上帝如何变得普遍感兴趣的读者，将不得不查阅其他文本。本章从故事中途进入，询问大写N的自然（Nature）的普遍性，即宇宙与地球生命令人敬畏的、法则般的系统性。

原页 88, 89

Nature and the globe have helped make each other. Today’s most powerful claims about the nature of the globe refer us to global Nature: If universal laws of Nature can be established, then the globe forms an orderly part of them. The globe is a node for the expression of universal logic. Scalemaking, in turn, is a foundational move in establishing the neutrality and universalism of Nature; only if observations are compatible and collapsible across scales can they be properly described by a universal logic. Yet to “think globally” is no easy task. To recognize the globe as the relevant unit for our imaginations requires work. Moreover, establishing Nature has never been simple.

原页 88, 89

自然与地球帮助彼此形成。今天关于地球本质最有力的主张把我们引向全球自然：如果自然的普遍法则可以被确立，那么地球就是它们的有序部分。地球是普遍逻辑表达的一个节点。反过来，尺度制造是确立自然的中立性与普遍主义的一个基础性举措；只有观察在不同尺度之间相容且可相互归并，它们才能被普遍逻辑恰当描述。然而“放眼全球地思考”并非易事。要把地球认识为想象的相关单位，需要付出努力。此外，确立自然从来都不简单。

原页 89

How does the universality of Nature operate in a world of friction? I approach this question through looking at the process of “generalization,” in which small details support great visions and the universal is discovered in particularities. Two features of generalization intrigue me. First, generalization to the universal requires a large space of compatibility among disparate particular facts and observations. As long as facts are apples and oranges, one cannot generalize across them; one must first see them as “fruit” to make general claims. Compatibility standardizes difference. It allows transcendence: the general can rise above the particular. For this, compatibility must pre-exist the particular facts being examined; and it must unify the field of inquiry. The searcher for universal truths must establish an axiom of unity—whether on spiritual, aesthetic, mathematical, logical, or moral principles.

原页 89

在充满摩擦的世界中，自然的普遍性如何运作？我通过考察“概括”过程来接近这个问题，在这个过程中，小细节支持宏大的愿景，普遍性在特殊性中被发现。概括的两个特征让我着迷。第一，向普遍的概括需要在不同特殊事实与观察之间存在一个大的兼容空间。只要事实是苹果和橘子，就不能跨越它们进行概括；必须先把它们看作“水果”，才能提出一般主张。兼容性使差异标准化。它允许超越：一般可以凌驾于特殊之上。为此，兼容性必须存在于被考察的特殊事实之前；它必须统一探究的场域。普遍真理的寻求者必须确立一条统一公理——无论是基于精神的、审美的、数学的、逻辑的还是道德的原则。

原页 89

Second, tentative and contingent collaborations among disparate knowledge seekers and their disparate forms of knowledge can turn incompatible facts and observations into compatible ones. Just as tiny convergences in incompatible testimonies at a criminal trial can establish a line of truth, the founding lines through which we learn to recognize Nature are often established in convergent opinions. Convergences offer legitimacy and charisma to nascent categories. They offer bridges over unrecognizable difference. Convincing universals must be able to travel with at least some facility in the world, and this requires negotiations across incompatible difference. Upon occasion, these give rise to collaboratively agreed upon Natural objects. The unfamiliar becomes the familiar through this process, and generalization can occur.

原页 89

第二，不同知识寻求者及其不同知识形式之间试探性的、偶然的合作，可以把不相容的事实与观察变成相容的。正如刑事审判中不相容证词之间的微小趋同可以确立一条真相线索，我们借以学会辨认自然的奠基性线索，常常是在趋同的意见中确立的。趋同为新生的范畴提供合法性与感召力。它们在无法辨认的差异之上架起桥梁。有说服力的普遍性必须至少能够较为顺畅地在世界上传播，而这需要跨越不相容差异的协商。有时，这些协商会产生合作商定的自然对象。陌生者通过这一过程变成熟悉者，概括得以发生。

原页 89

What is most striking to me about these two features of generalization is the way they cover each other up. The specificity of collaborations is erased by pre-established unity; the a priori status of unity is denied by turning to its instantiation in collaborations. Buoyed by axioms of unity, collaborations create convincingly agreed upon observations and facts that then appear to support generalization directly, that is, without the prior mediation of the collaboration. The contingency of the collaboration, and its exclusions, no longer seem relevant because the facts come to “speak for themselves.” ‘The pre-evidential status of the axiom of unity fades into the background, too, when facts naturalized through collaboration can be called on as the natural basis of generalization.

原页 89

让我最震惊的是这两个概括特征的相互遮蔽方式。合作的特殊性被预先确立的统一性抹除；统一性的先验地位则通过转向其在合作中的实例化而被否认。在统一性公理的支撑下，合作创造出令人信服地商定的观察与事实，这些观察与事实随后显得直接支持概括，也就是说，无需合作的先在中介。合作的偶然性及其排斥似乎不再相关，因为事实开始“自己说话”。当通过合作自然化的事实可以被援引为概括的自然基础时，统一性公理的先于证据的地位也退入背景。

原页 89, 90

Generalization to the universal is at the heart of much analytic work; it makes it possible to devise market principles from particular transactions, to interpret events within Biblical prophecy, to mobilize class struggle, and to make scientific observations speak to general laws. No one I know wants to accept every claim made through generalization—or to dismiss them all out of hand. To characterize the process of generalization is not to reject all its products. I am not making fun of this procedure in studying it; I have no interest in ironic dismissals. I write here only about generalizations that I care about.

原页 89, 90

对普遍的概括是许多分析工作的核心；它使从具体交易中设计市场原则、在圣经预言中解释事件、动员阶级斗争，以及让科学观察支持一般法则成为可能。我认识的没有人愿意接受通过概括提出的每一个主张——或者不加考虑地将它们全盘否定。描述概括的过程并不是拒绝它的所有产物。我研究这一程序并不是在取笑它；我对反讽式的否定没有兴趣。我在这里只写我关心的那些概括。

原页 90

In this chapter, I illustrate the interplay of the two processes of generalization I have introduced in defining the global scale together with universal Nature. For this, I have chosen discrepant examples: the emergence of botanical science, American nature loving, mathematical climate modeling, and an international forestry accord. Each offers a different axiom of unity through which individual observations are made available for generalization. Botanical science first generalized on the basis of God’s will, and only later substituted evolutionary process. American nature loving proposed a spiritual and aesthetic unity for Nature. Climate modeling has offered systems logic. Forest management advocates turned to international politics. Each project, in turn, has built from a divergent history of collaborative relations, such as those that connect botanical collectors across the world, or link nature lovers and promoters of tourism, or join scientists and policy makers. I show how these contingent collaborations are necessary to the process of generalization even as they are covered up by it. Axioms of unity and collaborations both need each other and hide each other; generalization—with its particularistic exclusions and biases—is produced as the product of this interaction.

原页 90

在本章中，我通过四个相异的例子，说明我引入的两种概括过程如何在定义全球尺度与普遍自然时相互作用：植物科学的兴起、美国人对自然的热爱、数学气候建模和一项国际森林协定。每个例子都提供一种不同的统一性公理，个别观察借此可供概括。植物科学首先以上帝的意志为基础进行概括，后来才代之以演化过程。美国自然之爱为自然提出了一种精神与审美的统一。气候建模提供了系统逻辑。森林管理的倡导者转向国际政治。每个项目又各自建立在不同的合作历史之上，例如连接世界各地植物采集者的关系，或连接自然爱好者与旅游推广者的关系，或连接科学家与政策制定者的关系。我要说明这些偶然合作如何是概括过程所必需的，即使它们被这一过程所掩盖。统一性公理与合作彼此需要，也彼此隐藏；概括——连同其特殊主义的排斥与偏见——作为这种互动的产物被生产出来。

原页 90

Naming God's Creations

原页 90

为上帝的造物命名

原页 90

[T]he world is a great library, and Fruit trees are some of his Bookes wherein we may read and see plainly the Attributes of God his Power, Wisdom, Goodness, etc.

原页 90

世界是一座大图书馆，果树是他的书中的几本，在其中我们可以阅读并清楚地看到上帝的属性——力量、智慧、善等等。

原页 90

—R. Austen, The Spiritual Use of an Orchard

原页 90

——R. 奥斯汀，《果园的精神用途》（The Spiritual Use of an Orchard）

原页 90

Botanical classification had a privileged role at the beginning of modern science. Botany pioneered understandings of Nature, showing the potential of a universal science. Botany was perhaps the first science concerned with uniting knowledge from around the globe to create a singular global knowledge. The global scale and the universal were developed and demonstrated for science in this emergent field.2

原页 90

植物分类学在现代科学开端拥有特殊地位。植物学开创了对自然的理解，展示了普遍科学的潜力。植物学也许是第一门致力于把来自全球的知识联合成单一全球知识的科学。全球尺度与普遍性在这门新兴学科中为科学而发展并得到展示。2

原页 90, 91

European voyages of discovery in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries stimulated interest in the diversity of plants around the world. The folk botanies of Europe could not incorporate the wealth of unfamiliar plants that were being described from Asia, Africa, and the New World. In the ensuing excitement about new plants, a universal logic was put forward for the task of ordering global diversity: the logic of God’s creation. Plants formed a unified set because God had created them according to His plan. The insight of botanical science was to imagine from this plan a universal system of classification. In the nineteenth century, the strength of the system allowed insights about an evolutionary history linking organisms, and only then did a logic within Nature usurp God as the unifying source of order of global biology. But by then, plant classification had begun its descent to the lowly scholarly status it occupies today: data collection. Today, newly discovered plants are members of a pre-established scientific set: the plant kingdom, with its constituent families, genera, and species. They are self-evident elements of Nature and thus of little abstract interest. This success in reducing mysteries to facts speaks to the transformation of consciousness involved in making universality, and the global scale, self-evident. Botanical classification was an important catalyst for this transformation.

原页 90, 91

15、16世纪欧洲的发现航行激发了对世界各地植物多样性的兴趣。欧洲的民间植物学无法纳入那些从亚洲、非洲和新世界被描述的大量陌生植物。在对新植物的兴奋中，一种普遍逻辑被提出来承担整理全球多样性的任务：上帝创造的逻辑。植物构成一个统一集合，因为上帝按照他的计划创造了它们。植物科学的洞见在于从这一计划想象出一个普遍的分类系统。19世纪，该系统的力量使人们得以洞见连接生物体的演化史，直到那时，自然内部的逻辑才取代上帝成为全球生物秩序的统一来源。但到那时，植物分类学已开始下降到它今天所处的低微学术地位：数据收集。今天，新发现的植物是预先确立的科学集合——植物界及其所属的科、属、种——的成员。它们是自然的自明元素，因此没有多少抽象趣味。把神秘简化为事实的成功，说明了使普遍性和全球尺度变得自明所涉及的意识转变。植物分类学是这一转变的重要催化剂。

原页 91

A key feature of this transformation was the erasure of the collaborations that made global knowledge possible. European botanical knowledge in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries was gained by learning from Asians, Africans, and indigenous Americans who introduced Europeans to their native plants. Botanical treatises from this period acknowledge the centrality of these knowledge exchanges. As European power grew around the world, however, European botanists came increasingly to imagine themselves as communing directly with plants—and the universality of science—without the mediation of non-European knowledge. The very collaborations that had made this science possible were covered up, and the plants were asked to speak for themselves as elements of Nature. In the history of systematics (the science of classification), universal premises and collaboratively established facts hid each other’s work. Given its importance in establishing Nature, it is worth elaborating this story in a little more detail.

原页 91

这一转变的一个关键特征是抹除使全球知识成为可能的合作。16、17世纪欧洲的植物学知识，是通过向亚洲人、非洲人和美洲原住民学习而获得的，他们向欧洲人介绍了自己的本土植物。这一时期的植物学论著承认这些知识交流的核心地位。然而，随着欧洲势力在世界各地的增长，欧洲植物学家越来越把自己想象为直接与植物——以及科学的普遍性——交流，无需非欧洲知识的中介。使这门科学成为可能的合作恰恰被掩盖了，植物被要求作为自然元素自己说话。在系统学（分类的科学）史中，普遍前提与合作确立的事实互相隐藏了对方的工作。鉴于它在确立自然中的重要性，这个故事的更多细节值得展开。

原页 91, 92

Let me return to the moment when plant classification became a site of intellectual discussion throughout Europe—the second half of the sixteenth century. World travelers brought news of unknown and exotic plants from foreign lands. European herbalists were overwhelmed. ‘Thus arose an exciting reconsideration of knowledge, which lasted for two centuries. During this period, plant classification was at the forefront of the development of science. Scholars of the diversity of life worked particularly from two resources: classical treatises, especially the work of Aristotle, and Christian teachings about the workings of God. Both taught of a universal Nature, accessible through reason and by studying life-forms; both suggested the possibility of a singular global system uniting all life. Scholars debated about which was more important: the logical, rational system through which diversity could be charted, or the empirical study of organisms, through which the system could be inductively built. Andrea Cesalpino, a professor at Pisa and papal physician, is known for his early attempt at a universal taxonomy of plants. He relied on Aristotle, as well as his Catholic faith, to construct a rational system to account for diversity. He also developed a dichotomous key to identify plants: On the one hand, it depends on the logic of dichotomy; on the other, it follows the identifying characteristics of real plants, rather than exhausting logical possibilities (Atran 1990: 157). Not much later, Gaspard Bauhin, a Huguenot who presided over the botanical garden at Basel, sought a system of classification through tracing relationships of thousands of plants from around the world (Drayton 2000: 16). Cesalpino has been criticized for being too much of a rationalist; Bauhin has been criticized for not having enough of a logical system. But the concerns about creating a system to understand empirical diversity are clear in each.

原页 91, 92

让我回到植物分类学成为全欧洲知识讨论场所的时刻——16世纪下半叶。世界旅行者从外国土地带回未知异域植物的消息。欧洲草药学家应接不暇。于是出现了对知识的令人兴奋的重新审视，持续了两个世纪。在此期间，植物分类学处于科学发展的前沿。研究生命多样性的学者特别依赖两种资源：古典论著，尤其是亚里士多德的作品，以及关于上帝运作的基督教教义。两者都教导一种普遍的自然，可通过理性和研究生命形式而接近；两者都暗示一个联合所有生命的单一全球系统的可能性。学者们辩论哪个更重要：可以用来绘制多样性的逻辑理性系统，还是可以借以归纳地构建系统的对生物体的经验研究。比萨教授、教皇御医安德烈亚·切萨尔皮诺以其对植物普遍分类的早期尝试而闻名。他依靠亚里士多德以及他的天主教信仰，构建一个解释多样性的理性系统。他还开发了一种鉴别植物的二分检索表：一方面，它依赖二分法的逻辑；另一方面，它遵循真实植物的识别特征，而不是穷尽逻辑可能性（Atran 1990: 157）。不久之后，主持巴塞尔植物园的胡格诺派加斯帕尔·博安，试图通过追溯来自世界各地数千种植物的关系来建立分类系统（Drayton 2000: 16）。切萨尔皮诺被批评过于理性主义；博安被批评缺乏足够的逻辑系统。但创建系统以理解经验多样性的关切在两人身上都很明显。

原页 92

Basic to this discussion was the search for universal order, that is, God’s order. Cesalpino, for example, classified plants by the organization of their flower and seed parts, not, as modern biologists might, because of the role of these organs in reproductive biology, but rather because he thought these parts were the best exemplification of God’s plan (Atran 1990: 152). It turned out that classification through flower and seed worked very well to order global plant diversity; it is because of the effectiveness of this framework that botany was so significant as an emergent science. (Zoology, in comparison, was a mess at the time.) Classification by flower and seed showed the potential of systematization.3

原页 92

这场讨论的基础是寻找普遍秩序，即上帝秩序。例如，切萨尔皮诺按花与种子部位的组成来分类植物，不是因为现代生物学家可能认为的这些器官在生殖生物学中的作用，而是因为他认为这些部位最好地体现了上帝的计划（Atran 1990: 152）。结果，按花和种子分类非常有效地整理了全球植物多样性；正是因为这一框架的有效性，植物学作为一门新兴科学才如此重要。（相比之下，当时的动物学一团糟。）按花和种子分类显示了系统化的潜力。3

原页 92

God could be known through reason or through observation, but there was no question about the underlying divine plan that would be revealed. Catholics and Protestants had their differences, but both read the world as God’s book. Among botanists, differences between those who stressed reason versus empirical study were expressed in arguments about the relative priority of the “genus”—a classificatory category that grouped closely related types of plants—versus the “species”—the basic plant type. But arguments for each depended on the stability of God's plan. He created the species, and told humans to name them. He created the logic of genus, which allowed species to develop, each to its proper place. “The Creator of all things, who gave us the faculty for giving names to plants, places in the plants themselves signifying marks” (Tourefort 1719: 54, quoted in Atran 1990: 166).

原页 92

上帝可以通过理性或观察被认识，但将要揭示的潜在神圣计划是毫无疑问的。天主教徒和新教徒有分歧，但两者都把世界读作上帝的书。在植物学家中，强调理性与强调经验研究的人之间的分歧，表现在关于“属”（一个把密切相关的植物类型归为一类的分类范畴）与“种”（基本植物类型）相对优先级的争论中。但对两者的论证都依赖上帝计划的稳定性。他创造了种，并让人类为它们命名。他创造了属的逻辑，使种得以发展，各归其位。“万物的创造者赋予我们为植物命名的能力，在植物自身中放置了指示性的标记”（Tourefort 1719: 54，引自 Atran 1990: 166）。

原页 92, 93

This search for the universal—in marks on the plants themselves, and in underlying logics of plant relationships—drew attention away from the knowledge about plants that was learned in dialogue between Europeans and non-Europeans. It might have been possible for Europeans to learn about plants merely by stumbling upon them, but, in fact, they took the easier route of learning about them from other people.

原页 92, 93

这种对普遍性的寻找——在植物自身的标记中，以及在植物关系的潜在逻辑中——把注意力从欧洲人与非欧洲人对话中学到的植物知识上引开。欧洲人本来也可能只是偶然撞见植物而了解它们，但实际上，他们选择了更容易的途径：向其他人学习。

原页 93

Historian Richard Grove has described two books about plants in India that drew explicitly from such interactions. Garcia de Orta, a Portuguese doctor in Goa, wrote a treatise on botany in 1563; it was quickly translated into Latin and incorporated into European natural history. The treatise is written as a dialogue between Orta, speaking for the importance of the indigenous knowledge of Goa, and a skeptical interlocutor. Grove writes: “In general the text is remarkably subversive and even hostile to European and Arabic knowledge, regarding it as superfluous in the face of the wealth of accurate local knowledge” (1995: 81). European knowledge was not globally dominant at this period. “Far from imposing European systems of classification and perception on South Asia, the invention of printing and the collation of regional botanical knowledge actually provided an opportunity for the diffusion of indigenous South Asian methodologies of classification throughout the European world, rather than the reverse” (Grove 1995: 80). When the Dutch botanist Hendrik van Reede tot Drakenstein made a new compilation of useful plants of Malabar a century later, he assumed a similar respect for indigenous knowledge. His botanical illustrations were annotated in five languages, including the local Malayam, Arabic, and Latin (Drayton 2000: Plate 3). His text discusses his special reliance on Ezhava collectors of the “toddy-tapper” caste, who were adept at medical knowledge as well as identification of plants. His classifications, which feature Ezhava knowledge, were readily absorbed into European discussions.

原页 93

历史学家理查德·格罗夫描述了两本关于印度植物的书，它们明确取材于这类互动。果阿的葡萄牙医生加西亚·德·奥尔塔于1563年写了一部植物学论著；它很快被译成拉丁文，并入欧洲自然史。该论著以对话形式写成，奥尔塔代表果阿本土知识的重要性，一位怀疑的对话者与之辩论。格罗夫写道：“总体而言，文本对欧洲和阿拉伯知识具有非凡的颠覆性，甚至敌意，认为在丰富的准确地方知识面前，这些知识是多余的”（1995: 81）。在这一时期，欧洲知识并未在全球占主导地位。“远非把欧洲的分类与感知系统强加于南亚，印刷术的发明和区域植物学知识的整理，实际上为南亚本土分类方法在整个欧洲世界的传播提供了机会，而不是相反”（Grove 1995: 80）。一个世纪后，荷兰植物学家亨德里克·范·里德·托特·德拉肯斯坦编纂马拉巴尔有用植物的新汇编时，也表现出对本土知识的类似尊重。他的植物插图用五种语言注释，包括当地马拉雅拉姆语、阿拉伯语和拉丁语（Drayton 2000: Plate 3）。他的文本讨论了他对“棕榈汁采集者”（toddy-tapper）种姓的埃扎瓦采集者的特别依赖，这些人既精通医学知识，也擅长识别植物。他的分类突出埃扎瓦知识，这些分类很容易被欧洲讨论吸收。

原页 93

Yet discussions among Europeans refused to acknowledge this global sharing of knowledge. Instead, they focused on the formation of a universal system of classification. John Ray, known for his “grammar” of botany (Atran 1990: 61), obviously read van Reede: “Who could believe that in one province of Malabar, hardly a vast place, there could be three hundred unique, indigenous species of trees and fruit?” (Ray 1686: sig. A3v quoted in Drayton 2000: 18). Yet he attributed no importance to the Ezhava dialogue that brought those species to him. The system itself was knowledge, not its component parts.

原页 93

然而，欧洲人之间的讨论拒绝承认这种全球知识共享。相反，他们专注于形成普遍的分类系统。以植物“语法”闻名的约翰·雷（Atran 1990: 61）显然读过范·里德：“谁能相信，在马拉巴尔的一个省，几乎不算一个广阔地方，竟有三百种独特的本土树木和水果？”（Ray 1686: sig. A3v，引自 Drayton 2000: 18）。但他并不重视把这些物种带给他的埃扎瓦对话。系统本身就是知识，而不是它的组成部分。

原页 93

Carl Linnaeus, known as the father of modern biological classification, explained the importance of the system in unifying and ordering a singular global knowledge:

原页 93

被称为现代生物分类学之父的卡尔·林奈，解释了系统在统一和整理单一全球知识方面的重要性：

原页 93, 94

The system is for botany the thread of Ariadna, without which there is chaos. Let us take, for example, an unknown plant of the Indies, and let a botanophile leaf through descriptions, figures, every index; he will not find it unless by chance. But a systematist will determine it straight away, be it old or new. ... The system indicates the plants, even those it does not mention; this, the enumeration of a catalog can never do. (Linnaeus 1751: sec. 156, quoted in Atran 1990: 170–71)

原页 93, 94

系统是植物学的阿里阿德涅之线，没有它，只有混沌。让我们以一株未知的印度诸地（the Indies）的植物为例，让一位植物爱好者翻阅描述、插图、每一个索引；除非碰巧，他不会找到它。但系统学家会立刻鉴定它，无论新旧。……系统指示植物，甚至包括它没有提到的植物；这是目录的列举永远做不到的。（Linnaeus 1751: sec. 156，引自 Atran 1990: 170–71）

原页 94

The system takes precedence over the plant, as well as the process through which that plant was gathered “out there.” Linneaus unselfconsciously adopted van Reede’s Malabar classifications without noting them as foreign (Grove 1995: 90). For him, all correct knowledge could be united through the use of a universal method. The method is the key to Nature. “Nowhere has the Supreme Creator exposed as many objects to the senses of man as in the Plant Realm, which covers and fills the globe we inhabit. Thus, if there be anywhere a proper method, it is that whereby we may hope to obtain a clear idea of Plants” (Linneaus 1737, quoted in Atran 1990: 151). Since it uncovers the handiwork of God, the system of classification must form a unified, homogeneous whole. There is no understanding here of knowledge as gained in dialogue—and certainly not dialogue between Christians and non-Christians.

原页 94

系统优先于植物，也优先于那株植物“在那里”被采集的过程。林奈不自觉地采用了范·里德的马拉巴尔分类，却没有注明它们是外来的（Grove 1995: 90）。对他来说，所有正确的知识都可以通过使用一种普遍方法联合起来。方法是通往自然的钥匙。“至高创造者从未像在植物界那样，把如此多的对象暴露给人的感官，植物界覆盖并充满我们居住的地球。因此，如果任何地方有恰当的方法，那就是我们借以有望获得植物清晰概念的方法”（Linnaeus 1737，引自 Atran 1990: 151）。由于它揭示上帝的杰作，分类系统必须构成一个统一、同质的整体。这里没有把知识理解为在对话中获得的理解——当然也不是基督徒与非基督徒之间的对话。

原页 94

As European hegemony grew, European knowledge increasingly directed global programs. If botanists came to see themselves as alone with Nature, it was because of this political power as well as the insight of “the system” in which all knowledges could be absorbed. Scholars of colonialism have pointed to the texts of eighteenthand nineteenth-century European botanists, gathering plants in non-European locales, as models for imperial consciousness. In contrast to the earlier period, European botanists wrote of the plants but not the people. Their texts emptied the landscapes they studied of human inhabitants, making them appropriate for European settlement and conquest (Pratt 1992; Carter 1987). In the process, they suppressed attention to the practices in which at least some of their knowledge was gained.

原页 94

随着欧洲霸权增长，欧洲知识越来越主导全球纲领。如果植物学家逐渐把自己看作与自然独处，那既是因为这种政治权力，也是因为“系统”的洞见——所有知识都可以被吸收其中。殖民主义学者指出，18、19世纪欧洲植物学家在非欧洲地点采集植物的文本，是帝国意识的典范。与更早时期相比，欧洲植物学家写植物，却不写人。他们的文本清空了所研究地景中的人类居民，使其适合欧洲定居与征服（Pratt 1992; Carter 1987）。在此过程中，他们压抑了对至少部分知识借以获得的那种实践的关注。

原页 94, 95

Contemporary efforts to describe plants around the world continue to rely on this emptying out of Nature: Although they often depend on folk experts familiar with local flora, they disavow collaboration except among scientists. Celia Lowe (1999) has studied the species-collection activities of a conservation organization in the Indonesian Togean Islands. She found that English-speaking foreign volunteers objected to learning native names; they imagined their task in finding Nature to be the direct matching of organisms and internationally recorded Latin species names. Their Indonesian hosts and guides juggled local, national, English, and Latin species names, and they used their familiarity with multiple systems to identify species. But they, too, favored Latin names to show their affinities with international science; in their reports, only Latin names counted. This use and disavowal of cross-cultural collaboration also characterizes commercial bioprospecting. In her study of pharmaceutical bioprospecting in Mexico, Corinne Hayden (2003) found that researchers depended upon folk knowledge of plants to acquire biologically active samples. The researchers she studied bought plants from market vendors, who described for them herbs used within Mexican folk medicine. However, it was protocol that samples forwarded to their North American partners for further testing be divested of this folk medical information. To count as scientific samples, the biological material was purified from the history of its discovery.

原页 94, 95

当代描述世界各地植物的努力继续依赖这种对自然的清空：尽管它们常常依靠熟悉当地植物的民间专家，却否认除科学家之间的合作之外的任何合作。西莉亚·洛（1999）研究了印尼托吉安群岛一个保护组织的物种采集活动。她发现，讲英语的外国志愿者反对学习当地名称；他们把自己的任务想象为直接把生物体与国际记录的拉丁物种名匹配。他们的印尼东道主和向导则在地方、国家、英语和拉丁物种名之间周旋，利用自己对多个系统的熟悉来识别物种。但他们也偏爱拉丁名，以显示自己与国际科学的亲近；在他们的报告中，只有拉丁名算数。这种对跨文化合作的使用与否认也表征了商业生物勘探。科琳·海登（2003）对墨西哥制药生物勘探的研究发现，研究人员依赖植物的民间知识来获得具有生物活性的样本。她研究的研究人员从市场商贩那里购买植物，商贩向他们描述墨西哥民间医学中使用的草药。然而，规程要求，转交给其北美合作伙伴进一步测试的样本必须剥离这些民间医学信息。为了算作科学样本，生物材料被从其发现史中净化出来。

原页 95

This is a very specific Nature. As the touchstone of biodiversity discourse, it is a resource for environmental politics, and it is one way of encompassing the local within the globe. It also can be criticized for its imperial gaze. Might it be possible to attend to Nature’s collaborative origins without losing the advantages of its global reach?

原页 95

这是一种非常特定的自然。作为生物多样性话语的试金石，它是环境政治的资源和一种把地方纳入全球的方式；也可以因其帝国式凝视而受到批评。能否既关注自然的合作起源，又不失去其全球触及的优势？

原页 95

Meanwhile, there are other possibilities for uniting God and Nature. I turn to a different way to the universal, and to the local in the global.

原页 95

与此同时，还有把上帝与自然结合的其他可能性。我转向通往普遍、以及通往全球中之地方的另一种方式。

原页 95

Nature Located—in a Global Gaze

原页 95

自然被定位——在一种全球凝视中

原页 95

[W]hen we contemplate the whole globe as one great dewdrop, striped and dotted with continents and islands, flying through space with other stars all singing and shining together as one, the whole universe appears as an infinite storm of beauty.

原页 95

当我们把整个地球看成一滴巨大的露珠，上面条纹斑驳、点缀着大陆和岛屿，与群星一起在太空中飞行，所有星辰一同歌唱、闪耀如一体，整个宇宙便显现为一场无限的美的风暴。

原页 95

—John Muir, Travels in Alaska

原页 95

——约翰·缪尔，《阿拉斯加游记》（Travels in Alaska）

原页 95

Nature soared in Europe and North America in the second half of the nineteenth century—in the gaze of educated travelers, in amateur and professional natural history, in emergent natural sciences, in philosophy, and in poetry. Looking back at this period, contemporary environmentalists single out Scottish-American nature writer John Muir as a prophet of Nature. Muir was a master of rhetoric who conjured reverence for Nature and zeal in protecting its significant wild places. In these wild places, he argued, the global force of Nature is condensed and made available in all its beauty and power for the appreciation of the cosmopolitan pilgrim.

原页 95

19世纪下半叶，自然在欧洲和北美翱翔——在受过教育的旅行者的凝视中，在业余和专业自然史中，在新兴自然科学中，在哲学和诗歌中。回望这一时期，当代环保主义者把苏格兰裔美国自然作家约翰·缪尔视为自然的先知。缪尔是一位修辞大师，他召唤对自然的敬畏，以及保护其重要荒野地方的热情。他主张，在这些荒野地方，自然的全球力量被凝缩，以其全部美丽与力量提供给世界主义朝圣者欣赏。

原页 95, 96

This vision of a condensed and located global Nature moved a public, who, like Muir, imagined themselves as travelers in a wide and astonishing world. Muir’s rhetoric galvanized an emergent movement of nature appreciators, bringing together natural scientists and lay people to create a new kind of public advocacy. Together with businessmen who promoted tourism and patriots who imagined U.S. wilderness as an equivalent to European monuments, these nature appreciators invented the idea of national parks, an idea that proved charismatic enough to spread around the world. The national park idea catered to a model of citizenship that privileged those who imagined themselves as cosmopolitan and civilized travelers, and thus potential park visitors. Wild nature would teach and refresh the cosmopolitan heart. Without a coalition of public forces, this vision would never have flourished. Yet its focus on personal inspiration in the encounter between an individual and Nature denied all social mediation.

原页 95, 96

这种凝缩且定位的全球自然观，打动了那些像缪尔一样把自己想象为广阔而惊人的世界中的旅行者的公众。缪尔的修辞激发了新兴的自然欣赏者运动，把自然科学家和普通人联合起来，创造了一种新的公共倡导。与推广旅游的商人以及把美国荒野想象为欧洲纪念碑对等物的爱国者一起，这些自然欣赏者发明了国家公园的理念，这一理念被证明具有足够的感召力，传播到全世界。国家公园理念迎合了一种公民身份模式，它赋予那些把自己想象为世界主义、文明旅行者的人以特权，因此他们也是潜在的公园游客。荒野自然会教导并滋养世界主义者的心灵。如果没有公共力量的联盟，这一愿景永远不会繁荣。然而，它专注于个人与自然相遇时的个人灵感，否认了一切社会中介。

原页 96

As in my previous example, the collaborative construction of Natural facts—here including inspiration—was shrouded by an axiom of unity in which individual experiences and observations could be referred directly to the universal. Here, too, the axiom of unity depended on the interplay of Nature and God. Yet Muir’s God was personal and pantheistic, leading him to discover not the system behind all diversity but rather the totality in the local, the global at home. The collaborations on which it depended (and which it hid) did not cross oceans but instead forged a cosmopolitanism ready to rebuild the nation. This coalescence, with its wide-reaching effects on global nature loving (see chapter 4), is worth exploring in more depth.

原页 96

如同我之前的例子，自然事实——这里包括灵感——的合作建构被一条统一性公理所遮蔽，个别经验和观察可以直接被归结为普遍。同样，这条统一性公理依赖自然与上帝的相互作用。然而缪尔的上帝是人格化的、泛神论的，这使他发现的不是所有多样性背后的系统，而是地方中的总体性，在家的全球。它所依赖的（并隐藏的）合作并没有跨越海洋，而是锻造了一种准备重建国家的世界主义。这种聚合，及其对全球自然之爱的广泛影响（见第四章），值得更深入地探讨。

原页 96

John Muir grew up with a potent mixture of Nature and God. His father was a strict and zealous Christian who, in pursuit of religious mission, moved the family from Scotland to rural Wisconsin. Muir recalls his childhood there as full of discipline and pioneer challenges. As a young man, Muir spent some time at the University of Wisconsin, where he was introduced to transcendentalist philosophy and botany. Evading the draft, he spent two years in search of rare plants in Canada. He returned to the United States to work in a factory in Indianapolis, where an industrial accident blinded him temporarily. In his recollections, Muir credits the accident for turning his path more fully toward Nature—as God. “I bade adieu to all my mechanical inventions, determined to devote the rest of my life to the study of the inventions of God” (Lankford 1991: 46).

原页 96
