约翰·缪尔在自然与上帝的强烈混合中长大。他的父亲是一位严格而狂热的基督徒，为了追求宗教使命，把家从苏格兰搬到威斯康星乡村。缪尔回忆那里的童年充满纪律与拓荒挑战。年轻时，缪尔在威斯康星大学待了一段时间，在那里接触到超验主义哲学和植物学。为逃避征兵，他在加拿大寻找稀有植物两年。他回到美国，在印第安纳波利斯的一家工厂工作，一次工业事故使他暂时失明。在回忆中，缪尔把这次事故归功于让他的道路更彻底地转向自然——作为上帝。“我告别了我所有的机械发明，决心把余生献给研究上帝的发明”（Lankford 1991: 46）。

原页 96, 97

In 1867, at the age of 29, Muir traveled south, determined to see the grandeur of Nature in South America as described by world explorer Alexander Humboldt. “How intensely I desire to be Humboldt!” he wrote to a friend (Fox 1981: 47). But a bout of malaria in Florida convinced him to travel west instead of south. He took a boat to California and walked east toward the Sierra Nevada Mountains. When he recalled his first glimpse of the Sierras later, it was with that potent religious vision of Nature that characterized so much of his writing. Starting from the western mountains, he looked east over California’s Central Valley, which at that time was strewn with flowers. “And from the eastern boundary of this vast golden flower-bed rose the mighty Sierra, miles in height, and so gloriously colored and so radiant, it seemed not clothed with light, but wholly composed of it, like the wall of some celestial city” (Muir 1988: 2). He was even more deeply moved upon finding himself in the spectacular Yosemite Valley. “I feel like preaching these mountains like an apostle,” he wrote (Fox 1981: 12). Although he later settled in San Francisco, and, after his marriage, on a ranch outside Oakland, it was Yosemite that remained the center of his gaze.

原页 96, 97

1867年，29岁的缪尔向南旅行，决心去看世界探险家亚历山大·洪堡所描述的南美洲自然的壮丽。“我是多么强烈地渴望成为洪堡！”他在给朋友的信中写道（Fox 1981: 47）。但在佛罗里达的一次疟疾发作说服他向西而不是向南。他乘船到加利福尼亚，向东步行前往内华达山脉。后来回忆起第一次瞥见内华达山脉时，他带着那种强烈的宗教性自然观，这成为他许多写作的特征。从西部山脉出发，他向东眺望加利福尼亚中央谷地，当时那里遍布鲜花。“从这片广阔金色花床的东部边界，升起雄伟的内华达山脉，高耸数英里，色彩如此辉煌、光芒如此四射，它似乎不是披着光，而是完全由光构成，像某座天城的城墙”（Muir 1988: 2）。当他发现自己置身壮观的约塞米蒂谷时，他更为深深感动。“我觉得自己要像使徒一样宣讲这些山脉，”他写道（Fox 1981: 12）。虽然他后来定居旧金山，婚后住在奥克兰郊外的一个牧场，但约塞米蒂始终是他凝视的中心。

原页 97

Muir’s descriptions of Yosemite helped others see Nature’s power. Some of these were men of influence: philosopher Ralph Waldo Emerson; future president Theodore Roosevelt. Others were friends and colleagues. Muir cofounded the Sierra Club, bringing together nature lovers, scientists, and advocates for the preservation of nature, and thus crystallizing that amateurprofessional-activist synthesis that still invigorates environmentalism today. Meanwhile, Muir’s writing mobilized an American love of Nature. One result of this mobilization was legislation designed to protect Yosemite Valley—passed first by California and then by the federal government to designate it a national park. Muir, then, is credited with inspiring the national parks movement that spread in and beyond the United States.

原页 97

缪尔对约塞米蒂的描述帮助他人看到自然的力量。其中一些人是有影响力的人物：哲学家拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生；未来的总统西奥多·罗斯福。其他人是朋友和同事。缪尔共同创立了塞拉俱乐部，把自然爱好者、科学家和保护自然的倡导者联合起来，从而结晶了那种业余者—专业人士—活动家的综合，它至今仍为环保主义注入活力。与此同时，缪尔的写作动员了美国人对自然的热爱。这种动员的一个结果是旨在保护约塞米蒂谷的立法——先由加州通过，然后由联邦政府指定为国家公园。因此，缪尔被认为启发了在美国内外传播的国家公园运动。

原页 97

Muir’s message depended on dramatic, emotionally charged modes of expression, infused with religious rhetoric. Consider Muir’s famous indictment of those who would dam Yosemite’s Hetch Hetchy Valley for a water reservoir: “The temple destroyers, devotees of raging commercialism, seem to have a perfect contempt for Nature, and, instead of lifting their eyes to the God of the mountains, lift them to the Almighty Dollar. Dam Hetch Hetchy! As well dam for water-tanks the people’s cathedrals and churches, for no holier temple has ever been consecrated by the heart of man” (Smith 1987: 177). This passage is characteristic of Muir’s identification of Nature as a focus of religious devotion. It mobilizes an advocacy for the sacred, and for the locally sacred—our church—as well as the universal religion it represents. Nature is God, in Hetch Hetchy and beyond. Muir was a priest of Nature, bringing it devotees. On meeting Emerson, Muir wrote: “I invite you to join me in a month’s worship with Nature in the high temples of the great Sierra Crown beyond our holy Yosemite.... With most cordial regards I am yours in Nature, John Muir” (Fox 1981: 5). Scholars of Muir have noted that Muir’s identification of God and Nature is hardly Christian orthodoxy.4 However, Muir’s worship of Nature shares much with the heterodox Protestant Christianity he knew best. Nature, like God, forms the basis of a universal Truth, accessible through direct experience and study. To study a particular instance offers a window into the universal. The local enfolds into the global and the universal; our devotions must simultaneously know the local and its transcendence.

原页 97

缪尔的讯息依赖戏剧性、充满情感的表达方式，浸透着宗教修辞。想想缪尔对那些要筑坝拦截约塞米蒂赫奇赫奇谷作水库的人的著名控诉：“神庙破坏者、狂热商业主义的信徒，似乎对自然怀有完全的蔑视，他们不抬眼看山中之神，而是抬眼看万能的美元。给赫奇赫奇筑坝吧！不如也为人民的座堂和教堂筑坝作水箱，因为人心从未奉献过比这更神圣的神殿”（Smith 1987: 177）。这段话典型地体现了缪尔把自然认同为宗教虔诚的焦点。它动员了对神圣者、对地方神圣者——我们的教堂——的倡导，也倡导它所代表的普遍宗教。自然是上帝，在赫奇赫奇，也在别处。缪尔是自然的祭司，为它带来信徒。在见到爱默生时，缪尔写道：“我邀请您与我一起，在我们神圣的约塞米蒂之外伟大的塞拉皇冠的高山神殿中，与自然共度一个月的礼拜……致以最诚挚的问候，在自然中忠于您的，约翰·缪尔”（Fox 1981: 5）。缪尔研究者注意到，缪尔把上帝与自然等同起来，很难说是基督教正统。4然而，缪尔对自然的崇拜与他最熟悉的异端新教基督教有许多共同之处。自然和上帝一样，构成普遍真理的基础，可通过直接经验与研究接近。研究一个特殊实例，就打开一扇通往普遍的窗户。地方包蕴于全球与普遍之中；我们的虔诚必须同时认识地方及其超越。

原页 98

Muir worked back and forth between evoking global Nature and its local instances. One interpreter of his writing speaks of the ubiquity of “planetary passages,” in which references to the “earth-planet” offer a heightened emotional charge to landscape descriptions (Lankford 1991: 35).5 Yosemite thus instantiated global space and time.

原页 98

缪尔在召唤全球自然与其地方实例之间来回工作。他写作的一位解释者谈到“行星段落”的普遍存在，其中对“地球—行星”的提及为地景描述增添了更高的情感强度（Lankford 1991: 35）。5约塞米蒂由此实例化了全球的空间与时间。

原页 98

Yosemite temples will be the more enjoyed by those who have traced ... the crystallization of the granite in the dark, thousands of centuries before development, and who know how in the fullness of time the sun called to lift water out of the sea in vapor which was carried by the winds to the mountains, crystallized into snow among the clouds, to fall on the summits, form glaciers, and bring Yosemite Valley ... to light. (Muir quoted in Lankford 1991: 41)

原页 98

那些追溯过……花岗岩在黑暗中的结晶过程——在其发育之前数千个世纪——并且知道时机成熟时，太阳如何召唤海水化作蒸汽升起，蒸汽被风带到山间，在云中结晶为雪，降落在峰顶，形成冰川，把约塞米蒂谷……带入光明的人，会更加欣赏约塞米蒂的神庙。（缪尔，引自 Lankford 1991: 41）

原页 98

Muir’s Nature—and his Yosemite—are forged in a scale-making project in which the local and the global are wrapped together and charged by the principles of the universal. Yosemite stood for the possibility of individual contact, through study and experience, with the hugeness of a global and universal Nature. Not any individual, however, can achieve this gaze. The subject who can grasp Nature here is the cosmopolitan traveler. Muir’s use of travel writing as the genre in which he conveyed his sense of Nature’s wonders is not incidental. Like Humboldt who inspired him, Muir appeals to the free metropolitan intellect who can imagine him- or herself in global travel. It is tempting to identify this reader as white, male, and wealthy, but this is not historically accurate. White women were among the most enthusiastic audiences for Muir’s writing, and women’s clubs energized the movement to create parks and nature reserves (Smith 1987).6 Moreover, Muir projected an ambiguous or androgynous gender identification in his writing, drawing female readers and gentle men (Jespersen 1997). Indeed, Muir’s opponents weakened him by portraying his cause as feminine; some scholars have argued that this feminization of nature protection kept environmentalism at a low profile through the first half of the twentieth century (Smith 1987). Race and class are also ambiguously implicated. Rather than reduce him to a “type,” it is useful to look at who joined this collaborative momentum.

原页 98

缪尔的自然——以及他的约塞米蒂——在一个尺度制造项目中被锻造，其中地方与全球被包裹在一起，并被普遍原则赋予力量。约塞米蒂代表了一种可能性：通过研究与经验，个人可以与一个全球性、普遍性自然的庞大整体接触。然而，并非任何个人都能获得这种凝视。在这里能够把握自然的主体是世界主义旅行者。缪尔使用旅行写作这一体裁来传达他对自然奇观的感受，并非偶然。像启发他的洪堡一样，缪尔诉诸自由的大都市知识分子，他们能想象自己置身全球旅行。人们很容易把这位读者认定为白人、男性、富有，但这在历史上并不准确。白人女性是缪尔写作最热情的受众之一，妇女俱乐部为创建公园和自然保护区的运动注入了活力（Smith 1987）。6此外，缪尔在写作中投射出一种模糊的或兼具两性特征的性别认同，吸引了女性读者和文雅的男性（Jespersen 1997）。事实上，缪尔的对手通过把他的事业描绘为女性化来削弱他；一些学者认为，这种对自然保护的女性化使环保主义在20世纪上半叶未能获得广泛关注（Smith 1987）。种族和阶级也以模糊的方式牵涉其中。与其把他简化为一个“类型”，不如看看谁加入了这一合作势头。

原页 98, 99

Consider, then, Muir’s most powerful allies: scientists, nature lovers, and a certain set of entrepreneurs and politicians. Each of these was invested in the cosmopolitan gaze upon Nature. In science, Muir’s affinities were with scientists who themselves were working through the relation between local and global instances of universal Natural law. Muir’s study of glaciation in Yosemite Valley was in direct dialogue with Louis Agassiz, a Harvard naturalist who studied the chronology of rock strata as evidence of a global era of glaciation. Muir also worked with evolutionary biologist Asa Gray in collecting Western flora. In studies of glaciation and botany, Muir’s sense that Nature formed a book that could be read—a global/local instancing of the universal—brought him inside an important current of nineteenth-century naturalism.

原页 98, 99

那么，考虑缪尔最强大的盟友：科学家、自然爱好者，以及某类企业家和政治家。他们每一个人都投入于对自然的世界主义凝视。在科学中，缪尔的亲和力在于那些自身正在处理普遍自然法则的地方与全球实例之间关系的科学家。缪尔对约塞米蒂谷冰川作用的研究，直接与哈佛博物学家路易斯·阿加西对话，后者研究岩层年代学，作为全球冰川期证据。缪尔还与演化生物学家阿萨·格雷合作采集西部植物。在冰川学和植物学研究中，缪尔认为自然构成一本可读的书——普遍性的全球/地方实例化——这把他带入19世纪博物学的重要潮流。

原页 99

Muir’s most enduring fans have been nature lovers and environmentalists. It is only because of their efforts that his legacy continues to be important today. Even during Muir’s lifetime, they came in different sorts, from the activist hikers of the Sierra Club, to the women’s clubs already mentioned, to tourists, scholars, and publishers. Despite their differences, the Californians among these nature lovers shared certain orientations: California was a new state, still at the edge of being a colonial territory. Through much of the nineteenth century, “science” in California consisted mostly of military surveys, commissioned for the purpose of securing administrative control. Muir formed part of a change in which science and nature loving signaled a more civilian form of citizenship. The settlers became citizens through their love of the land. Muir’s evocation of Nature helped to secure this form of settler consciousness (Smith 1987)7

原页 99

缪尔最持久的粉丝一直是自然爱好者和环保主义者。正是因为他们的努力，他的遗产今天仍然重要。即使在缪尔生前，他们也以不同种类出现，从塞拉俱乐部的参与行动的徒步者，到已经提到的妇女俱乐部，再到游客、学者和出版商。尽管有差异，这些自然爱好者中的加州人共享某些取向：加州是一个新州，仍处于是否属于殖民领地的模糊边界上。19世纪的大部分时间里，加州的“科学”主要由军事勘测构成，委托目的是确保行政控制。缪尔参与了这样一场变化：科学与自然之爱标志着一种更平民化的公民身份形式。定居者通过热爱土地而成为公民。缪尔对自然的召唤帮助确立了这种定居者意识（Smith 1987）。7

原页 99

The support of these groups only translated into political effectiveness, however, because of influential allies: the bosses of the Southern Pacific Railroad. Muir formed a friendship with railroad baron E. H. Harriman, who convinced the U.S. Congress to designate Yosemite a national park (Fox 1981). The railroad was interested in the development of tourism since tourists came to the western United States mainly by train. Larger issues of what it meant to be a citizen were also at stake. The railroad block promoted notions of citizenship in which cosmopolitan travelers—people on the move—were the quintessential U.S. citizens. These people could benefit from encounters with Nature; indeed, these mobile and malleable citizens could be made as such in encounters with Nature. The railroad bosses fought for a particular point of view in the making of the western United States, and Muir’s version of Nature supported their struggle.

原页 99

然而，这些群体的支持只有通过有影响力的盟友才能转化为政治效力：南太平洋铁路的老板们。缪尔与铁路大亨 E. H. 哈里曼结成友谊，后者说服美国国会把约塞米蒂指定为国家公园（Fox 1981）。铁路对旅游业的发展感兴趣，因为游客主要通过火车来到美国西部。关于作为公民意味着什么的更大问题也牵涉其中。铁路集团推广这样一种公民观念：世界主义旅行者——移动中的人——是典型美国公民。这些人可以从与自然的相遇中受益；事实上，这些流动而可塑的公民可以在与自然的相遇中被塑造成这样的人。铁路老板们在美国西部的制造中为一种特定观点而斗争，缪尔版本的自然支持了他们的斗争。

原页 99

Muir’s articulation also created opponents and areas of invisibility. Ranchers were Muir’s most explicit enemies; ranchers used the wilderness rather than experiencing or studying it. They were cut off from the universal; they destroyed it through inattention. Ranchers became the icon of one side of a dichotomy dividing the exploitation of Nature from its study and protection.

原页 99

缪尔的接合也制造了对手和不可见的区域。牧场主是缪尔最明确的敌人；牧场主利用荒野，而不是体验或研究它。他们被排除在普遍之外；他们因不注意而毁灭它。牧场主成为二分法一方的象征，这种二分法把对自然的开发与其研究和保护分隔开来。

原页 99

This dichotomy forms the basis of the most well-known divide in U.S. environmental politics: the divide between “conservation” and “preservation.” (These terms take on particular meanings for this debate; after discussing the debate I return to using the term “conservation” much more broadly.) Histories of U.S. environmentalism often begin with Muir’s disagreements with Gifford Pinchot, who became the first head of the U.S. Forest Service.8

原页 99

这种二分法构成美国环境政治中最著名的分歧的基础：“保育”（conservation）与“保存”（preservation）之间的分歧。（这些术语在这场辩论中具有特定含义；讨论完这场辩论后，我将回到更广泛地使用“保育”一词。）美国环保主义的历史常常从缪尔与吉福德·平肖的分歧开始，平肖成为美国林务局的第一任局长。8

原页 100

Pinchot, educated in the emerging European science of scientific forestry, believed that forests should serve economic and state-administrative interests. Ranching, timbering, and other forms of commercial use were a proper part of forest management; the goal of forestry was to maintain a national stock of forest lands precisely for such uses. Pinchot here stands for a view of the forests that combines utilitarian use and bureaucratic control, in this story called “conservation.” Muir, in contrast, stands for the full protection of Nature for its own sake.

原页 100

平肖接受过新兴欧洲科学林业的教育，认为森林应服务于经济和国家行政利益。牧牛、伐木和其他形式的商业利用是森林管理的正当部分；林业的目标正是为国家维持森林土地储备以供这些用途。平肖在这里代表一种结合功利性使用与官僚控制的森林观，在这个故事中称为“保育”。相比之下，缪尔代表为了自然本身而全面保护自然。

原页 100

Both sides of this debate formed their momentum through culturally specific claims about the universal that blocked attention to the sometimes discordant collaborations that enlivened each agenda. Scientific forestry promoted universals of rationalism and profit. The uses of nature could be planned through a calculus of management. This agenda drew bureaucrats and businessmen. It also appealed to popular democracy: people should use forests. In this spirit, small as well as large users have been drawn to the resource management agenda. However, it is useful to remember that the legacies of both Pinchot and Muir articulate problematic universals and draw dangerous allies into the struggle for environmental well-being.

原页 100

这场辩论双方都通过文化特定的普遍性主张形成势头，这些主张阻挡人们关注使各自议程活跃起来的、有时不协调的合作。科学林业推广理性主义与利润的普遍性。自然的各种用途可以通过管理计算来规划。这一议程吸引了官僚和商人。它也诉诸大众民主：人民应该使用森林。本着这种精神，小用户和大用户都被吸引到资源管理议程中。然而，值得记住的是，平肖和缪尔的遗产都阐发了成问题的普遍性，并把危险的盟友拉进环境福祉的斗争。

原页 100, 101

The debate reminds us why Muir’s vision continues to inspire. In contrast to the resource managers, Muir tells us that Nature cannot be reduced to the needs of capitalism and the state. Nature deserves protection for itself. Here too are the shortcomings of the collaborative legacy of Muir’s vision. The nature protection that Muir stimulated has not done well in forming alliances with local residents, who tend to be dismissed as users and therefore despoilers of nature. It has been easier to gain the support of distant corporate sponsors, who, like Muir’s railroad friends, support nature tourism, rather than resident communities. As the national park idea spread around the world, parks advocacy formed even more problematic alliances with colonial heritages of resettlement and the displacement of indigenous residents. Residents have been evicted from nature reserves by force; local livelihoods have been disrupted. Recent environmental scholarship is full of documentation on the conflicts between residents and parks.9 The challenges loom large.10

These alliances and enmities are the collaborative legacy John Muir set into motion. They form the power and the danger of this legacy; they set an awkward agenda. Yet nature lovers rarely acknowledge these issues; certainly Muir himself did not. Why? Muir’s vision of Nature itself shut out the possibility that collaborations were important. Nature was knowable through direct experience. We need no conversations to make Nature come to life; we want direct access to the universal text. “The clearest way into the Universe is through a forest wilderness” (Muir quoted in Lankford 1991: 38). Environmentalists and nature lovers must struggle with this legacy, which offers both the transcendent power of Nature and the inability to know one’s own collaborative positions.

原页 100, 101

这场辩论提醒我们缪尔的愿景为何继续激励人。与资源管理者相反，缪尔告诉我们，自然不能被简化为资本主义和国家的需要。自然应为其自身而受到保护。这里也有缪尔愿景合作遗产的缺陷。缪尔所激发的自然保护，在与当地居民结盟方面做得不好，当地居民往往被斥为使用者，从而是自然的掠夺者。获得远方企业赞助者的支持更容易，他们像缪尔的铁路朋友一样支持自然旅游，而不是居民社区。随着国家公园理念在世界各地传播，公园倡导与殖民遗产的重新安置和土著居民流离失所形成了更成问题的联盟。居民被武力驱逐出自然保护区；地方生计受到扰乱。晚近的环境学术研究充满了关于居民与公园之间冲突的记录。9挑战极其巨大。10

这些联盟与敌意是约翰·缪尔启动的合作遗产。它们构成这份遗产的力量与危险；它们设定一个尴尬的议程。然而自然爱好者很少承认这些问题；缪尔本人当然也没有。为什么？缪尔对自然本身的愿景排除了合作很重要的可能性。自然可以通过直接经验被认识。我们不需要对话来让自然活起来；我们想要直接进入普遍文本。“进入宇宙最清晰的路，是穿过一片森林荒野”（Muir，引自 Lankford 1991: 38）。环保主义者和自然爱好者必须与这份遗产抗争，它既提供了自然的超越力量，也提供了无法认识自身合作位置的无能。

原页 101

Meanwhile, the United States launched other understandings of the globe. After World War II, U.S. military intelligence research was responsible for new kinds of globalisms, in which a mechanical vision of the relations of the parts to the whole replaces God as the author of universal laws. Cybernetics, systems dynamics, systems ecology, and circulation models were developed from the insight that systems create their own dynamics. Information about the interrelationship of elements within a system can generate knowledge of the whole. In contrast to Muir’s endorsement of the global condensed in the local, these models bypass locality completely, except as an unmarked moment in scaling up and down. The system of flow and feedback takes precedence to any internal point. The global emerges as a node of systematicity. A key example is the model-making at the heart of public and scientific discussion of global climate change. My focus here is not the making of a universal logic but rather its use in the construction of a new kind of global scale. Collaborations across difference are both demanded and denied in this process.

原页 101

与此同时，美国推出了对地球的另一些理解。二战后，美国军事情报研究促成了新型全球主义，其中一种关于部分与整体关系的机械论视角取代上帝，成为普遍法则的作者。控制论、系统动力学、系统生态学和环流模型的发展，源于系统创造自身动态的洞见。关于系统内各要素相互关系的信息可以产生关于整体的知识。与缪尔赞成的全球凝缩于地方相反，这些模型完全绕过地方性，除非把它当作尺度放大和缩小中一个未被标记的时刻。流动与反馈的系统优先于任何内部点。全球作为系统性的节点出现。一个关键例子是处于全球气候变化公共与科学讨论核心的模型制造。我在这里关注的不是普遍逻辑的制造，而是它在建构一种新全球尺度中的使用。在这一过程中，跨越差异的合作既被要求，又被否认。

原页 101

Global Climate is a Model

原页 101

全球气候是一个模型

原页 101

Developing a predictive understanding of global environmental change in order to provide a scientific basis for national and international policy and decision making requires a comprehensive, interdisciplinary approach to studying the total Earth system.

原页 101

为了给国家和国际政策与决策提供科学基础，发展对全球环境变化的预测性理解，需要一种全面的、跨学科的方法来研究整个地球系统。

原页 101

—SEDAC, Consortium for International Earth Science Information Network, “a part of NASA’s Earth Observing System Data and Information System,” 1993 brochure

原页 101

——SEDAC，国际地球科学信息网络联盟，“NASA地球观测系统数据与信息系统的一部分”，1993年宣传册

原页 101

In the 1990s, global climate change was the center of what environmentalists, and the interested public, thought about when they imagined environmental issues as global. When environmental organizations wanted to prove that they were tapped into transnational networks, they mentioned global climate change. Government officials and businesses pointed to global climate change to index the common problems of the world. One kind of globality, or at least multilocality, of climate change, then, is its multiple referencing by groups in varied social and physical locations.

原页 101

20世纪90年代，当环保主义者和感兴趣的公众把环境问题想象为全球性时，全球气候变化是他们思考的中心。当环保组织想证明自己接入了跨国网络时，他们就提到全球气候变化。政府官员和商界指出全球气候变化来标示世界的共同问题。因此，气候变化的一种全球性，或至少是多地方性，就是不同社会和自然位置的群体对它的多重指涉。

原页 101, 102

Climate change seemed “global” to the public, too, because the issue was introduced during a period of concern about transboundary environmental issues: species loss, water pollution, acid rain, radioactivity. In the United States, a hot, dry summer in 1988 corresponded to the peak of public concern about the destruction of the rainforests in Amazonia. The emission of greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide and other gases whose increase in concentration is causing global warming) linked the U.S. climate and the loss of the Brazilian forest. The world was losing the carbon sink of the forests, while the burning of the forests produced more greenhouse gases. The idea of global climate change articulated the new realization that places far apart from each other were still connected for their basic survival, especially through the circulation of air and water.

原页 101, 102

气候变化在公众看来也显得“全球”，因为这个问题是在人们对跨境环境问题——物种丧失、水污染、酸雨、放射性——关切的时期被引入的。在美国，1988年一个炎热干燥的夏天正好对应公众对亚马孙雨林破坏关切的顶峰。温室气体（二氧化碳和其他浓度增加导致全球变暖的气体）的排放把美国的气候与巴西森林的丧失联系起来。世界正在失去森林的碳汇，而森林燃烧又产生更多温室气体。全球气候变化的想法阐明了新的认识：相隔遥远的地方仍然因基本生存而相互连接，尤其是通过空气和水的循环。

原页 102

The most easily identified “globality” of this realization, however, has been in the model that climate experts promoted to explain and predict climate change. General Circulation Models (GCM) use the laws of circulation of air and water to generate an abstraction we might call global climate. These models are self-conscious representations. They do not purport to describe the globe but rather to picture it in the model. They simplify and reduce the social and natural world to geophysical laws. In the process, they develop a globe that is unified, neutral, and understandable through the collection and manipulation of information.11

原页 102

然而，这一认识最容易识别的“全球性”出现在气候专家为解释和预测气候变化而推广的模型中。大气环流模型（GCM）运用空气和水的环流定律，生成一种我们可以称为全球气候的抽象。这些模型是自觉的表征。它们并非意在描述地球，而是在模型中描绘它。它们把社会和自然世界简化并还原为地球物理定律。在此过程中，它们通过信息的收集与操作，发展出一个统一、中立、可理解的地球。11

原页 102

This is a specific—even a peculiar—kind of globe. The global scale is privileged above all others. In contrast to Linnean plant classification or Muir-inspired nature appreciation, the global scale is the locus of prediction as well as understanding. Local conditions can be predicted from the global model; that is the point of its globality. Local data may adjust the global model but never defy it. Its globality is all-embracing.

原页 102

这是一种特定的——甚至奇特的——地球。全球尺度被赋予高于所有其他尺度的特权。与林奈植物分类或缪尔启发的自然欣赏相比，全球尺度既是理解也是预测的所在。地方条件可以从全球模型中被预测；这就是其全球性的要点。地方数据可以调整全球模型，但绝不能违抗它。它的全球性是包罗万象的。

原页 102

The model declares itself continually to be science. It is expert, neutral, rational, and empirically grounded. We know this, in part, because the model is complex and constantly under revision. It requires the computational prowess of computers because it integrates many factors. It admits to many uncertainties. Because of all the uncertainties integrated into it, using it requires great skill. Experts must train as part of a “community” of model users; they must develop common standards and trust. They should also communicate with the public. Experts use the models to tell the public about risks; public representatives can then debate what to do about these risks. “Uncertainties,” “trust,” “risk”: These terms circle in the model’s orbit. Through them, the model both secures its place as science and stimulates debate. The model unleashes its own dangers: This is its goal. Neither botanists nor nature lovers have used globality to push potential collaborators to the negotiating table, but climate modelers do just that.

原页 102

模型不断宣称自己是科学。它是专家的、中立的、理性的、以经验为基础的。我们知道这一点，部分是因为模型复杂且不断修订。它需要计算机的计算能力，因为它整合许多因素。它承认许多不确定性。由于其中整合了所有不确定性，使用它需要高超技巧。专家必须在模型使用者“共同体”中接受训练；他们必须发展共同标准与信任。他们还应该与公众沟通。专家用模型告诉公众风险；公众代表随后可以辩论如何应对这些风险。“不确定性”、“信任”、“风险”：这些术语在模型的轨道上循环。通过它们，模型既确保自己作为科学的地位，又激发辩论。模型释放自己的危险：这是它的目标。植物学家和自然爱好者都没有利用全球性把潜在合作者推到谈判桌前，但气候建模者正是这么做的。

原页 102, 103

, It is my contention that the global commitments of the model are strategic: They are tuned to stimulate international dialogue. They also cover up dialogue through reference to the unified globe of the model. Modelbuilding practitioners are self-conscious about the effects of their models on policy makers and the public. They want to create collaborations, and they know what kind they want. They want their models to show the way to global standards and structures of management. Their models show that only such standards and structures will promote survival. The modelmakers want to bring policy makers into the modeling effort. They want policy makers to be future-oriented global citizens. The model is an attempt to make this happen by denying pre-existing interests and identities—and thus the necessity of negotiation within the collaborations they endorse. The global unit supercedes nations, classes, cultures, or specific business interests. The model’s generalizations promote negotiation by making its necessity disappear into a seamless globe.

原页 102, 103

我认为模型的全球承诺是战略性的：它们被调校以刺激国际对话。它们也通过指向模型的统一地球来掩盖对话。模型建造实践者自觉关注模型对政策制定者和公众的影响。他们想创造合作，而且知道自己想要哪种合作。他们希望模型为全球标准和管理结构指明道路。他们的模型表明，只有这样的标准和结构才能促进生存。模型制造者想把政策制定者带入建模努力。他们希望政策制定者成为面向未来的全球公民。模型是一种尝试，通过否认既有的利益与身份——从而否认他们所认可的合作中协商的必要性——来实现这一点。全球这一单位超越国家、阶级、文化或特定商业利益。模型的概括促进协商，办法是让协商的必要性消失在一个无缝的地球中。

原页 103

The models incorporate strategy through the forms of global Nature they delineate. To see this, it is useful to examine the culture of modelers. First impressions, imbued with the shock of cultural difference, can perhaps convey this culture’s strangeness and specificity. I offer an ethnographic arrival story.

原页 103

模型通过它们描绘的全球自然形式纳入战略。要看到这一点，考察建模者的文化是有用的。第一印象带着文化差异的冲击，也许能传达这种文化的陌生性与特殊性。我提供一个民族志抵达故事。

原页 103

I had my first taste of global climate models, and their makers, at the “First Open Meeting of the Human Dimensions of Global Environmental Change Community” in 1995 at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina. This was a very specific segment of the “community”: the meeting was organized by political scientists, who have their own global agendas; the modelers present were those most interested in socioeconomic rather than geophysical data. Yet if I ignore the political science and focus on the surprises of my first impressions of modeling, I can introduce some recurrent cultural features.

原页 103

1995年，在北卡罗来纳州达勒姆的杜克大学，“全球环境变化人文维度共同体第一次公开会议”上，我第一次体验全球气候模型及其制造者。这是“共同体”中一个非常特定的部分：会议由政治学家组织，他们有自己的全球议程；到场的建模者是对社会经济数据而非地球物理数据最感兴趣的那些人。然而，如果我忽略政治学，专注于我对建模第一印象中的惊讶，我就可以介绍一些反复出现的文化特征。

原页 103

For me, everything seemed exotic: the incessant clicking of laptops in the lecture halls; the parade of computer projections; the use of acronyms; the programmatic nature of much of the research, in which results were just an example of potential. It seemed that U.S. modelers wore dark, drab suits and armed themselves with piles of overheads, while Europeans wore bright jackets and flamboyant ties and spoke of creativity and culture. Women appeared as representatives of official organizations; they hid behind charts. Used to the informality of scholars who imagine themselves as of little public importance, I could tell I had entered an unfamiliar scene of action and effectiveness. Details of dress and presentation were geared for particular policy audiences. More so the models, which, through the ways they surprised me, instructed me in fundamentals.

原页 103

对我来说，一切似乎都很陌生：演讲厅里笔记本电脑不停的点击声；接连不断的电脑投影演示；缩略词的使用；许多研究的纲领性，其中结果只是潜力的一例。美国建模者似乎穿着深色、单调的西装，带着成堆的幻灯片；欧洲人则穿着鲜艳的夹克和浮夸的领带，谈论创造力和文化。女性作为官方组织的代表出现；她们躲在图表后面。我习惯了那些自认为无足轻重的学者的随和，因此我能看出自己进入了一个陌生的行动与效力场景。衣着和展示的细节是为特定政策受众调校的。模型更是如此，它们通过让我惊讶的方式，教给我基本的东西。

原页 103, 104

I recall my first surprise: The global scale takes precedence—because it is the scale of the model. A geographer showed us how to use climate models for social science research. We needed to understand the procedures for “downscaling” from the global model to predict local environmental impacts. He used his computer to demonstrate for us how to predict the weather in one Swiss canton two hundred years in the future.

原页 103, 104

我记得第一个惊讶：全球尺度优先——因为它是模型的尺度。一位地理学家向我们展示如何把气候模型用于社会科学研究。我们需要理解从全球模型“降尺度”以预测地方环境影响的程序。他用电脑向我们演示如何预测瑞士一个州两百年后的天气。

原页 104

At first, I was just shocked by the temerity of predicting the local from the global. What happened to the social and natural landscape of that canton? Could it mean nothing? Then I did see that his demonstration was not just a direct downscaling. One can “nest” a limited-area atmospheric model within the global climate model, thus including a certain amount of local information. Smaller scale information can be incorporated in global climate models in a number of ways. “Parameters” are introduced into the global model from regional and local empirical studies; these keep the model closer to accepted descriptions of reality. Model users may add data from other sources to create regional and landscape scale predictions. There is considerable interest in “meso-scale” modeling. Finally, there is much discussion among modelers about problems of scale. In a special issue of Science on global environmental problems, for example, two scientists argue that neither “scale-up” nor “scale-down” research paradigms can provide reliable ecological assessments. They advocate “strategic cyclical scaling,” which integrates regional and local empirical data into global models, correcting global projections with the results of smaller-scale monitoring and evaluation of actual effects (Root and Schneider 1995).

原页 104

起初，我只是震惊于从全球预测地方的胆大妄为。那个州的社会与自然地景怎么了？它可以毫无意义吗？然后我确实看到，他的演示不只是直接降尺度。人们可以在全球气候模型中“嵌套”一个有限区域大气模型，从而纳入一定量的地方信息。较小尺度的信息可以通过多种方式纳入全球气候模型。区域和地方经验研究把“参数”引入全球模型；这些使模型更接近被接受的对现实的描述。模型使用者可以加入其他来源的数据，以创建区域和地景尺度的预测。“中尺度”建模受到相当关注。最后，建模者之间关于尺度问题有许多讨论。例如，在《科学》关于全球环境问题的特刊中，两位科学家论证，“放大”和“缩小”研究范式都不能提供可靠的生态评估。他们提倡“战略性循环缩放”，把区域和地方经验数据整合进全球模型，用较小尺度监测和实际效果评估的结果来校正全球预测（Root and Schneider 1995）。

原页 104

Within these nuances, a set of assumptions about scale remains. Scales ought to fit neatly inside each other, the small inside the large, each neutral and fully encompassed by the next scale up. If they don’t, we must fiddle, looking for a more realistic fit. The incompatibility of scales is a practical problem. It does not challenge the principles of the model, which requires that the local disappear compatibly inside the global.

原页 104

在这些细微差别中，一套关于尺度的假设仍然存在。尺度应该整齐地相互嵌套，小的在大的里面，每一个都是中立的，并被上一级尺度完全包含。如果不是，我们必须摆弄，寻找更现实的契合。尺度的不相容是一个实际问题。它并不挑战模型的原则，而模型要求地方以相容的方式消失在全球之中。

原页 104

My second surprise: Models breed more models. One man lectured on the modeling of uncertainty. It was one of the more unusual kinds of social science I had seen. He discussed, for example, the degree of trust that different climate scientists had in the global climate model, based on a survey. He then correlated their trust with personal characteristics, such as whether they smoked. I thought at first it was a joke, but I hadn’t been around the discussion of uncertainty, or modeling. Models are made more reliable by incorporating uncertainties into the model, that is, by modeling them.

原页 104

我的第二个惊讶：模型繁殖更多模型。一位男士就不确定性建模作演讲。这是我见过的最不寻常的社会科学之一。例如，他根据一项调查讨论了不同气候科学家对全球气候模型的信任程度。然后他把他们的信任与个人特征相关联，比如是否吸烟。起初我以为这是个玩笑，但我此前没有接触过关于不确定性或建模的讨论。通过把不确定性纳入模型，也就是通过为它们建模，模型变得更加可靠。

原页 104, 105

Since the emergence of global climate models, much concern has been expressed about the fact that the GCM does not include social information: The world is reduced to physical laws. Modelers have responded by developing more extensive models that incorporate everything. This is called integrated assessment (IA), and it requires combining rather different kinds of models. Social features of the globe are usually modeled using systems dynamics models, which are then combined with geophysical circulation models. Other kinds of modeling may be brought in as well. Since it is not clear how to do this, many forms of integrated assessment compete for attention. Everyone wants to include population and land use, but there are many other categories; some have even tried adding “culture” to that which can be modeled. The common assumption is that everything can be quantified and located as an element of a system of feedback and flow. “Uncertainties” pile up. One IA project admits, “In view of the accumulation of uncertainties, the interpretative and instructive value of the... model is far more important than its predictive capacity, which is limited by the incomplete science upon which it is constructed” (Rotmans 1995b: 3). Is modeling a teaching practice or a predictive science?

原页 104, 105

自全球气候模型出现以来，人们一直对大气环流模型不包括社会信息这一事实表示关切：世界被还原为物理定律。建模者的回应是开发纳入一切的更广泛模型。这被称为综合评估（IA），它需要结合相当不同的模型。地球的社会特征通常使用系统动力学模型建模，然后与地球物理环流模型结合。其他类型的建模也可能被引入。由于如何做到这一点并不清楚，许多综合评估形式争夺注意力。每个人都想纳入人口和土地利用，但还有许多其他范畴；有些人甚至尝试把“文化”加入可建模之物。共同的假设是，一切都可以被量化并定位为反馈与流动系统的一个要素。“不确定性”堆积起来。一个IA项目承认：“鉴于不确定性的累积，……模型的解释和教育价值远远重要于其预测能力，而预测能力受制于其构建所依据的不完整科学”（Rotmans 1995b: 3）。建模是一种教学实践还是预测科学？

原页 105

Another surprise: Models must be charismatic and pedagogical. One modeler compared the success of European modeling with the failures of U.S. counterparts. He explained that the first success of climate modeling in Europe occurred as a result of concerns over acid rain. The European Union was just emerging, with transboundary issues as its reason to exist. The modelers brought policy makers from the EU into their modeling efforts. They let them design simulations. The policy makers became involved; they integrated the models into their positions. In contrast, he argued, U.S. modelers have had much less success. Their models are too complex and too academic; policy makers aren’t attracted to them. Modeling, he argued, is a tool, not a declaration of truth.

原页 105

另一个惊讶：模型必须具有感召力和教育性。一位建模者比较了欧洲建模的成功与美国同行的失败。他解释说，欧洲气候建模的首次成功源于对酸雨的关切。欧盟刚刚兴起，跨境问题是其存在的理由。建模者把欧盟的政策制定者带入建模努力。他们让政策制定者设计模拟。政策制定者参与进来；他们把模型整合进自己的立场。相反，他认为，美国建模者的成功少得多。他们的模型太复杂、太学术；政策制定者不被吸引。他说，建模是一种工具，不是真理的宣告。

原页 105

The embedding of smaller scales into the global; the enlargement of models to include everything; the policy-driven construction of the models: Together, these features make it possible that models can bring diplomats to the negotiating table. Indeed, the models have helped stimulate negotiations, as in Rio in 1992 and in Kyoto in 1997. Yet, rather than the consensus that modelers hoped for, these negotiations have been arenas of conflict. Two conflicts have dominated the field: differences between representatives of the global north and south, and differences between the United States and Europe. The former takes the unified globe of the models apart, dividing it into sectors with dissimilar interests. The latter disputes environmental science, arguing for other forms of knowledge. Each reveals the collaborative structure of modeling through claims of being excluded.

原页 105

把较小尺度嵌入全球；扩大模型以包含一切；政策驱动的模型建构：这些特征合在一起，使模型有可能把外交官带到谈判桌前。的确，模型帮助刺激了谈判，如1992年里约和1997年京都。然而，谈判并没有形成建模者希望的共识，反而成了冲突的场域。两种冲突主导了这一领域：全球北方与南方代表之间的差异，以及美国与欧洲之间的差异。前者把模型的统一地球拆开，划分为利益不同的部分。后者质疑环境科学，主张其他形式的知识。每一种冲突都通过被排斥的主张，揭示了建模的合作结构。

原页 105, 106

Spokespeople for the global south argue that global climate models are an articulation of northern interests. Global climate models show everyone invested in the same reductions of greenhouse gases; they cover up the fact that most of these gases are emitted in northern countries. In blaming southern countries for a share of the greenhouse gas problem, the models also obscure differences between northern and southern emissions. Many greenhouse gases emitted in southern countries are “subsistence emissions,” in contrast to the “luxury emissions” of northern countries. Global modeling, they imply, is not neutral but rather positioned with those wealthy nations who can cut emissions—but want others to help them. In international negotiations before the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, this argument was convincing enough to be incorporated into the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.12

原页 105, 106

全球南方的发言者主张，全球气候模型是北方利益的接合。全球气候模型表明每个人都投入于同样的温室气体减排；它们掩盖了大部分这些气体在北方国家排放的事实。在把温室气体问题的一部分归咎于南方国家时，模型也模糊了北方与南方排放之间的差异。南方国家排放的许多温室气体是“生存排放”，与北方国家的“奢侈排放”相对。他们暗示，全球建模并非中立，而是站在那些能够减排——但想让别人帮忙——的富裕国家一边。在1992年里约地球峰会之前的国际谈判中，这一论点足够有说服力，被纳入《联合国气候变化框架公约》。12

原页 106

This north-south separation was one reason anti-environmental politicians in the United States criticized climate change negotiations, and, in the face of international disapproval, withdrew from the Kyoto Protocol in 2001. U.S. politicians have advocated a different form of universals through which they imagine the globe: private property, free trade, and the entrepreneurial spirit. U.S. negotiators had already done their best to bring these business-oriented perspectives into discussions of climate change.13 Yet the models of global change that informed climate negotiations still privileged the environment for itself. These environmental universals had not won over U.S. politics.

校注10
原页 106

这种南北分离是美国反环境政治家批评气候变化谈判的原因之一，并且在国际反对声中，他们于2001年退出了《京都议定书》。美国政治家提倡一种不同的普遍性形式，借以想象地球：私有财产、自由贸易和企业家精神。美国谈判代表已经尽力把这些商业导向的视角带入气候变化讨论。13然而，为气候谈判提供信息的全球变化模型仍然为环境本身赋予特权。这些环境普遍性没有赢得美国政界的支持。

校注10
原页 106

U.S. intransigence warns us against the glorification of incompatibility; when claims of difference are combined with unilateral power, they can be ugly. Whereas representatives of the south asked for revisions of the model, the most powerful nation of the north merely refused to discuss it. Powerful blocs have worked hard to stop global agreements based on international cooperation and amity. The expertise of modelers has formed defensive walls against such power plays, but generalizations more directly dependent on international politics have had fewer defenses.

原页 106

美国的不妥协警告我们不要美化不相容性；当差异的主张与单边权力结合时，它们可能很丑陋。南方代表要求修订模型，而北方最强大的国家只是拒绝讨论它。强大的集团努力阻止基于国际合作与友好的全球协议。建模者的专业知识形成了抵御这种权力游戏的防御墙，但更直接依赖国际政治的概括防御更少。

原页 106

The recognition of environmental crisis has brought nations to the negotiating table to talk about a variety of universal standards. But not all negotiations result in effective generalization. Negotiators must agree upon common objects. As long as they refuse all compatibility, generalization is impossible. The troubled progress of international negotiations illuminates the specificity of the generalization process, in which productive collaborations and sincerely endorsed axioms of unity are not easy achievements. I turn to these troubles.

原页 106

对环境危机的认识把各国带到谈判桌前，讨论各种普遍标准。但并非所有谈判都能产生有效的概括。谈判者必须就共同对象达成一致。只要他们拒绝一切相容性，概括就不可能。国际谈判的艰难进展阐明了概括过程的特殊性，在其中，富有成效的合作与真诚认可的统一公理都不是容易的成就。我转向这些困难。

原页 106

A Universal Regime?

原页 106

一种普遍性体制？

原页 106

The ITTO’s underlying concept is to sustainable development of tropical forests by encouraging and assisting the tropical timber industry and trade to manage and thus conserve the resource base on which they depend.

原页 106

ITTO的基本理念，是通过鼓励并协助热带木材产业与贸易部门管理并进而保护它们所依赖的资源基础，实现热带森林的可持续发展。

原页 106

—International Tropical Timber Organization, “What Is the International Tropical Timber Agreement?”

原页 106

——国际热带木材组织，《什么是国际热带木材协定？》（“What Is the International Tropical Timber Agreement?”）

原页 107

The combination of trade promotion and conservation is a heady brew for international politics. Nowhere has this been more important than in the International Tropical Timber Organization, better known as the ITTO. With this combination brewing, the dream of a global management regime was born. Could forest protectors and exploiters, and wood producers and consumers, come together to form universal standards, governance procedures, and expectations about the use of forests?14

原页 107

贸易促进与保护的结合，对国际政治是一杯烈酒。这种结合在国际热带木材组织（以简称ITTO更为人熟知）中尤为重要。随着这种结合开始酿制，全球管理制度之梦诞生了。森林保护者与开发者、木材生产者与消费者，能否走到一起，形成关于森林使用的普遍标准、治理程序和期望？14

原页 107

The ITTO’s hopes for forming universal standards came to life around the concept of “sustainable forest management.” Sustainable management emerged at the intersection of varied concerns about “protection”: of wood supplies for consumer industry; of state forestry institutions; of wood prices for timber companies; of the reputation of the forest-products trade; and, of course, of forests themselves. Sustainable management showed the potential to reshape conservation, trade, forestry, and industry, so that they formed a common trajectory in a commitment to a managed global Nature. Sustainable management could be the cornerstone of a new governmentality. Yet the most exciting thing about the ITTO turned out to be its failure. Everyone saw quickly that “sustainable management” was an empty concept. The ITTO stayed on, but the action, emerging from other sites, swirled around it. The ITTO took up the defensive role of managing participants’ agendas in the light of what was happening elsewhere.

原页 107

ITTO形成普遍标准的希望围绕“可持续森林管理”概念而活跃起来。可持续管理出现在各种“保护”关切的交汇处：为消费产业保护木材供应；保护国家林业机构；为木材公司保护木材价格；为林产品贸易保护声誉；当然也保护森林本身。可持续管理显示出重塑保护、贸易、林业和工业的潜力，使它们在对被管理的全球自然的承诺中形成共同轨迹。可持续管理可以成为新治理术的基石。然而，ITTO最令人兴奋的事结果却是它的失败。大家很快看出，“可持续管理”是一个空洞的概念。ITTO留了下来，但来自其他场所的行动围绕它旋转。ITTO承担起防御性角色，根据别处正在发生的事情管理参与者的议程。

原页 107

This section, then, turns from relatively successful agendas for global Nature to consider a relatively unsuccessful one. A coalition politics continues to sustain the ITTO, but it is not a coalition that has forged effective collaborations. Some participants hang in, hoping to exert influence on other players and on international programs. They advocate global accord for the name, not the substance; they are most involved in their separate mandates. In their still-strident efforts, global Nature stutters, and falls silent. Why?

原页 107

因此，本节从相对成功的全球自然议程转向一个相对不成功的议程。联盟政治继续维持ITTO，但它并不是一个锻造了有效合作的联盟。一些参与者坚持留下，希望对其他行动者和国际项目施加影响。他们倡导全球协议是为了名义，而不是实质；他们最投入于各自的职责目标。在他们仍然尖锐的努力中，全球自然结结巴巴，然后沉默。为什么？

原页 107, 108

The ITTO was imagined as a forum in which compromises might bridge disagreements among dissimilar parties. Even while claiming to search for common ground, the organization worked assiduously to maintain these globe-ripping divides. The ITTO began as a Japanese dream, suggested to the UN Conference on Trade and Development in 1977. The Japanese representatives said they were concerned about the stability of the tropical timber trade, for which Japan was the most prominent consumer. Conservationists and foresters had pointed to evidence of rapid deforestation; supplies in key Japanese source areas, such as the Philippines, were already running out. The Japanese plan blocked other possibilities. Sporadic discussions among tropical wood producing countries had generated speculation that a cartel might form to influence supply and pricing. It also seemed possible that conservationists, concerned about the rapid loss of tropical forests, might themselves succeed in forming international forestry standards. In either case, Japan's business profits would suffer. These concerns informed several years of discussion of the proposal. In 1983, an International Tropical Timber Agreement (ITTA) was signed, to take effect in 1985. The agreement formalized the dialogue between tropical wood producing countries and consuming countries. It included conservation as well as trade promotion goals. The agreement also formed the ITTO.

原页 107, 108

ITTO被想象成一个论坛，在其中妥协也许能弥合不同各方之间的分歧。即使在声称寻找共同基础时，该组织也努力维持这些撕裂地球的分歧。ITTO最初是一个日本梦想，于1977年向联合国贸易和发展会议提出。日本代表说，他们担心热带木材贸易的稳定，日本是其中最突出的消费国。环保主义者和林业工作者已经指出快速毁林的证据；日本关键来源地区如菲律宾的供应已日渐枯竭。日本的计划阻止了其他可能性。热带木材生产国之间零星的讨论引发了猜测：可能形成一个卡特尔来影响供应和定价。似乎也有可能的是，担心热带森林迅速丧失的环保主义者自己可能成功形成国际林业标准。无论哪种情况，日本的商业利润都会受损。这些关切为几年间对该提案的讨论提供了信息。1983年，《国际热带木材协定》（ITTA）签署，1985年生效。该协定正式确立了热带木材生产国和消费国之间的对话。它包括保护目标，也包括贸易促进目标。该协定还成立了ITTO。

原页 108

Bureaucratic structure seems cut and dry; but much agonizing and struggle went into settling the structure of the ITTO. Who would participate? What global, national, or business commitments would dominate the agenda? These were questions hammered out in the organizational structure. The ITTA made a start. The organization would be divided into moities, consisting of representatives of nation-states, and identified respectively as “producers” and “consumers”—thus assuring that the ITTO would function neither as a price-setting cartel nor as a forum for global citizens. Votes were to be distributed in proportion to a nation-state’s “involvement” with the tropical timber trade; countries that either bought or sold more tropical wood received more votes. As one critic points out: “The net result is that the more a country destroys tropical forests, the more votes it gets. The voting structure ensures that the ITTO’s primary role of promoting the timber trade heavily outweighs its secondary conservation role” (Colchester 1990: 167).

These arrangements meant that the struggle over the organization’s goals was played out in relation to the representation of different countries. Forest conservation objectives became identified with countries such as the United Kingdom and the Netherlands; the voice of the wood-products industry was heard from Japan; the defense of national sovereignty and rights to destroy the forests became identified with Indonesia and Malaysia. Thus, too, the struggle over which nation would supply the Executive Director and where the secretariat would be seated was a struggle over organizational definition. The battle was heated. Finally, the Japanese government offered to fund the ITTO in exchange for gaining the secretariat. Japanese support then boosted a Malaysian forester, Dr. Freezailah, to the post of Executive Director (Colchester 1990).

原页 108

官僚结构似乎明确而固定；但为了确定ITTO的结构，经历了大量痛苦与斗争。谁将参与？哪些全球、国家或商业承诺将主导议程？这些都是在组织结构中锤炼出来的问题。ITTA开了一个头。组织将分为两部分，由民族国家代表组成，分别称为“生产者”和“消费者”——从而确保ITTO既不会作为定价卡特尔运作，也不会作为全球公民的论坛。选票将按民族国家与热带木材贸易的“参与程度”比例分配；买卖更多热带木材的国家获得更多选票。正如一位批评者指出：“净结果是，一个国家破坏热带森林越多，它获得的选票就越多。投票结构确保ITTO促进木材贸易的主要角色大大超过其次要的保护角色”（Colchester 1990: 167）。

这些安排意味着，围绕组织目标的斗争是在不同国家的代表权关系中展开的。森林保护目标与英国、荷兰等国联系在一起；木制品产业的声音从日本发出；捍卫国家主权和毁林权的声音则与印尼和马来西亚联系在一起。因此，围绕哪个国家提供执行主任、秘书处设在哪里的斗争，也是一场关于组织定义的斗争。这场战斗很激烈。最后，日本政府提出资助ITTO以换取秘书处。日本的支持随后把马来西亚林业官员弗里扎伊拉博士推上执行主任的位置（Colchester 1990）。

原页 108, 109

Despite this alignment of Japanese and Malaysian interests in rapid timber exploitation, conservationists hung on. Getting forest conservation goals into a mandate that had begun as a trade agreement was a victory; they were not about to retreat. For nongovernmental organizations, the goal of participating at all in ITTO negotiations seemed overwhelmingly important. In Indonesia, for example, environmental NGOs were just then struggling for a voice in the nation—in the legal system, in forestry, and in public culture. Indonesia was a major player in the ITTO, and NGOs wanted to be involved.15

原页 108, 109

尽管日本和马来西亚在快速木材开发上的利益如此一致，自然保护者仍坚持下来。把森林保护目标纳入一项最初作为贸易协定的授权，是一场胜利；他们不打算撤退。对非政府组织来说，能够参与ITTO谈判似乎极其重要。例如，在印尼，环境非政府组织当时正努力在国家中获得发言权——在法律系统、林业和公共文化中。印尼是ITTO的主要参与者，非政府组织想要参与。15

原页 109

In other arenas—including global climate change—agreement among experts has sparked intergovernmental cooperation. Not so for forest protection. Experts are differently aligned. Foresters have been trained to work with the timber industry, not the environmental movement; in contrast, conservation biologists, often spokespersons for environmentalism, may oppose logging. Anthropologists, who may speak up for forest-dwelling peoples, are rarely given credence by either foresters or biologists. Economists are given much credence although they may know nothing about forests. Agendas for forest management thus multiply. Most experts adopt a rhetoric of concern for forests, whether they propose to stay or hasten their disappearance. The 1992 UN Earth Summit at Rio produced a set of principles on forests that affirm state sovereignty and promote free trade; what does this have to do with forest protection?16 Thus, too, the ITTO combines and juxtaposes agendas that, everyone admits, contradict each other.

原页 109

在其他领域——包括全球气候变化——专家之间的一致引发了政府间合作。森林保护则不是这样。专家的阵营不同。林业工作者受训与木材产业合作，而不是与环境运动合作；相比之下，保护生物学家常常是环保主义的代言人，可能反对伐木。人类学家可能为森林居民发声，却很少得到林业工作者或生物学家的信任。经济学家得到很多信任，尽管他们可能对森林一无所知。因此，森林管理的议程成倍增加。大多数专家都采用关心森林的修辞，无论他们主张遏止还是加速森林的消失。1992年里约联合国地球峰会产出了一套关于森林的原则，肯定国家主权并促进自由贸易；这与森林保护有什么关系？16因此，ITTO也把大家都承认相互矛盾的议程结合并并置在一起。

原页 109

Sustainable management holds the mix together. But it is not enough. The ITTO promotes sustainable management of forests. But, given the selfconscious reliance on contradictory programs, it is difficult for the organization to define the term substantively. Here is the organization’s formal definition:

原页 109

可持续管理把这种混合维系在一起。但这还不够。ITTO促进森林的可持续管理。然而，鉴于自觉依赖相互矛盾的项目，该组织很难实质性定义这个术语。以下是该组织的正式定义：

原页 109

Sustainable forest management is the process of managing forest to achieve one or more clearly specified objectives of management with regard to the production of a continuous flow of desired forest products and services without undue reduction of the inherent values and future productivity and without undue undesirable effects on the physical and social environment.17

原页 109

可持续森林管理是管理森林的过程，以达到一个或多个明确规定的管理目标，涉及持续产生所需的森林产品和服务，同时不过度减少固有价值和未来生产力，也不对物理和社会环境产生过度的不良影响。17

原页 109

This is obviously a compromise between sustainable yield—the foresters’ dream of stable timber production (“a continuous flow of desired forest products”)—and sustainable ecological function—the environmentalists’ goal (“inherent values,” “undesirable effects”). The product is almost incomprehensible. Furthermore, no one knows how to do it. No one, even industry experts, thinks that current tropical logging techniques are allowing the forest to regenerate—even for timber.

原页 109

这显然是可持续产量——林业工作者稳定木材生产的梦想（“持续产生所需的森林产品”）——与可持续生态功能——环保主义者的目标（“固有价值”、“不良影响”）——之间的妥协。产物几乎无法理解。此外，没有人知道如何做到。没有人，甚至行业专家，认为当前的热带伐木技术能让森林再生——即使是为了木材。

原页 109, 110

Two paths present themselves as ways out of this conundrum. One could use the term as public relations rhetoric to defend the reputation of current logging practices, taking them out of the opprobrium of environmentalist criticism. The advantage here is that it doesn’t matter if the definition is incomprehensible. Alternatively, one could focus on management itself as the true objective. By rationalizing data collection and bureaucratic structures for forestry while at the same time highlighting technical training, one might achieve some goals, even if they might not be forest protection ones. After all, the definition says that sustainable management is meeting the specified objectives of management. It is management itself that must be sustainable. The ITTO has worked back and forth between these two paths.

原页 109, 110

有两条路径可以摆脱这个难题。人们可以把该术语用作公共关系的修辞，以捍卫当前伐木实践的声誉，使其免受环保主义批评的责难。这样做的好处是，定义是否不可理解并不重要。或者，人们可以专注于管理本身作为真正目标。通过使林业的数据收集和官僚结构合理化，同时突出技术培训，人们可能实现某些目标，即使这些目标可能不是森林保护的目标。毕竟，定义说可持续管理就是达到规定的管理目标。必须可持续的是管理本身。ITTO在这两条路径之间来回工作。

原页 110

Throughout the 1990s, the highest profile program of the ITTO was the “Year 2000 Objective,” the promise to limit trade in tropical timber to supplies from sustainably managed forests by the year 2000. The promise was passed as a producer-countries’ resolution in 1991, with participating environmental organizations, and even some representatives from consumer countries, bewildered about just what this promise meant. The first possibility that occurred to critics is that the promise meant nothing at all: “In fact, ‘Target 2000’ will present the timber industry with few difficulties, for, according to the rhetoric of the producers and traders, logging as practiced already is sustainable” (Colchester 1990: 169). As 2000 approached, the organization began to suggest that the Year 2000 Objective was rhetoric: “The . . . ITTO has done more in the 15 years of its existence than any other organization to advance the idea of sustainable tropical forest management” (ITTO 2000). Spreading the idea of sustainable management is enough.

校注13
原页 110

整个20世纪90年代，ITTO最引人注目的项目是“2000年目标”，即承诺到2000年把热带木材贸易限制在来自可持续管理森林的供应。这项承诺于1991年作为生产国决议通过，参与的环境组织甚至一些消费国代表都困惑于这项承诺究竟意味着什么。批评者想到的第一种可能性是，这项承诺根本没有任何意义：“事实上，‘2000年目标’不会给木材产业带来多少困难，因为根据生产者和贸易者的修辞，目前实行的伐木已经是可持续的”（Colchester 1990: 169）。随着2000年临近，该组织开始暗示2000年目标是修辞：“……ITTO在其存在的15年中，在推进可持续热带森林管理理念方面所做的比任何其他组织都多”（ITTO 2000）。传播可持续管理的理念就够了。

校注13
原页 110

Meanwhile, the organization sponsored a variety of technical studies and data collection exercises, some of which might lead to more, if not better, management. Guidebooks for standards of forestry are being published. “Reduced impact logging” offers the solution of managing timber industry workers to address the problem of logging’s destructive impact. Other ITTO grants sponsor studies of illegal logging—one of the few evils on which state bureaucracies, the timber industry, and tree-counting conservationists can agree. These activities advance the bureaucratic ideal; however, little effort has gone into addressing the problems of legal logging, the loss of local livelihoods, and the opening of forests to destructive forms of settlement and mining. The technical solutions of ITTO programs do not address either ecological or social questions. Sustainable forestry management is self-contained—an “anti-politics machine” that converts social issues into technical ones.18

原页 110

与此同时，该组织赞助了各种技术研究和数据收集活动，其中一些可能带来更多的管理，即便未必是更好的管理。林业标准指南正在出版。“减少影响伐木”提供了管理木材产业工人以解决伐木破坏性影响的方案。其他ITTO资助项目赞助非法伐木研究——这是国家官僚机构、木材产业和数树的自然保护者能够达成一致的少数恶行之一。这些活动推进了官僚理想；然而，几乎没有努力解决合法伐木、地方生计丧失以及森林向破坏性定居和采矿形式开放的问题。ITTO项目的技术解决方案既不解决生态问题，也不解决社会问题。可持续林业管理是自足的——一台把社会问题转化为技术问题的“反政治机器”。18

原页 110, 111

The machine asserts its globality mainly as a rampart against attacks from other transnational sources. The ITTO's major activity has involved neutralizing other initiatives for tropical forest management. It has been particularly active against environmentalist initiatives, such as tropical wood boycotts to protest destructive logging. ITTO fought the concept of wood-products labeling as well as certification, which environmentalists proposed as a way of identifying better and worse timber sources. When it became clear that labeling and certification were ideas that would not go away, the ITTO then rushed in to create its own profit-friendly programs.19

原页 110, 111

这台机器主要作为抵御其他跨国来源攻击的壁垒来主张其全球性。ITTO的主要活动涉及抵消其他热带森林管理倡议。它特别积极地反对环保主义倡议，例如为抗议破坏性伐木而抵制热带木材。ITTO反对木制品标签和认证的概念，环保主义者提出这些作为识别木材来源好坏的方式。当标签和认证显然是不会消失的理念时，ITTO便冲进来创建自己的亲利润项目。19

原页 111

Meanwhile, the ITTO has taken a stand for particular governments against international pressure. In 1989, at the height of the international campaign against the logging of Sarawak, Malaysia, the ITTO sent an official mission to assess “the sustainable utilization and conservation of tropical forests” there (ITTO 1990: 2). The mission made no attempt to meet with indigenous protestors or environmentalist critics; instead it limited its vision to the formal aspects of forest management. “The mission inverts the priorities of Sarawak’s forest policy, putting the production of timber above local needs,” environmentalists proclaimed (Rowley 1990). Meanwhile, the Sarawak government touted the ITTO mission’s regard as an endorsement of its sustainable forest management.

原页 111

与此同时，ITTO为特定政府对抗国际压力站台。1989年，在反对马来西亚沙捞越伐木的国际运动高潮中，ITTO派官方代表团评估那里的“热带森林可持续利用与保护”（ITTO 1990: 2）。代表团没有尝试会见土著抗议者或环保主义批评者；相反，它把视野局限于森林管理的正式方面。“代表团颠倒了沙捞越森林政策的优先次序，把木材生产置于地方需要之上，”环保主义者宣称（Rowley 1990）。与此同时，沙捞越政府把ITTO代表团的关注标榜为对其可持续森林管理的认可。

原页 111

None of this is doing the tropical forests much good. The conditions of tropical forests have only deteriorated since the formation of the ITTO, and no amelioration seems in sight. Nor has there been much success in forming global accord. No mechanisms have been set for compliance with forestry standards, should meaningful standards be suggested. Everyone who knows about the problems of forestry on the ground—from local foresters, to residents, to spokespeople for wildlife—has been excluded. Practical forestry solutions would look quite different with their input.

原页 111

这些都没有给热带森林带来多少好处。自ITTO成立以来，热带森林的状况一直在恶化，似乎看不到改善的迹象。在形成全球协议方面也没有多少成功。如果有意义的标准被提出，也没有建立遵守林业标准的机制。所有了解实地林业问题的人——从地方林业工作者，到居民，到野生动物代言人——都被排除在外。如果有他们的投入，实际的林业解决方案会相当不同。

原页 111

These failures show the weakness of the process of generalization the ITTO put in motion. International cooperation did not prove a convincing axiom of unity. The ITTO’s retreat to technical rhetoric is an exemplar of the weakness of contemporary international politics in forging a “universal regime.” Yet, given its penchant for blocking more meaningful forest solutions, the organization’s ineffectiveness is perhaps its best quality.

原页 111

这些失败显示了ITTO启动的概括过程的弱点。国际合作没有被证明为令人信服的统一公理。ITTO退回到技术修辞，是当代国际政治在锻造“普遍性体制”方面软弱的一个例证。然而，鉴于它阻止更有意义的森林解决方案的倾向，该组织的无效性也许是它最好的品质。

原页 111

Nature and the Globe

Making the globe our frame of reference is hard work. This chapter has explored projects for making global commitments that rely on Nature as a set of universal, orderly, and inspiring laws. Looking at universals, I find that they include contrasting sources of knowledge and define varied kinds of participants in the knowledge-making process. Their quiet exclusions, and their heralded opponents, are equally varied. Yet they rely on a common process: Global Nature both facilitates and obscures worldwide collaborations.

原页 111

自然与地球

把地球作为我们的参照框架是艰苦的工作。本章探讨了依靠自然作为一套普遍、有序、鼓舞人心的法则来制造全球承诺的项目。考察普遍性，我发现它们包含不同的知识来源，并定义了知识制造过程中不同类型的参与者。它们不动声色的排斥，以及它们所宣告的对手，同样多种多样。然而它们依赖一个共同过程：全球自然既促进又掩盖世界范围的合作。

原页 111, 112

Nature offers various kinds of commitment to a global scale. Global Nature can collate facts from around the world. In forming a plant classification system, global Nature made the knowledge of varied localities compatible. It offered a universal system to bring together local knowledges. Global Nature can inspire moral views and actions. In nature appreciation and the parks model, localities are charged with global insight; they are microcosms of universal knowledge. Global Nature can also form a common object for the formation of international standards. In global climate models, the material primacy of the globe seen in the model can impel the urgency of international negotiation. And global Nature can facilitate governance regimes, making technical standardization an international imperative. The sustainably managed forests of the International Tropical Timber Organization are leaky boats for Nature. But, like the other projects introduced here, they are claims about Natural universals that make the globe the relevant forum.

原页 111, 112

自然为全球尺度提供各种承诺。全球自然可以整理来自世界各地的资料。在形成植物分类系统时，全球自然使各个地方的知识变得相容。它提供了一个普遍系统来汇集地方知识。全球自然可以激发道德观点和行动。在自然欣赏和公园模式中，地方被赋予全球洞见；它们是普遍知识的微观宇宙。全球自然也可以为国际标准的形成提供一个共同对象。在全球气候模型中，模型中看到的地球的物质首要性可以推动国际谈判的紧迫性。全球自然还可以促进治理体制，使技术标准化成为国际必需。国际热带木材组织可持续管理的森林，是为自然服务的漏船。但如同这里介绍的其他项目，它们是关于自然普遍性的主张，使地球成为相关论坛。

原页 112

These forms of global Nature are resources for everyone involved in using or advocating for the environment. They make it possible to make claims for Nature, and for the globe. The cultural specificity of their universals does not, in itself, make them wrong. However, claims of universality do make it hard for us to see just who can imagine themselves inside, and who is out.

原页 112

这些全球自然的形式，是所有参与使用或倡导环境的人的资源。它们使人有可能为自然、为地球提出主张。其普遍性的文化特殊性本身并不使它们错误。然而，普遍性的主张确实使我们难以看清：究竟谁能把自己想象在内，谁在外。

原页 112

The projects for making nature and scale that I describe in the rest of this book draw on these cultural resources. You will hear more about botanizing as a moment of cultural sharing, about nature loving in the legacy of Muir, about the dreams and models of environmental science, and about heated debates over the protection of tropical forests. These projects are deployed and transformed in varied social contexts—making and remaking the variety of small-n nature.

原页 112

我在本书其余部分描述的自然与尺度制造项目，借鉴这些文化资源。你将更多地听到作为文化共享时刻的植物采集、缪尔遗产中的自然之爱、环境科学的梦想与模型，以及围绕热带森林保护的热烈辩论。这些项目在不同社会语境中被部署和转化——制造并重新制造各种小写n的自然。

原页 112

For this task, however, I need a different approach than I have used in this chapter. To see practices of nature and scale-making in their variety, I can’t just work with famous examples; I need to investigate more ordinary environmental politics. Instead of beginning with successful globe-making projects and ferreting out their collaborators, I must proceed the other way around. I must follow the articulative process, however partial and incomplete its results. I dip into the cultural resources I have introduced here, but I do not privilege their globe-making perspectives. Instead, I track globemaking interactions much closer to the ground.

原页 112

然而，为此任务，我需要一种不同于本章所用的方法。要看到自然与尺度制造实践的多样性，我不能只使用著名例子；我需要调查更普通的环境政治。与其从成功的全球制造项目开始并侦察其合作者，我必须反过来进行。我必须跟随接合过程，无论其结果多么局部和不完整。我吸取这里介绍的文化资源，但不赋予其全球制造视角以特权。相反，我在更接近地面的地方追踪全球制造互动。

原页 113

“Dark rays”

原页 113

“暗射线”

原页 113

[On environmental ethics]

原页 113

[论环境伦理]

原页 113

Popular environmental knowledge is diverse and syncretic. It takes multiple forms of expertise and brings them down to size. This is not a one-way street, however. Individuals, including scientists, politicians, and activists, apply their eclectic perspectives in forming projects of nature-making.

原页 113

通俗环境知识是多样且混合的。它采用多种专业知识形式，并把它们缩小到可理解的尺度。然而，这并不是一条单行道。个人，包括科学家、政治家和活动家，在形成自然制造项目时运用他们兼收并蓄的视角。

原页 113

It makes no sense to search for a singular “Indonesian” environmental knowledge or one divided neatly into ethnic groups or religions. Instead, we might begin by identifying distinctive confluences of knowledge, as well as the nodes of practice and discourse informed by these confluences.

原页 113

寻找一种单一的“印尼”环境知识，或一种按族群或宗教整齐划分的知识，是没有意义的。相反，我们也许可以首先识别知识的不同汇流，以及受这些汇流影响的实践与话语节点。

原页 113

1997. President Suharto is still in power, but the New Order regime is beginning to unravel. Oppositional voices are growing louder even in the provinces. In South Kalimantan, these voices are moral and religious in their tone. They raise a new question about the environment: What if nature is a moral question?

原页 113

1997年。苏哈托总统仍在掌权，但新秩序政权开始瓦解。即使在各省，反对声音也越来越响亮。在南加里曼丹，这些声音在语调上是道德和宗教的。它们提出了一个关于环境的新问题：如果自然是一个道德问题呢？

原页 113, 114, 115

Late one night, in a provincial town in South Kalimantan, the guests had finally left the mulut gathering, and I found myself in focused conversation with the host, a batik merchant, who was smoking a cigarette.

“People say that smoking causes sickness; but actually it is the human heart [hati] that causes sickness. If you have only good deeds, cigarettes—or any foods—won’t harm you. The important thing is what is in your heart. It is better to associate with thieves than with someone whose speech is different than his heart.

“Everything that a person does should have a use for others. Otherwise people are more stupid than rocks, more stupid than the sun, moon, and stars. How can people be as stupid as dead matter? God made humans to guard the conservation of the earth. But this can only be done by recognizing that people do not live alone, like Robinson Crusoe. We live in a world connected with others, and everything we do must be of use to others. It is useless to do meditation exercises alone on mountains or on a rock in the ocean: What use does this have for others? Everything we do must have use, and this can only be gained by losing one’s ego, one’s ‘I.’ We don’t need to hate others, to be jealous, to be angry. Our sense of ego is what causes ruin in the world.

“People are worried about climate change. But it’s not industry that causes climate change. It’s the doing of people. Every action of a person causes a wave, and these waves meet and reverberate in the atmosphere. A good action causes a ray of brightness; a bad action causes a dark ray [cehaya gelap]. If there are many dark rays, the sunshine will not come through.

“There are many kinds of rays: ultraviolet; alpha; beta; x-rays. (They call them ‘x-rays’ because they don’t understand them; so they say ‘x.’ Did you know this?) There are other rays caused by human conduct. These influence the world.

“There is electricity in the human body. It’s not the same as electricity in the world, which lights the lamps. But how could a child form in the womb before it has received a soul? Only because of electricity. The man has positive electricity. The woman has negative electricity. The woman has elements of the earth; the man has elements of the heavens. These come together and a child is made from earth and sky, positive and negative electricity.

“Human actions affect atomic particles. There are two kinds of atomic particles: those under control, and those out of control. A bad heart makes things out of control. A good heart makes things under control. This is where science and religion meet. It’s no different from what foreign scientists say, but they haven’t given these things enough attention.

“God made the elements of the earth to stabilize the earth. There is iron, gold, silver, oil, coal: All give the earth stability. When people mine these until one element is gone, there will be no more stability to the crust of the earth. Inside the earth, lava flows in a more and more liquid form, and deep inside there is gas. It is very hot, perhaps 6,000 degrees or more. If the stability of the crust of the earth is disturbed, it will sink into the liquid and gas below. If you take out any of the elements of the earth until one is gone, the stability will be lost.

“Can you take this in, Anna?

“Every religion, whether Islam, Christianity, Judaism, or Buddhism, teaches us the effects of our hearts on our own world. Why do we pray? It’s not just to praise God. Our prayers come back to us humans, to make us conscious of ourselves. That is the promise of prayer, to raise self-consciousness [kesadaran diri]. The conscience [hati kecil] has its own influence on the world, different than thoughts. For example, sometimes you have a feeling you shouldn’t travel; you travel anyway and meet an accident. It is the conscience that should guide our actions. This is only possible by uniting microcosm and macrocosm, and by losing the sense of self.

“Have you ever seen water flow up? It always flows down. When you drop a rock, does it ever go upwards? It always falls to the ground. This is the way of nature. People are greedy and don’t accept this.”

原页 113, 114, 115

深夜，在南加里曼丹一个地方城镇，客人终于离开了 mulut 聚会，我发现自己与主人——一位正在抽烟的蜡染商人——进行着专注的交谈。

“人们说吸烟导致疾病；但实际上是人心（hati）导致疾病。如果你只有善行，香烟——或任何食物——都不会伤害你。重要的是你心里有什么。与其和说话与心不一的人交往，不如和小偷交往。

“一个人所做的一切都应该对他人有用。否则人比石头还愚蠢，比太阳、月亮和星星还愚蠢。人怎么能像死物质一样愚蠢？上帝造人是为了守护和保全大地。但这只有通过认识到人不是像鲁滨逊·克鲁索那样独自生活才能做到。我们生活在一个与他人相连的世界中，我们所做的一切都必须对他人有用。独自在山上或海中的岩石上冥想是没用的：这对他人有什么用处？我们所做的一切都必须有用，而这只有通过失去自我、失去‘我’才能获得。我们不需要恨别人、嫉妒、愤怒。我们的自我感是造成世界毁灭的原因。

“人们担心气候变化。但造成气候变化的不是工业。是人的所作所为。一个人的每一个行动都会引起波，这些波在大气中相遇并回响。善行产生一束明亮射线；恶行产生一道暗射线（cehaya gelap）。如果暗射线很多，阳光就透不过来。

“射线有很多种：紫外线；阿尔法射线；贝塔射线；X射线。（他们称之为‘X射线’是因为他们不理解它；所以他们说‘X’。你知道这个吗？）还有人类行为引起的其他射线。这些影响世界。

“人体内有电。它不同于世界上点亮灯的电。但一个孩子在获得灵魂之前，怎么能在子宫里形成？只因为电。男人有正电。女人有负电。女人有土的元素；男人有天的元素。这些结合在一起，孩子由土与天空、正电与负电造成。

“人类行为影响原子粒子。原子粒子有两种：受控的和失控的。坏心使事物失控。好心使事物受控。这就是科学与宗教相遇的地方。这与外国科学家所说的没有不同，只是他们没有给予这些事情足够的关注。

“上帝创造地球的元素来稳定地球。有铁、金、银、石油、煤：所有这些都给地球稳定。当人们开采这些，直到某种元素消失，地壳将不再有稳定性。地球内部，熔岩以越来越液态的形式流动，深处有气体。那里非常热，也许6000度或更高。如果地壳的稳定性受到扰动，它将沉入下面的液体和气体。如果你取出地球的任何元素，直到一种消失，稳定性就会丧失。

“你能接受这些吗，安娜？

“每一种宗教，无论是伊斯兰教、基督教、犹太教还是佛教，都教导我们心对我们自己世界的影响。我们为什么祈祷？不只是为了赞美上帝。我们的祈祷回到我们人类身上，使我们意识到自己。这就是祈祷的承诺，提升自我意识（kesadaran diri）。良心（hati kecil）对世界有自己的影响，不同于思想。例如，有时你有种感觉不应该旅行；你还是旅行了，遇到了事故。应该指导我们行动的是良心。这只有通过统一微观宇宙与宏观宇宙、通过失去自我感才有可能。

“你见过水向上流吗？它总是向下流。当你丢下一块石头，它会向上吗？它总是落到地上。这是自然之道。人们贪婪，不接受这一点。”

原页 115

Ahmad is an educated man. He spends most of his days seated at his stall at the market unfolding colorful sarongs for customers and supervising the young men who help him show his cloths. But he has been to college, and he has kept up particularly with natural science, philosophy, and religion. I have known him for a long time, and we often have these kinds of conversations when I see him. He knows me as a fellow scholastic, with whom he can share serious thoughts.

原页 115

艾哈迈德是个受过教育的人。他大多数日子坐在市场摊位上，为顾客展开色彩鲜艳的纱笼，并监督帮他展示布料的年轻人。但他上过大学，尤其关注自然科学、哲学和宗教。我认识他很久了，每次见到他，我们常有这类对话。他把我当作一位学者同侪，可以与之分享严肃想法。

原页 115

I didn’t want to be a merchant. I wanted to study when I was still a bachelor. I studied so much my father worried I would go crazy, so he married me off.

我不想做商人。我还是单身时想学习。我学得太用功，父亲担心我会发疯，就让我结了婚。

原页 115

Then I had to make a living for my wife and children.

原页 115

原页 115

Ahmad reads voraciously. Most of what is locally available are pamphlets on various aspects of Islamic faith. He pulls these together with his thoughts on science to forge a synthesis between the world as known by science and as known by religion.

原页 115

艾哈迈德博览群书。当地可得到的大部分是关于伊斯兰信仰各方面的小册子。他把这些与自己对科学的思考结合起来，在科学所知的世界与宗教所知的世界之间锻造一种综合。

原页 115

The Koran speaks of the seven layers of the earth and the seven layers of the heavens. Science has only begun to know the first layers. It is all written in the Koran, but we have yet to know about these things. For example, it will be found that there are fourteen planets, seven we know and seven beyond Pluto that we don’t yet know.

原页 115

《古兰经》谈到地球的七层和天的七层。科学才刚刚开始认识最初的几层。这一切都写在《古兰经》里，但我们还没有认识这些事情。例如，人们会发现有十四颗行星，七颗我们知道，七颗在冥王星之外我们尚不知道。

原页 115

The synthesis he offers is distinctive, but it does not make use of only local materials. Ahmad mentions Robinson Crusoe; when he talks about philosophy, he refers to Aristotle, Descartes, Hobbes, and Kant. After the conversation above, he recommended a book to me, which turned out to be the Indonesian translation of a treatise published by the State University of New York, called The Tao of Islam (Murata 1992). Ahmad is especially drawn to spiritual forms of understanding through which to blend religion and science.

原页 115

他提供的综合很独特，但并不只使用地方材料。艾哈迈德提到鲁滨逊·克鲁索；谈到哲学时，他提到亚里士多德、笛卡尔、霍布斯和康德。上述对话之后，他向我推荐了一本书，结果是纽约州立大学出版社出版的一部论著的印尼文译本，名为《伊斯兰之道》（The Tao of Islam）（Murata 1992）。艾哈迈德尤其被精神性的理解形式所吸引，借此融合宗教与科学。

Through this distinctive cosmopolitanism, he has put together a philosophy of nature—and, indeed, of nature conservation.

通过这种独特的世界主义，他拼合出一种自然哲学——实际上也是一种自然保护哲学。

It never used to be so hot as this. This is probably due to cutting down the trees. Every movement has a sound. Now there are more sounds than movements, because of television, radio, chain saws, motorboats, and the like. The atmosphere is like a container; sounds are not lost from it. They travel from one place to another creating new influences. The relation between the earth and the sun changes as a result.

原页 116

以前从没这么热过。这大概是因为砍树。每个运动都有声音。现在声音比运动多，因为电视、收音机、链锯、摩托艇等等。大气就像一个容器；声音不会从中消失。它们从一个地方传到另一个地方，创造新的影响。地球与太阳的关系因此改变。

原页 116

Ahmad’s discussion of nature conservation would not be recognized by environmental activists in South Kalimantan as their kind of talk; they would consider him countrified, quirky, and out of touch. He does not share their access to international circuits of environmental information and action; he does not use their rhetoric. Yet his ideas are consonant in many ways with the spirit of engaged intellectual discussion of nature in South Kalimantan. Like better recognized intellectuals, Ahmad looks for nature in the confluence between modern science and Islamic precept. Ahmad does not think that science and religion offer alternate ways of approaching nature. There is no divide between faith and reason, as in Western tradition. Instead, modern science and Islam reveal the same truth. Apparent divergences are only temporary misunderstandings that will disappear as we learn more about God’s world. The challenge of learning is to accept this.

原页 116

艾哈迈德关于自然保护的讨论，不会被南加里曼丹的环保活动家认作他们那类谈话；他们会认为他土气、古怪、脱离时代。他不享有他们进入国际环境信息与行动渠道的机会；他不使用他们的修辞。然而，他的想法在许多方面与南加里曼丹介入现实的知识分子关于自然的讨论的精神一致。像更受认可的知识分子一样，艾哈迈德在现代科学与伊斯兰教义的交汇处寻找自然。艾哈迈德不认为科学与宗教提供接近自然的替代方式。这里不存在西方传统中那种信仰与理性之间的分界。相反，现代科学与伊斯兰教揭示同一个真理。表面分歧只是暂时的误解，随着我们对上帝世界了解更多就会消失。学习的挑战就是接受这一点。

原页 116, 117

Ahmad identifies the route to understanding nature as proceeding through personal spiritual experience, as well as ethical choice for right conduct. The microcosm of one’s personal awareness must be brought into alignment with the macrocosm of the universe. Personal self-interest must be discarded so that a larger “global” understanding can enter one’s consciousness. Although the personal character of awareness is essential in Ahmad’s discussion, this is not the same personal spirituality that I heard about from the Javanese student nature lovers I describe in the next chapter. For cosmopolitan Javanese youth, personal spirituality is a break from the rigidity of established values; it is a world of insight that comes directly from mysterious sources, bypassing orthodox opinion. It recognizes equal ties to U.S. New Age spirituality, Islamic religiosity, and Javanese mysticism. In contrast, Ahmad’s personal spirituality opens the self to the power of truth in religion and science. It does not require nonconformism; indeed, it rejects the goal of self-differentiation as self-aggrandizement. Instead of egotistically searching out mysteries, we must each ask ourselves about our willingness to accept God’s universe, just as Ahmad asked me: “Can you take this in?”

Authoritative texts are an important way to open one’s understanding of God’s universe. These include the Koran and its interpretations, as well as the texts of modern science. Reading and rereading these texts, one can lose self-interest and approach the truth. This is the point of scholarship, whether religious or scientific.

原页 116, 117

艾哈迈德认为，理解自然的道路要通过个人精神体验，以及对正确行为的伦理选择。个人意识的微观宇宙必须与宇宙的宏观宇宙对齐。个人私利必须被抛弃，以便更大的“全球”理解进入意识。虽然意识的个人性在艾哈迈德的讨论中至关重要，这与我下一章描述的爪哇学生自然爱好者告诉我的个人灵性并不相同。对世界主义的爪哇青年来说，个人灵性是摆脱既定价值僵化的一种突破；它是一个直接来自神秘来源的洞见世界，绕过正统意见。它承认与美国新时代灵性、伊斯兰宗教性和爪哇神秘主义的平等联系。相比之下，艾哈迈德的个人灵性向宗教与科学中的真理力量敞开自我。它不要求人们离经叛道；事实上，它拒绝自我区分的目标，视之为自我膨胀。与其自我中心地寻找神秘，我们必须各自问自己是否愿意接受上帝的宇宙，就像艾哈迈德问我：“你能接受这些吗？”

权威文本是打开对上帝宇宙理解的重要方式。这些包括《古兰经》及其解释，以及现代科学的文本。阅读和重读这些文本，人可以失去私利并接近真理。这就是学术的要义，无论是宗教还是科学。

原页 117

These assumptions frame intellectual discussion of the big questions of nature and society in South Kalimantan. In the mid-1990s, activists, professionals, and professors developed these frames together with ordinary ethical men. The environment, along with democracy and justice, emerged as an object at the confluence of religion and science. The management of the relationship of humans and nature was best considered through the interpretation of authoritative texts, and the goal was to raise ethical standards of behavior.

原页 117

这些假设构成了南加里曼丹关于自然与社会大问题的知识讨论框架。20世纪90年代中期，活动家、专业人士和教授与讲求伦理的普通男性一起发展这些框架。环境，连同民主与正义，作为宗教与科学交汇处的对象出现。人与自然关系的管理最好通过解释权威文本来考虑，目标是提高行为的伦理标准。

原页 117

In the mid-1990s, Professor N. was a teacher, a journalist, and a political activist in the provincial capital.1 He was the founder of an organization that specialized in issues of law and the environment. Unostentatious and sociable, he was a popular teacher, and many of his students followed him into his NGO to pursue the interests he sparked in them concerning democracy and governance. “Usman” also wrote essays for the local newspaper. He became a political commentator in authoritarian times; he was brave but cautious in his opinions. In public seminars, he raised sharp and pressing questions. But he also quickly withdrew them if they attracted too much attention.

原页 117

20世纪90年代中期，N教授是省会的一名教师、记者和政治活动家。1他创立了一个专门处理法律与环境问题的组织。他不张扬，善于交际，是一位受欢迎的老师，许多学生跟随他进入他的非政府组织，追求他激发起的对民主与治理的兴趣。“乌斯曼”还为当地报纸写文章。他在威权时代成为政治评论员；他的观点勇敢而谨慎。在公开研讨会上，他提出尖锐而紧迫的问题。但如果这些问题引起太多注意，他也会很快收回。

原页 117

Usman did not come to environmental issues as a nature lover; he was a student activist. When we spoke in 1997, he admitted to me good-naturedly that he formed his NGO first and then looked around for some issues for it to address; he picked the environment because he thought he could make a difference with this issue, given its high public profile. His wife, however, was once a student nature lover. She had been an avid rock climber when they met. Now, he chuckled, their one-year-old baby loves to play with ropes. He forbids his wife to climb, he explained solicitously; it is too dangerous for women. Rock climbing is a better sport for men. They went camping, once, but the baby was angry and cried.

原页 117

乌斯曼并非作为自然爱好者进入环境议题；他曾是学生活动家。1997年我们交谈时，他和气地向我承认，他先成立了自己的非政府组织，然后才四处寻找一些议题让它处理；他选择了环境，因为他认为鉴于该议题的高公众关注度，他可以有所作为。然而，他的妻子曾是学生自然爱好者。他们相识时，她是个热心的攀岩者。现在，他咯咯笑着说，他们一岁的宝宝喜欢玩绳子。他体贴地解释说，他禁止妻子攀岩；这对女人太危险。攀岩是更适合男人的运动。他们去露营过一次，但宝宝生气了，哭个不停。

原页 117, 118

After inviting me to his house and introducing me to his reticent, pious, and polite wife, who, indeed, it seemed, had been domesticated by marriage, Usman opened the big notebooks that held the manuscripts of the essays he had written for the newspaper. The bulk of what he showed me were articles on environmental law. But I could see, interlaced with them, many articles on religion. He explained that these had become his two passions—each at the heart of political action. Each structured his approach to both scholarship and politics: the laws of God and the laws of society.

原页 117, 118

在邀请我去他家，并把我介绍给他沉默、虔诚、礼貌的妻子——她确实看起来已被婚姻驯化——之后，乌斯曼打开大笔记本，里面是他为报纸写的文章手稿。他给我看的大部分是关于环境法的文章。但我能看到，与它们交织的还有许多关于宗教的文章。他解释说，这些已成为他的两大热情——各自处于政治行动的核心。每一个都塑造了他对学术和政治的方法：上帝的法则与社会的法则。

原页 118

Law was at the center of Usman’s moral world. He had written at least one essay about the nature of law itself. Law, he argues, is at the heart of our ability to choose right conduct. From law, cultural norms emerge, which help us negotiate the tension between ideals and realities. Laws are norms that challenge people to reach their ideals, within cultural standards. The abstract and systemic nature of law makes it available as a system of guidelines for human behavior. Through the careful study of law, it is possible to raise awareness about environmental and theological issues. Through awareness, people may make better choices.

原页 118

法律是乌斯曼道德世界的中心。他至少写过一篇关于法律本身性质的文章。他论证说，法律是我们选择正确行为能力的核心。文化规范从法律中产生，帮助我们协商理想与现实之间的张力。法律是挑战人们在文化标准内达到理想状态的规范。法律的抽象和系统性，使其可以作为人类行为的指导体系。通过仔细研究法律，有可能提高对环境与神学问题的意识。通过意识，人们可以作出更好的选择。
