Coda

原页 269

尾声

原页 269

Contemplating the emerging triumph of free-market liberalism in his country, a Russian scholar is said to have quipped, “The future is clear and well-known. Only the past is worth studying, because only the past still has mystery.” The successes of corporate consolidation, free-ranging finance, and transnational economic standardization backed by military muscle have made it difficult for people all over the world to think beyond the story of neoliberal globalization. This story is not enough. Like the apocryphal Russian scholar, this book has turned away from the sureties of a self-making future to re-open a sense of mystery that might yet enrich the possibilities for imagining the about-to-be-present.

原页 269

据说一位俄罗斯学者在思考自由市场自由主义在其国家新兴的胜利时打趣道：“未来是清楚而众所周知的。只有过去值得研究，因为只有过去仍有神秘。”企业整合、自由流动的金融以及军事力量支持的跨国经济标准化的成功，使世界各地的人们难以想象新自由主义全球化故事之外的东西。这个故事还不够。像那位轶闻中的俄罗斯学者，本书背离了自我制造未来的确定性，重新打开一种神秘感，它或许仍能丰富想象即将到来的当下的可能性。

原页 269

How shall we re-open mystery in our times? To emerge from under the shadow of inevitability, it seems important to bring back the passions and the stakes of global connection. Instead of inscribing structures of self-fulfillment, we might immerse ourselves in the drama of uncertainty of global capitalism and transnational liberalism. What seems at first to be a minor skirmish may yet determine history. Since we don’t know how things will turn out, it’s worth attending to states of emergence—and emergency. Here hope and despair huddle together, sometimes dependent on the same technologies. Urgency springs up in ruined landscapes; utopian dreams, and crass ambitions, are formed. The guaranteed futures of globalization theory seem strange and far away in this storm.

原页 269

我们如何重新打开时代的神秘？要走出必然性的阴影，似乎重要的是带回全球联结的激情与利害。与其铭刻自我实现的结构，我们不如沉浸于全球资本主义和跨国自由主义的不确定性戏剧。起初看似小规模冲突的事，或许仍能决定历史。既然我们不知道事情会如何发展，就值得关注涌现——以及紧急——的状态。希望与绝望在此挤在一起，有时依赖同样的技术。紧迫性在毁坏的地景中涌现；乌托邦梦想和粗鄙野心得以形成。在这场风暴中，全球化理论那些有保证的未来显得陌生而遥远。

原页 269

Here, indeed, I write in conversation with other scholars who would interrupt the easy flow of global capital by conjuring a heady mixture of outrage and millenialism. In the interplay of ruin and possibility, they argue, lie alternative and more open forms of global commitment. Thinking through Indonesia’s history of anti-colonial struggle and state-sponsored terror, philosopher Pheng Cheah tells of radical nationalisms that offer populist hope at the same time as they are made possible by state disciplines (2003). Life and death haunt each other in these nationalisms, he says, making them both poison and medicine. Even the most utopian initiatives—say, human rights for women of the global south—are contaminated by the logics of power, and, yet, too, they carry our dreams for justice (Cheah 1997).

原页 269

确实，我在这里与其他学者对话，他们通过召唤愤怒与千禧年主义的醉人混合，来打断全球资本的顺畅流动。他们认为，在毁灭与可能性的相互作用中，存在另类且更开放的全球承诺形式。哲学家 Pheng Cheah 思考印尼反殖民斗争和国家赞助的恐怖史，讲述了激进民族主义既提供民粹主义希望，又由国家规训使其成为可能（2003）。他说，在这些民族主义中，生与死相互萦绕，使它们既是毒药也是药物。即使最乌托邦的倡议——比如全球南方女性的人权——也受到权力逻辑的污染，然而它们也承载着我们关于正义的梦想（Cheah 1997）。

原页 269, 270

If justice and repression must be grasped simultaneously, so too must exploitation and creative labor. Thus, literary scholar Neferti Tadiar (forthcoming) introduces the concept of “historical experience” to tell of the subjective labor of the marginalized and displaced, which fuels narratives of capital and nation yet falls beyond these narratives’ scope of explanation. For example, the experience of Filipina labor migrants—maids, prostitutes, entertainers, all disgorged from the country to earn remittances—articulates and transforms the Philippines’ global disadvantage into both the worst disappointments and the most heartfelt desires. Their experience exposes them to the worst terrors of the global economy, even as it articulates the possibilities of new, emergent forms of social relation. This mingling of despair and hope reformulates representations of global capital, remaking the culture and politics of globalization.

原页 269, 270

如果正义与压迫必须同时把握，剥削与创造性劳动也必须同时把握。因此，文学学者内费尔蒂·塔迪亚尔（Neferti Tadiar，即将出版）引入“历史经验”概念，讲述边缘化和流离失所者的主体性劳动，这种劳动为资本与民族国家的叙事提供燃料，却落在这些叙事的解释范围之外。例如，菲律宾女性劳工移民——女佣、妓女、艺人，全都从国内被推向海外，以赚取侨汇——的经验，把菲律宾的全球劣势表述并转化为最深的失望和最真挚的欲望。她们的经验使她们暴露于全球经济最可怕的恐怖，同时也表述了新生的社会关系形式的可能性。这种绝望与希望的混合重新表述全球资本的再现，重塑全球化的文化与政治。

原页 270

The most exciting feature of this conversation for me is its requirement that the analysis be located inside the world of globalization’s struggles and passions. Unlike most social scientists and area studies specialists, these scholars refuse to objectify the participants from the perspective of an imagined global management. Instead, Cheah and Tadiar bring us to understand the risks, collusions, and uncertainties from the perspective of those whose well-being is at stake. This opens up the analysis to the promises and dangers of history; contingency matters because it shifts the options for justice and repression, exploitation and creative hope. In this same spirit, this book has followed the contending forms of hazard, curiosity, and zeal of natural resource entrepreneurs, environmental advocates, student nature lovers, and indigenous farmer-foragers.

原页 270

对我来说，这场对话最令人兴奋的特征，是它要求把分析置于全球化斗争与激情的世界内部。与大多数社会科学家和区域研究专家不同，这些学者拒绝从想象性的全球管理视角把参与者对象化。相反，Cheah 和 Tadiar 让我们从那些福祉受到威胁者的视角理解风险、共谋和不确定性。这使分析向历史的承诺与危险敞开；偶然性重要，因为它改变了正义与压迫、剥削与创造性希望的选择。本着同样的精神，本书追随自然资源企业家、环保倡导者、学生自然爱好者和原住民农耕—采集者相互竞争的冒险、好奇与热忱形式。

原页 270

This perspective of engagement also informs Cheah’s argument for the importance of claims to the universal (2001). As long as area studies closes itself to the universal, he says, it will cordon off those it studies from participation in remaking the world. Only because area studies scholars have conventionally imagined themselves in the service of the all-seeing West, he argues, have they confined the scope of the non-Western dreams and nightmares they study into area-bound particularities. From inside any “area,” universal claims are key to global agency. Inspired by Cheah’s challenge, I have taken a close look at the universal, making it a key category for my research. I call universals “engaged” to acknowledge the fact that to be effective they must enter the fray. Universal claims allow people to make history, but not under the conditions those claims might lead them to choose.

原页 270

这种介入的视角也影响了 Cheah 关于普遍性主张重要性的论证（2001）。他说，只要区域研究对普遍物封闭自己，它就会把它所研究的对象圈起来，不让其参与世界的重造。他论证说，只是因为区域研究学者习惯上把自己想象为服务于全视的西方，他们才把所研究的非西方梦想与噩梦的范围限定为区域性的特殊性。在任何“区域”内部，普遍性主张都是全球能动性的关键。受 Cheah 挑战的启发，我仔细审视普遍物，使其成为研究的关键范畴。我把这些普遍性称为“介入性的”，以承认这样一个事实：要有效，它们必须进入战斗。普遍性主张让人们能够创造历史，但不是在他们可能因这些主张而选择的条件下。

原页 270, 271

This book has argued that we know and use nature through engaged universals. The “environment” spreads around the world through the friction of engagement, both for commercial users, who tap into its divergences for capitalist commodity chains, and for advocates, who find in these same divergences the means to study, enjoy, or preserve it. As I have shown, what seem at first to be equivalent requirements to work across difference lead to contrasting consequences for humans and nonhumans. In the spirit of scholars such as Cheah and Tadiar, I suggest that social analysis can explore these diverging scenes of possibility only through its own engaged immersion in the histories it plots.

原页 270, 271

本书论证我们通过介入性的普遍性来认识和使用自然。“环境”通过介入的摩擦传遍世界，无论是对商业使用者——他们利用其分歧为资本主义商品链服务——还是对倡导者——他们在同样的分歧中找到研究、欣赏或保护它的手段。如我所展示的，起初看似同等的要求——跨越差异工作——对人类和非人类导致截然不同的后果。本着 Cheah 和 Tadiar 等学者的精神，我提出，社会分析只有通过自身对所描绘历史的介入性沉浸，才能探索这些分歧的可能性场景。

原页 271

My own ability to enter this history is that of an ethnographer—a listener and a teller of tales. Yet my project stretches and changes the practice of ethnography. As I reach to describe global connections, my ethnography necessarily diverges from the holism of more familiar models, in which each anecdote or custom forms a scrap in a larger, unified pattern. Instead, following the example of subaltern studies historians who retrieve forgotten pasts plowed over by national histories, I endorse the fragment (Pandey 2000). In this project, I have used ethnographic fragments to interrupt stories of a unified and successful regime of global self-management.

原页 271

我自己进入这段历史的能力，是民族志学者的能力——一个倾听者和讲故事者。然而我的项目延伸并改变了民族志实践。当我伸手描述全球联结时，我的民族志必然背离更熟悉模式的整体主义；在那些模式中，每则轶事或习俗都构成更大统一图案中的碎片。相反，我效仿那些打捞被国家历史碾过、遭到遗忘的过去的庶民研究历史学家，认可碎片（Pandey 2000）。在这个项目中，我用民族志碎片打断统一而成功的全球自我管理体制的故事。

原页 271

Ethnographic fragments ask us to pay attention to details. The travels that inspire global connection turn out to be less controllable than those at the top imply. Making claims about scale, including globalization, turns out to be an arena of contention.

原页 271

民族志碎片要求我们注意细节。激发全球联结的旅行，结果比高层所暗示的更不可控。关于尺度——包括全球化——的主张，结果是一个争论的竞技场。

原页 271

And thus there is no reason to begin a retelling of global connections in imagined world centers such as New York, Tokyo, or Geneva. Globalization is not delivered whole and round like a pizza, to be munched and dismantled by the hungry margins. Global connections are made in fragments—although some fragments are more powerful than others. My telling of global connections has featured rural Kalimantan, where the fragmentary nature of global process is especially evident. Following global connections out of Kalimantan, I found myself exploring other sites, including powerful centers of finance, science, and policy. But these, too, produce only fragments, and my Kalimantan beginnings remind me of this. Some fragments are able to make themselves look whole. Honoring the fragment means acknowledging this power but not accepting it as a done deal. Through fragments, ethnographers can immerse themselves in the contests and engagements of the present.

原页 271

因此，没有理由从纽约、东京或日内瓦等想象的世界中心开始重述全球联结。全球化不是像披萨一样整块完整地送达，供饥饿的边缘啃食和拆解。全球联结是在碎片中制造的——尽管有些碎片比其他碎片更强大。我对全球联结的讲述以加里曼丹乡村为特色，在那里全球过程的碎片性尤为明显。顺着全球联结走出加里曼丹，我发现自己探索其他地点，包括金融、科学和政策的强大中心。但这些地方也只生产碎片，我在加里曼丹的开端提醒我这一点。有些碎片能够使自己看起来完整。尊重碎片意味着承认这种权力，但不把它当作既成事实接受。通过碎片，民族志学者可以沉浸于当下的争夺与介入。

原页 271

Fragments need not reduce analysis to simply noticing idiosyncrasy and happenstance. This book has proposed a series of methods to enable more nuanced understandings of global connection. They interrupt dominant stories of globalization to offer more realistic alternatives. Instead of positing a triumphant global regime, these methods guide us to the disjunctions of global travel, such as those I have traced in the excesses of capitalist proliferations and the awkward conjunctures of social movement building. Here it is possible to consider the practical shape of global politics and culture without the interference of self-fulfilling prophecies.

原页 271

碎片不必把分析降低为仅仅注意到特异性和偶然。本书提出了一系列方法，以便对全球联结作出更细致的理解。它们打断全球化的主导故事，提供更现实的替代方案。这些方法不是设定一个胜利的全球体制，而是引导我们走向全球旅行的断裂，例如我在资本主义增殖的过度和社会运动建设的别扭汇合中所追踪的那些。在这里，可以考虑全球政治与文化的实际形态，而不受自我实现预言的干扰。

原页 271, 272

Instead of requiring an evolutionary process of change, these methods show the pervasive effects of historical encounters. Instead of starting with the dichotomy between global force and local response, these methods show the importance of contingent and botched encounters in shaping both business-as-usual and its radical refusals. Thus, I have described how cosmopolitan nature loving—like capitalist resource use—has emerged in the crossroads of old cultural legacies. I show how well-intentioned advocacy for the indigenous peoples of the forest extends the logics of power, forging new gaps in what can be said about people and forests. Yet sometimes in the urgency of a campaign, such misunderstandings are productive as objects in common begin to coalesce in the space of partial agreement. It is these moments of conjuncture that make social activism worthwhile. Meanwhile, they interrupt and change the principles of activism, introducing further genealogies of meaning and coercion into the risky mix that signifies empowerment.

原页 271, 272

这些方法不要求一个进化的变化过程，而是展示历史遭遇的普遍效果。这些方法不从全球力量与地方回应之间的二分开始，而是展示偶然与搞砸的遭遇在塑造一切照常及其激进拒绝中的重要性。因此，我描述了世界主义自然之爱——像资本主义资源利用一样——如何在旧文化遗产的十字路口出现。我展示了对森林原住民善意倡导如何延伸权力逻辑，在人与森林的可言说范围中制造新的空白。然而，有时在运动的紧迫情势中，这类误解具有生产力，因为共同对象开始在部分共识的空间中凝聚。正是这些汇合时刻使社会行动主义值得付出。同时，它们打断并改变行动主义的原则，把更多意义与强制的谱系引入标志着赋权的风险混合体。

原页 272

Such fragments of varied schemes and travels and encounters do create a world of global connections. These are global connections made, and muddled, in friction. Curiosity about such friction might yet re-open the mystery of our times.

原页 272

这些多样方案、旅行和遭遇的碎片确实创造了一个全球联结的世界。这些全球联结是在摩擦中制造、也被摩擦搅乱的。对这种摩擦的好奇，或许仍能重新打开我们时代的神秘。

原注

前言

1
原页 273

I first gained familiarity with Meratus social life in a two-year “deep immersion” fieldwork experience in the Meratus Mountains between 1979 and 1981. I planned other long fieldwork stays, first to study the making of social landscape, and, later, to study environmental mobilizations, but I was unable to coordinate my research permission, my health, my grants, and my teaching job. Instead, my field research has been organized into a series of shorter periods, usually of several months. Luckily, the other groups on whom I focused—nature lovers, activists, donors, scholars—felt enough of an affinity to my own social position to make ethnographic fieldwork relatively easy to arrange. (I failed in my attempts to conduct more than superficial interviews with timber and mining company representatives. Their hostility also restrained me from seeking out active employees.) And so I found myself—mostly during North American summers—traveling from Jakarta to various provincial capitals and towns and to the Meratus Mountains, letting myself follow the connections of acquaintance, and the events and issues of rainforest politics that I could triangulate across them. My fieldwork included stints in 1986, 1994, 1997, and 2000.

↩ en
原页 273

我第一次熟悉梅拉图斯的社会生活，是1979年至1981年间在梅拉图斯山脉进行的一次为期两年的“深度沉浸”田野调查。我原计划再作几次长期田野停留，先研究社会地景的形成，后来研究环境动员，但我无法协调研究许可、健康状况、资助经费和教职工作。于是，我的田野调查被安排成一系列较短的时段，通常为期数月。幸运的是，我后来关注的另一些群体——自然爱好者、行动者、资助者、学者——觉得与我的社会位置有足够的亲近感，使民族志田野调查相对容易安排。（我试图与木材和矿业公司代表进行超出表面交谈的访谈，但未能成功。他们的敌意也使我不敢主动接触在职员工。）就这样——大多在北美夏季——我发现自己从雅加达前往各省会和城镇，再前往梅拉图斯山脉，让自己跟随熟人关系，以及我能通过他们交叉印证的雨林政治事件和议题。我的田野工作包括1986、1994、1997和2000年的停留。

8
原页 274

Thinking through the universal involves techniques of formal abstraction. One must learn to generalize from one instance to another, to see an underlying or emergent principle of commonality across apparent difference. The principle must tie both instances not just to each other but to a radically open field that could at least potentially cover all other instances. It is these habits of generalization and abstraction that make proponents of universal truths uninterested in criticisms that universals do not take the heterogeneity of the world into account. The existence of particularity does not get in the way of the universal. The point of universalism is to move from particular instances to more general laws. The abstract universal is always open; new discoveries, principles, and proponents are welcome. The mechanics of universality are discussed further in chapter 3.

↩ en
原页 274

思考普遍物涉及形式抽象的技术。人必须学会从一个实例推广到另一个实例，看到表面差异之下或之中浮现的共性原则。该原则必须不仅把两个实例彼此联系起来，而且把它们联系到一个至少在潜在意义上能涵盖所有其他实例的根本开放场域。正是这些概括与抽象的习惯，使普遍真理的倡导者对“普遍物没有考虑世界异质性”的批评不感兴趣。特殊性的存在并不妨碍普遍物。普遍主义的关键在于从特殊实例走向更普遍的规律。抽象的普遍物始终开放；新的发现、原则和倡导者都受到欢迎。普遍性的机制将在第三章进一步讨论。

Dubois (1997) describes the use of universalism by slaves in revolt in the French Caribbean. The French Revolution and the Haitian Revolution were tightly connected in their development of notions of universal rights. (In this vein, BuckMorss [2000] argues that Hegelian ideals of universal history were developed in dialogue with Haiti’s revolution.) Enlightenment ideals and universal truths were also key to the spread of Asian anti-colonialism. Pramoedya (1991) offers a literary account of the inspiration of Enlightenment ideals on an emerging nationalism in colonial Java. Universalisms have inspired both national and transnational commitments. Duara (2001) traces the interplay between European and north Asian discourses of universal truth and civilization in early twentieth century discourses of pan-Asianism.

Dubois（1997）描述了法属加勒比地区起义奴隶对普遍主义的使用。法国大革命与海地革命在普遍权利观念的发展中紧密相连。（沿着这条线索，Buck-Morss〔2000〕论证黑格尔式的普遍历史理想是在与海地革命的对话中形成的。）启蒙理想与普遍真理也是亚洲反殖民主义传播的关键。Pramoedya（1991）以文学方式讲述了启蒙理想对殖民地爪哇新兴民族主义的启发。普遍主义既激发了民族承诺，也激发了跨国承诺。Duara（2001）追溯了20世纪初泛亚洲主义话语中欧洲与北亚关于普遍真理和文明的话语之间的相互作用。

14
原页 274, 275

The broad spectrum of universalism’s appeal has inspired political philosophers ina lively discussion of universals in relation to the making of democracy, cosmopolitanism, and social change. At the radical edge of the discussion, a number of theorists offer tools for thinking through the practical dilemmas of engaged univer- sals. Judith Butler comments on the exclusions of even the most progressive univer- salisms that follow from “the cultural location of the enunciation of universality” (2000: 37). Pursuing this linguistic metaphor, she argues for the importance of trans- /ation as the process through which excluded groups struggle for inclusion within the privileges granted to universalism’s unmarked subjects. Because of the specificities of language, translation is always both representation and misrepresentation. All universalisms, Butler suggests, are made in histories of translation. Ernesto Laclau (2000) points to the importance of historical contingency in the transformation of particular complaints into universal goals. To enter the political process, Laclau suggests, a class segment must present its aims as realizing the universal aims of the community. It is the contingent nature of this process that makes it key to political struggle.

↩ en
原页 274, 275

普遍主义吸引力的广泛光谱，激发了政治哲学家们就普遍物与民主、世界主义和社会变革之生成的关系展开活跃讨论。在讨论的激进一端，一些理论家提供了思考介入性的普遍性所面临的实践困境的工具。Judith Butler 评论说，即使是最进步的普遍主义，也因“普遍性表述的文化位置”而产生排斥（2000: 37）。沿着这一语言学隐喻，她论证翻译的重要性：被排斥的群体通过翻译过程，争取进入普遍主义未标记主体所获特权的空间。由于语言的特殊性，翻译始终既是再现，也是误现。Butler 认为，一切普遍主义都诞生于翻译的历史。Ernesto Laclau（2000）指出，历史偶然性在把特殊不满转化为普遍目标的过程中至关重要。Laclau 认为，要进入政治过程，一个阶级派别必须把自身目标呈现为实现共同体的普遍目标。正是这一过程的偶然性质，使它成为政治斗争的关键。

In the earliest period of the timber boom, military officers and foundations took a large share. The military formed arrangements with foreign companies and Sino-Indonesian firms to do the logging, while the military supplied the concession. In this, President Suharto pursued an accommodation he began in funding the military indirectly through letting it control Indonesia’s oil. In a later period, foreign firms were pushed out of timber. Concessionaires’ off-budget contributions allowed the regime to balance and appease varied military and civilian elites (Ascher 1998; McCulloch 2000).

↩ en
原页 275

在木材繁荣的最早期，军官和基金会占有很大份额。军方与外国公司及华裔印尼公司作出安排，由后者从事伐木，军方提供采伐特许权。苏哈托总统在此延续了一种利益协调安排：他早先通过让军方控制印尼石油，间接为军方提供资金。后来，外国公司被逐出木材业。特许经营者的预算外贡献使政权得以平衡并安抚各种军方和文职精英（Ascher 1998; McCulloch 2000）。

Other Southeast Asian forests were also involved in this transformation act. The sogo shosha had first approached the Philippines for dipterocarps. When Philippine forests were depleted, the traders moved to the forests of Sabah, Sarawak, and only then Indonesia. The regional sweep of these biologically somewhat similar forests allowed the Japanese traders’ ambitions to grow. Unsustainable harvests are fine, because other forests await. Environmental scholar Peter Dauvergne (1997) de- scribes Japanese trading companies as casting a long “ecological shadow” over Southeast Asia, as they moved across the region decimating forests in first one coun- try and then another.

原页 275

其他东南亚森林也卷入了这一转变过程。综合商社最初为获取龙脑香科木材而接触菲律宾。菲律宾森林耗尽后，贸易商转向沙巴和砂拉越的森林，之后才转向印尼。这些在生物构成上颇为相似的森林在区域内的广泛分布，使日本贸易商的野心得以增长。不可持续的采伐无妨，因为还有别的森林在等待。环境学者 Peter Dauvergne（1997）描述日本贸易公司如何跨越该地区，先在一个国家、再在另一个国家毁坏森林，从而在东南亚投下一道长长的“生态阴影”。

Over 100 logging firms went bankrupt, and many foreign and military investors sold off their holdings (Ross 2001: 182-83; see also Brown [1999] who argues that military investments were still significant). The new policy had the effect it planned: By 1985, there were 101 plywood-producing firms in Indonesia—up from 19 in 1978—and the industry’s production was 6.5 million cubic meters per year. (In 1978, production was only 800,000 m’.) By 1990, production was 12.6 million m’ (Barr 1998: 9). In 1992, the ban was replaced by an export tax (Ascher 1998: 50). In 1998, IMF agreements forced the New Order to lift the ban (Barr 1998: 35).

In the 1980s, a large part of Indonesia’s forests came into the hands of SinoIndonesian logging companies (Ross 2001: 183-85). Hasan, indeed, pioneered the intimate relationship between regime officials and ethnic Chinese businessmen that became the hallmark of the New Order economy. Hasan was a business associate of Suharto from the days when they jointly used smuggling to finance a division of the army (Barr 1998: 2-4). When Suharto became president in 1967, his regime made this kind of association a model. Sino-Indonesian entrepreneurs became a convenient and controllable national substitute for foreign investors. Denied the privileges of full citizenship, they offered finance and business experience in exchange for the right to make great fortunes—some of which were funneled back to their political patrons. Meanwhile, the military also maintained an important presence in promoting both legal and illegal resource extraction (McCulloch 2000).

Conservation in Indonesia involves government bureaucrats, foreign organizations, and national environmentalists. Each of these has had very different agendas. In this book, I discuss only the last of these three. Barber (1989) offers a good introduction to New Order state forestry. Lowe (1999) offers an ethnographically informed critique of foreign conservation programs. Stone and D’Andrea (2001) discuss the World Wildlife Fund, a transnational organization with a strong domestic base in Indonesia. During the New Order, the national environmental movement organized particularly around umbrella institutions with their headquarters in Jakarta. The Indonesian Environmental Forum (WALHI) continues to coordinate dozens of regional and issue-oriented groups and speaks for the national cause in both foreign and domestic fora. In the 1980s, the Indonesian NGO Network for Tropical Forest Conservation (SKEPHI) was also a national umbrella organization; in the 1990s it became an issue group.

原页 276

印尼的保护涉及政府官僚、外国组织和本国环保人士。这三者各有非常不同的议程。本书只讨论这三者中的最后一项。Barber（1989）对新秩序国家林业作了很好的介绍。Lowe（1999）对外国保护项目提出了具有民族志自觉的批评。Stone 和 D’Andrea（2001）讨论了世界自然基金会——一个在印尼有强大本国基础的跨国组织。新秩序时期，本国环保运动尤其围绕总部设在雅加达的伞状机构组织起来。印尼环境论坛（WALHI）继续协调数十个地区和议题导向的团体，并在国内外论坛上代表全国环保事业发声。1980年代，印尼非政府组织热带森林保护网络（SKEPHI）也是一个全国性伞状组织；1990年代它变成了一个议题团体。

2
原页 278

As much as any place in the world, Indonesia rode high on the wave of enthusiasm for mobile, finance-driven international investment in the 1980s and early 1990s. Between the late 1980s and 1997, economic growth averaged about 8 percent per year, and in early 1997, for economists, “there was little sign of the turmoil that was to emerge” when the economy crashed and the Suharto regime followed in 1998 (McLeod, 1999: 209). Looking back, many once-enthusiastic analysts blamed the crisis on “cronyism,” residual protectionism, and bad national regulatory practices. See, e.g., Jackson (1999).

↩ en
原页 278

印尼在1980年代和1990年代初，与世界任何地方一样，乘着移动的、金融驱动的国际投资热潮腾飞。1980年代末至1997年间，经济增长平均每年约8%；1997年初，对经济学家而言，“几乎看不出后来出现的动荡迹象”，随后经济崩溃，苏哈托政权于1998年倒台（McLeod, 1999: 209）。回望过去，许多一度热情洋溢的分析师把危机归咎于“裙带关系”、残余的保护主义和糟糕的国家监管实践。例如见 Jackson（1999）。

↩ zh
3
原页 278, 279

From the first, the Bre-X story caught the popular imagination, especially in Canada, and thousands of articles have been written about it. Most major Canadian newspapers covered the story in detail; The Calgary Sun, The Calgary Herald, and the Ottawa Citizen have had many installments of Bre-X news. Only rather late in the game did U.S. newspapers cover the Bre-X story regularly, but at the height of its fame and infamy, much of the media across North America covered the story. Indonesian newspapers and news magazines also offered considerable coverage. Indonesian nongovernmental organizations added their perspectives in flyers and newsletters. Several books have been published about Bre-X, mainly by journalists. Francis (1997) and Goold and Willis (1997) tell the story with lively excitement. Danielson and Whyte (editor and staff writer, respectively, for The Northern Miner) offer their expertise on the people and politics of the mining scene (1997). Bondan Winarno’s (1997) account includes useful detail on Indonesian politics and texts of a number of Bre-X documents. Jennifer Well’s coverage for the Canadian news magazine Macleans and John McBeth’s coverage for the Far Eastern Economic Review have also been very informative. John Behar (1997) offers a useful description of Bre-X’s operations. Internet investor chat lines with Bre-X “threads” offer a wealth of both technical information and personal views on the drama.

↩ en
原页 278, 279

从最初起，Bre-X 的故事就抓住了大众的想象，尤其是在加拿大，关于它的文章已有数千篇。大多数加拿大主要报纸都详细报道过此事；The Calgary Sun、The Calgary Herald 和 The Ottawa Citizen 刊登过许多期 Bre-X 新闻。美国报纸较晚才开始定期报道 Bre-X，但在其名声与恶名最盛之时，北美大部分媒体都报道了这一事件。印尼报纸和新闻杂志也提供了相当多的报道。印尼非政府组织在传单和通讯中加入了它们的视角。关于 Bre-X 已出版了几本书，主要出自记者之手。Francis（1997）和 Goold and Willis（1997）以生动的兴奋笔调讲述了这一故事。Danielson 和 Whyte（分别为 The Northern Miner 的编辑和专职记者）提供了他们对矿业界人物与政治的专门知识（1997）。Bondan Winarno（1997）的记述包含关于印尼政治的有用细节以及若干 Bre-X 文件的文本。Jennifer Well 为加拿大新闻杂志 Macleans 所作的报道，以及 John McBeth 为 Far Eastern Economic Review 所作的报道，也提供了非常丰富的信息。John Behar（1997）对 Bre-X 的运营作了有用的描述。带有 Bre-X “主题帖”的互联网投资者聊天热线，既提供了大量技术信息，也提供了个人对这出戏剧的看法。

To “conjure” is both to call forth spirits and to perform magical tricks; in each case, the term highlights the intentionality of the performance, the studied charisma of the performer, and the hope of moving the audience beyond the limits of rational calculation. These features characterize the economic strategies I discuss here, in which everyday performance requirements—for contracts, marketing, reports, and the like—are made into dramatic shows of potential.

↩ en
原页 279

“conjure”兼有召唤神灵和施行魔术之意；在两种情况下，这个词都突出表演的意向性、表演者刻意的魅力，以及使观众超越理性计算之限的期望。这些特征正是我在此讨论的经济策略的特点：在这些策略中，合同、营销、报告等日常表演要求，被制成展示潜力的戏剧性演出。

In the words of the report: “We very much regret having to express the firm opinion that an economic gold deposit has not been identified in the Southeast zone of the Busang property, and is unlikely to be. We realize that the conclusions reached in this interim report will be a great disappointment to the many investors, employees, suppliers, and the joint-venture partners associated with Bre-X, to the Government of Indonesia, and to the mining industry elsewhere. However, the magnitude of the tampering with core samples that we believe has occurred and resulting falsification of assay values at Busang, is of a scale and over a period of time and with a precision that, to our knowledge, is without precedent in the history of mining anywhere in the world” (Farquarson 1997: 27).

21
原页 280

Personal narratives of frontier gold discovery often give more clues to the interdependence of company miners and independent gold seekers than official discovery tales. Bre-X geologists were quite willing to admit, informally, that they chose their prospecting sites through the advice of small-scale Kalimantan miners, who led them to gold-rich sites. Consider, for example, the narrative Bre-X chief geologist Felderhof told reporters about how he first found Busang: “Felderhof had first heard of Busang in the early 1980s, when he and his Australian colleague Mike Bird were exploring the logging roads of Borneo on rented motorcycles. They roared from village to village, asking the locals to point out where they had found gold nuggets in stream beds” (Goold and Willis 1997: 36). Indeed, one of the earliest clouds of suspicion about the rich “southeast zone” of Busang was generated by the fact that small-scale miners did not pan for gold in this area (Danielson and Whyte 1997: 197). Despite acknowledging this interdependence, it never occurred to the geologists that it might interfere with their personal rights—or their official stories—of “discovery.”

↩ en
原页 280

关于边疆采金发现的个人叙述，往往比官方的发现故事更能揭示公司矿工与独立淘金者之间的相互依存。Bre-X 的地质学家私下很愿意承认，他们通过加里曼丹小规模矿工的建议选择勘探地点，是这些人把他们带到黄金富集地。例如，Bre-X 首席地质学家 Felderhof 向记者讲述他最初如何发现 Busang 的故事：“Felderhof 第一次听说 Busang 是在1980年代初，当时他和澳大利亚同事 Mike Bird 骑着租来的摩托车探查婆罗洲的伐木道。他们从一个村庄轰隆隆地开到另一个村庄，请当地人指出他们在河床里哪里发现过金块”（Goold and Willis 1997: 36）。事实上，关于 Busang 富饶的“东南区”最早出现的疑云之一，正是因为小规模矿工不在这一地区淘金（Danielson and Whyte 1997: 197）。尽管承认这种相互依存，地质学家却从未想到，它可能会干扰他们个人的“发现”权利——或他们官方的“发现”故事。

23
原页 281

More restrictive second-generation and less restrictive third-generation CoWs were introduced in 1968 and 1976, respectively. 1986-87 marked the Australian “gold rush” in Indonesia and introduced fourth-generation CoWs, with “one year of general survey ending with 25% relinquishment of concession area; three years of exploration with 75% relinquishment by the end of the fourth year; an Indonesian partner in the CoW; and equity divestment after five years of operation so that ideally after 10 years of production the local partner holds 51%” (Marr 1993: 16). Fifth-generation contracts began in 1990, with tax incentives and low tariff property taxes. A 1992 law required foreign investors in frontier areas to reduce their equity shares to a maximum of 95 percent within five years and to 80 percent within 20 years (Marr 1993: 17). Sixth-generation CoWs, requiring environmental impact assessments, were offered in 1997 (Winarno 1997: 28).

↩ en
原页 281

限制更严的第二代采矿合同（CoW）和限制较少的第三代合同分别于1968年和1976年推出。1986—87年标志着澳大利亚在印尼的“淘金热”，并引入第四代 CoW，其规定为：“一年普查，结束时放弃25%的矿区；三年勘探，到第四年末放弃75%；在 CoW 中有印尼合伙人；运营五年后转让部分股权，以便理想情况下生产十年后当地合伙人持有51%”（Marr 1993: 16）。第五代合同始于1990年，带有税收优惠和低费率财产税。1992年一项法律要求边疆地区的外国投资者在五年内将股权降至最多95%，并在二十年内降至80%（Marr 1993: 17）。要求进行环境影响评估的第六代 CoW 于1997年推出（Winarno 1997: 28）。

Bre-X 的小额大众投资的重要性，凸显了这一国家议程的重要性。“1996年5月顶峰时，Bre-X 的2.4亿股中有70%掌握在个人投资者手中”（Goold and Willis 1997: 239）。相比之下，一家更普通的加拿大公司可能只有30%的股份由个人持有。根据 Goold and Willis（1997: 105），1996年 Bre-X 有13,000名股东，包括养老基金和保险公司。根据 Francis（1997: 199），约5%的 Bre-X 交易来自加拿大以外。Bre-X 全部交易的90%在多伦多证券交易所进行（Francis 1997: 197）。

↩ zh
34
原页 281, 282

It is possible to make a great deal of money from speculation even if the product comes to nothing. Bre-X shareholders made money merely by selling their shares while the price was still high. The outspoken investors Greg and Kathy Chorny, for example, sold two-thirds of their stock for C$40 million and lost a comparatively minor sum on remaining shares (Francis 1997: 196). At the end, smart investors made money by “short selling,” that is, borrowing Bre-X shares from brokers, selling them, and returning them by buying them back at a lower price. Goold and Willis (1997: 221) report that 5.5 million Bre-X shares were sold short; Francis (1997: 203) reports that the investment bank Oppenheimer and Co. made C$100 million shorting Bre-X stock. Meanwhile, other firms and individuals, including Quebec’s public pension fund and the Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board, lost major amounts of money (Goold and Willis 1997: 248).

↩ en
原页 281, 282

即使产品最终化为乌有，也可以靠投机赚大钱。Bre-X 股东仅仅在价格仍高时卖出股票就赚了钱。例如，直言不讳的投资者 Greg 和 Kathy Chorny 卖掉了三分之二的持股，得到4000万加元，余下股票的损失相对较小（Francis 1997: 196）。最后，聪明的投资者通过“卖空”赚钱，即从经纪人那里借入 Bre-X 股票卖出，再以较低价格买回还给经纪人。Goold and Willis（1997: 221）报告称，有550万股 Bre-X 被卖空；Francis（1997: 203）报告称，投资银行 Oppenheimer and Co. 通过卖空 Bre-X 股票赚了1亿加元。与此同时，其他公司和个人，包括魁北克公共养老基金和安大略教师养老金计划委员会，损失了大量资金（Goold and Willis 1997: 248）。

↩ zh
35
原页 282

Other Bre-X allegories have been suggested, for example, that greed blinds everyone’s eyes (Goold and Willis 1997: 267), or that the international flow of money means business must deal with “exotic and troublesome regimes” (Francis 1997: 232). Outside of Canada, the allegorical reading arose that this was just the way of Canadian business, where stock exchanges are a “regulatory Wild West” (quotation attributed to the U.S. mass media in Winarno 1997: 208). My reading refuses the distinction between the seeing and the blind to point to the money being made even in a scam. I emphasize the exotic and troublesome nature of capitalism itself—both in and beyond Canada and Indonesia.

↩ en
原页 282

有人提出过其他 Bre-X 寓言，例如贪婪蒙蔽所有人双眼（Goold and Willis 1997: 267），或认为国际资金流动意味着企业必须与“奇特而麻烦的政权”打交道（Francis 1997: 232）。在加拿大以外，产生了这样一种寓言式解读：这就是加拿大企业的作风，那里的证券交易所是一片“监管上的蛮荒西部”（此语转引自 Winarno 1997: 208 所引美国大众媒体）。我的解读拒绝在明眼人与盲人之间作区分，而是要指出即使在一场骗局中也有钱可赚。我强调资本主义本身——无论在加拿大和印尼之内还是之外——那种奇特而麻烦的性质。

原页 282, 283

Muir’s vision of Nature seemed powerful and convincing in part because it helped resolve an imperial problem: Was California a part of the U.S. nation or part of its global empire? Yosemite National Park was a firm claim to the national status of the still-wild western states, Nationalizing nature brought the global-imperial agenda of travel, conquest, and awe into domestic, national space. Muir himself did not focus on this national problem; arriving in California on a boat, he could have been arriving in South America. He was not invested in the national project, but his vision articulated a new national presence for California. One reason that the parks model took off around the world is that it showed one way nation-states could incorporate the wild frontiers of their imperial ambitions.

↩ en
原页 282, 283

缪尔的自然观之所以显得有力而令人信服，部分原因在于它帮助解决了一个帝国问题：加利福尼亚是美国的一部分，还是其全球帝国的一部分？约塞米蒂国家公园坚定地主张了当时仍属荒野的西部各州作为国家一部分的地位。将自然纳入国家版图，把旅行、征服和敬畏这一全球—帝国议程带入了国内的国家空间。缪尔本人并未关注这一国家归属问题；他乘船抵达加利福尼亚，就像抵达南美洲一样。他并未投身国家建构计划，但他的视野为加利福尼亚表述出了一种新的国家存在方式。公园模式之所以在世界各地兴起，原因之一在于它展示了一种方式，使民族国家能够把其帝国野心的荒凉边疆纳入自身。

10
原页 283

The question of indigenous residents has been one of those challenges. Can advocates for nature move beyond Muir’s problematic relationship with Native Americans? Native Americans enter Muir’s vision in several ways. First, they are a troubling absence: the haunting absence of the dead. The genocidal murder of Native Americans in California contributed to the emptiness of Nature that Muir appreciated as the window to sacred presence. Native Americans had been hunted down and murdered; remnant groups were rounded up and forced into forts and resettlement areas, where many died. Only then could the environment to which na- tive livelihoods contributed come to seem the exclusive handiwork of God, laid out for the gaze of settlers. Second, Muir was not sympathetic to those Native Americans who remained. Yosemite Indians—so called by neighboring enemies—still inhabited the valley, although in small numbers. Muir’s writing contains only derogatory mention of them (Lankford 1991: 234). Besides being non-Christians, the native population joined white ranchers as users, rather than students, of nature. The reservation of the valley as a park did not help the native residents. Federal marshals rounded up the native population and evicted them from their lands. Yet, third, Muir scholars have argued that Native American philosophies inspired Muir’s vision of Nature. (See Fleck 1985.) This brings up contemporary challenges for the Muir legacy. In stating their support for indigenous communities, advocates of nature protection so often go directly to native philosophies. Other issues—such as subsistence and survival—are easily ignored. Indigenous leaders willing to endorse nature philosophies do well with nature protection groups; those who stress community development and resource use are drawn, instead, to alliances with developers. The common split within communities with some leaders arguing for support of environmentalists and others siding with developers is a piece of this legacy.

↩ en
原页 283

原住民居民问题一直属于这些挑战之一。自然的倡导者能否超越缪尔与美洲原住民之间那种成问题的关系？美洲原住民以多种方式进入缪尔的视野。首先，他们是一种令人不安的缺席：死者的萦绕不去之缺席。对加利福尼亚美洲原住民的种族灭绝式屠杀，助成了缪尔所欣赏的那种自然的空无——他把这空无视为通向神圣临在的窗口。美洲原住民遭到追捕和屠杀；残余群体被围捕，强迫迁入堡垒和重新安置区，许多人在那里死去。只有到那时，原住民生计所参与塑造的环境，才可能显得完全是上帝的杰作，铺展在定居者的凝视之下。其次，缪尔对留下来的美洲原住民并不同情。约塞米蒂印第安人——邻近敌对群体如此称呼他们——仍然居住在山谷中，尽管人数很少。缪尔的文字中只有对他们的贬损性提及（Lankford 1991: 234）。除了是非基督徒，原住民居民还和白人牧场主一样，是自然的使用者，而非学生。将山谷保留为公园，并没有帮助原住民居民。联邦法警围捕原住民人口，把他们逐出自己的土地。然而，第三，研究缪尔的学者们主张，美洲原住民的哲学启发了缪尔的自然观。（见 Fleck 1985。）这引出了缪尔遗产在当代面临的挑战。自然保护的倡导者在表示支持原住民社群时，往往直接诉诸原住民哲学。其他问题——如生计和生存——则容易被忽略。愿意为自然哲学背书的原住民领袖，与自然保护团体相处得很好；而那些强调社群发展和资源利用的人，则被吸引去与开发者结盟。社群内常见的分裂——一些领袖主张支持环保主义者，另一些则与开发者站在一起——正是这一遗产的一部分。

The Protocol allows countries to lower their emissions through business rather than environmental accounting: They can trade in emission reductions by buying figures showing reduced rates from other countries (“international emissions trade”) or by supporting emissions reductions wherever they are cheapest (“joint implementation”). However, for many business leaders, these concessions were not enough. See Demeritt (1999).

Caesar Sardi tells the story this way in his senior thesis (1995: 24): “Mapala UI [the University of Indonesia nature lovers’ group] was the first organization of university student nature lovers. Around 1964, a group of students from the Humanities Faculty, including Soe Hok Gie, Aristides Katoppo, Rudi Badil, Herman Lantang, and others, felt tired out by the play of politics at that time. The bringing together of nature lovers represented an organization that freed itself from politicization, when most student organizations were involved in political work to influence powerful elites.” Under New Order political repression, depoliticization moved way beyond their original frame of expectations. By the late New Order, the quietude of censorship was stifling, and at least some of the early nature lovers had become important activists, fighting for a wider breadth for political speech. Aristides Katoppo, for example, an environmentalist journalist, took a leading role in the independent journalists’ opposition to New Order censorship.

Soe Hok Gie’s remarkable essay “Conquering Mt. Slamet” (1995) relates his experience on one early nature lovers’ outing. In sharp contrast to more recent nature lovers’ essays, Soe is obviously immersed in the politics of the countryside. He describes his patriotic motives for nature loving: to get to know the country and to train to be a better citizen. He comments on the political strife that has shaped the Javanese landscape. Even at the top of the volcano, he engages in political debate— stimulated by pro-Sukarno graffiti—over freedom of speech.

The flexibility of the concept of “planting” is suggested by the way tree claims are tied to the whole range of ways, from deliberate to casual, of sprouting the tree. A Meratus who threw a durian seed out the door of her house while eating the fruit would never describe herself as “planting.” However, if the seed sprouted and grew, she would claim the tree as one of her planting, because of its timing and location next to her house. Fruit trees that sprouted in the area of someone's current house or swidden were always claimed by the householders as their trees unless they were planted with some ceremony by someone else (as, for example, when I was invited to plant durian for when I came back).

↩ en
原页 286

“种植”这一概念的灵活性，体现在树木所有权主张与各种使树发芽的方式——从刻意到随意——之间的联系上。一个梅拉图斯人在吃榴莲时把种子从家门扔出去，绝不会说自己在“种植”。然而，如果种子发芽生长，她就会主张这棵树是自己种植的，因为它发芽的时间与她居住于此的时期吻合，而且位置就在她家旁边。在某人现在的房屋或刀耕火种地范围内发芽的果树，除非是别人以某种仪式种下的（例如，我曾被邀请种下一棵榴莲树，以备我将来回来时享用），否则总是被住户声称为自己的树。

There are many kinds of huyi, each with long, flexible stems that are good for tying and weaving. Huyi lamab and huyi lantau are used for tying posts and bamboo walkways. Huyi galang and huyi irit are also good for tying; before the market was homogenized, they had good market value. Huyi lilin, “waxy rattan,” is a fine-stemmed rattan used whole, rather than split, to tie house floors. Huyi kaningai is similar, but it is only found in wet mountain saddles, in the kind of forest called gunungan. Huyi karas, “hard rattan,” has a more brittle stem. Huyi wariung is a dark-stemmed rattan with excellent weaving qualities; it makes the most durable back-baskets. Huyi dabanan is the stiffest of the rattans called huyi; it makes superior spear handles. There are also many rattans not classified as huyi, such as nangi, pikak, and ariwa.

E. P. Thompson (1975) describes the harsh laws created in England to enclose the forests, keeping out peasant “poachers.” In a similar spirit, Peter Sahlins ( 1994) describes the resistance of French peasants to the exclusivity of state and industrial forest claims. Nor were such enclosures limited to Europe: Gold and Gujar (2002) tell how royalty in Rajastan claimed exclusive privilege over the forest; as soon as the king was deposed, peasants flocked into these royal spaces, destroying them. The willingness of peasants to destroy forests leads many analysts to conclude that forest users cannot conserve. Yet this conclusion ignores the political history of elite expropriation, in which peasants and forests became pitted against each other.

2
原页 288

The governor may or may not have known that Banjar and Meratus languages, while close, are not identical; he also probably did not care, and this lack of attentiveness is one of the key translation practices here. He addressed the Meratus demonstrators as pian sampaian, “all of you [respected ones]” (Banjarmasin Post, March 15, 2000). Banjar language uses pronouns that differentiate listeners in terms of age and status; pian is respectful. Meratus language has no such status-differentiating pronouns. The governor's respect was thus contingent on Meratus willingness to consider themselves Banjar. Certainly, all the Meratus demonstrators understood the Banjar pronoun; they would have understood Indonesian, the national language, equally well. The point was not comprehension but the making of a form of populism that would work for the state, in alliance with the demonstrators.

↩ en
原页 288

省长也许知道、也许不知道班贾尔语和梅拉图斯语虽相近却并不相同；他很可能也不在意，而这种不留意正是这里的关键翻译实践之一。他称呼梅拉图斯示威者为 pian sampaian，“你们所有人〔受尊敬者〕”（Banjarmasin Post，2000年3月15日）。班贾尔语使用按年龄和地位区分听者的代词；pian 是敬称。梅拉图斯语没有这种区分地位的代词。因此，省长的尊重取决于梅拉图斯人是否愿意把自己视为班贾尔人。当然，所有梅拉图斯示威者都听懂了班贾尔语的代词；他们同样完全能听懂国语印尼语。问题不在于理解，而在于制造一种能为国家所用、并与示威者结盟的民粹主义。

In supporting the pro-Kodeco demonstrators, the governor spoke the very words Kodeco’s critics used to make their case. “[W]e will use [the natural resources of the Meratus Mountains] with care to the environment and conservation,” he began, continuing with the claim that, of course, the government would never allow any logging to which the populace did not agree and in which it did not participate (Banjarmasin Post, March 15, 2000). Participatory and environmentally friendly logging would be the government's goal. Kodeco would surely agree, and then it would be left to disgruntled environmentalists and Meratus residents to contest the practice of this agreement.

这种虚幻的“分享财富”包容性，也通过挪用对手的话语来运作。在支持亲 Kodeco 的示威者时，省长说的正是 Kodeco 批评者用来论证其立场的话。“我们将注意环境与保护，利用〔梅拉图斯山脉的自然资源〕，”他开口说道，接着声称政府当然绝不会允许任何民众不同意、也不参与的伐木活动（Banjarmasin Post，2000年3月15日）。参与式且环保的伐木将成为政府的目标。Kodeco 想必会同意，然后就轮到心怀不满的环保主义者和梅拉图斯居民来质疑这项协议的实际做法了。

3
原页 288, 289

Hardt and Negri (2000: 36) argue that transnational NGOs are at the forefront of a new disciplinary Empire: “These NGOs are completely immersed in the biopolitical context of the constitution of Empire; they anticipate the power of its pacifying and productive intervention of justice.” Other critics of global liberalism borrow the term “governmentality” from the writing of philosopher Michel Foucault, who analyzed the mechanisms of liberal power both in and out of state rule (Foucault 1991). Barry, Osborne, and Rose (1996) show the relevance of this analysis to the contemporary spread of liberalism. Readings of Foucault’s assessment of social movements differ; however, many anthropologists, environmental studies scholars, and critics of NGO politics have found in the concept of “governmentality” a route to discuss the role of environmentalism, feminism, and human rights in extending, rather than challenging, coercive power. For critiques of environmental initiatives, see Li (2003a) and Ferguson and Gupta (2002). Agrawal (2003) uses the term “environmentality” to discuss the regulative power of community forest management.

↩ en
原页 288, 289

Hardt 和 Negri（2000: 36）主张，跨国非政府组织处于一种新的规训性“帝国”的前沿：“这些非政府组织完全沉浸在帝国构成的生物政治语境中；它们先行体现了帝国那种安抚性和生产性的正义干预所具有的力量。”其他全球自由主义批评者借用哲学家 Michel Foucault 写作中的“治理术”一词；Foucault 分析了国家统治之内与之外的自由主义权力机制（Foucault 1991）。Barry、Osborne 和 Rose（1996）展示了这一分析对当代自由主义传播的相关性。对 Foucault 社会运动评价的解读各有不同；然而，许多人类学家、环境研究学者和非政府组织政治批评者发现，“治理术”概念提供了一条途径，用以讨论环保主义、女性主义和人权在扩展而非挑战强制性权力方面的作用。关于对环境倡议的批评，见 Li（2003a）和 Ferguson and Gupta（2002）。Agrawal（2003）使用“环境治理术”一词讨论社区森林管理的规制性权力。

↩ zh
4
原页 289

It is not useful to overestimate the heterogeneity of liberal projects around the world; in fact, there are enormous pressures toward standardization and consolidation. The coercions of structural adjustment packages; the intimacies of international conference culture; the prestige of northern training programs; the requirements for funding and participation in transnational organizations; the threat of international sanctions: Each of these and more facilitate standardization and consolidation of liberal programs. Yet none of these has much to do with liberal theories of synchronized self-regulation and perfect replication. Understanding the spread of liberalism requires getting outside of liberalism’s self-portrait.

↩ en
原页 289

不应高估世界各地自由主义项目的异质性；事实上，存在着朝向标准化和整合的巨大压力。结构调整方案中的强制；国际会议文化的亲密性；北方培训项目的声望；获取资助及参与跨国组织须满足的要求；国际制裁的威胁：每一项以及更多因素都促进自由主义项目的标准化与整合。然而，这些都与自由主义关于同步化自我规制和完美复制的理论没有多大关系。理解自由主义的传播，需要走出自由主义的自画像。

My discussion focuses on social mobilizations around the environment rather than on conservation bureaucracies or organizations. Conservation organizations and bureaucracies have often focused on the enforcement of environmental protection without regard for the social context in which protection has been proposed. The social dynamics of conservation enforcement require an entirely different analytic treatment. For a New Order example, see Peluso (1993); for a post-New Order discussion, see Lowe (2003).

↩ en
原页 289

我的讨论聚焦于围绕环境的社会动员，而非保护官僚机构或组织。保护组织和官僚机构往往专注于环境保护的执法，而不考虑提出保护时所处的社会语境。保护执法的社会动态需要一种完全不同的分析处理。关于新秩序时期的一个例子，见 Peluso（1993）；关于后新秩序时期的讨论，见 Lowe（2003）。

Government suspicion of the idea of nongovernmental organizations meant that a direct Indonesian translation of the term NGO could not be used in New Order Indonesia. “Nongovernmental” was interpreted as anti-state. Instead, the categories lembaga swadaya masyarakat (LSM)—“self-reliant community institutions,” and lembaga pembangunan swadaya masyarakat (LPSM)—“self-reliant community development institutions,” were used. Eldridge (1989) discusses the dilemmas of political dependence of these groups. Aditjondro (1990) discusses the community development counterculture some groups were able to promote, for example in designing alternative technology.

↩ en
原页 289

政府对非政府组织这一观念的怀疑，意味着 NGO 一词的印尼文直译不能在新秩序时期的印尼使用。“非政府的”被解释为反国家。于是改用 lembaga swadaya masyarakat（LSM）——“自力更生的社群机构”，以及 lembaga pembangunan swadaya masyarakat（LPSM）——“自力更生的社群发展机构”这两个类别。Eldridge（1989）讨论了这些团体在政治依赖上的困境。Aditjondro（1990）讨论了某些团体得以推行的社群发展反文化，例如在设计替代技术方面。

原页 290

Transnational NGOs operating in Indonesia chose varied relations to the national cause. In the 1990s, WWF-Indonesia engaged in national environmental politics. The national branch used divisions within the transnational organization to craft self-consciously Indonesian environmental strategies, for example, in acknowledging the draw of charismatic megafauna (tigers, pandas) on northern donors but funneling these funds into rebuilding social landscapes through what WWF called “integrated conservation and development projects.” In contrast, Greenpeace acted as a foreign presence in Indonesia. Young Indonesians were attracted to Greenpeace precisely because of the allure of the foreign. In contrast to WWF, Greenpeace materials were available only in English.

↩ en
原页 290

在印尼活动的跨国非政府组织，与民族事业建立了各种不同的关系。1990年代，WWF-Indonesia 参与了国家环境政治。这个国别分部利用跨国组织内部的分歧，制定自觉具有印尼特色的环境策略，例如，承认魅力型大型动物（老虎、熊猫）对北方捐助者的吸引力，却把这些资金引入重建社会地景的工作，通过 WWF 所谓的“综合保护与发展项目”。相比之下，Greenpeace 在印尼以外国存在的身份行动。年轻印尼人被 Greenpeace 吸引，恰恰因为外国的魅力。与 WWF 不同，Greenpeace 的材料只有英文版。

原页 290

The term “liberal” was not a New Order piece of rhetoric. New Order politicians called Indonesia a “panca sila democracy” in contrast to a “liberal democracy” to argue for the importance of consensus. (Panca Sila are the five official principles of citizenship.) Yet international liberalism shaped the state and its bureaucracy, including its embrace of the rhetoric of law, elections, property, and the like. Meanwhile, the term liberal was available in translation for varied nonofficial uses. In the late 1990s, for example, a group formed calling itself Islam Liberal to differentiate itself from Islamicism.

↩ en
原页 290

“自由主义的”一词并不是新秩序时期的修辞。新秩序政治家把印尼称为“潘查希拉民主”，与“自由民主”相对，以论证共识的重要性。（潘查希拉是五项官方公民原则。）然而，国际自由主义塑造了国家及其官僚机构，包括其对法律、选举、财产等修辞的接纳。与此同时，“liberal”一词在翻译中可用于各种非官方用途。例如，1990年代末，一个团体成立并自称“自由伊斯兰”（Islam Liberal），以区别于伊斯兰主义。

原页 290, 291

A series of articles in Kritis in 1990 and 1991 offers the flavor of national debate about the Kedung Ombo campaign. Aditjondro (1990) opens with a criticism of the mobilization for ignoring “structural” features of big dam building—such as bureaucratic centralization and the Green Revolution destruction of peasant agriculture—in favor of raising sympathy for dam victims. He writes of the importance of long-term “cultural critique,” including appropriate technology movements, and warns against too quick a celebration of the campaign’s success. In a follow-up article, Arief Budiman (1990) picks up this last point to lambast Aditjondro for cynicism and to offer an optimistic account of the possibilities for NGOs and student activists to work together. Student activists open up issues, he says, while NGOs follow up on them. Aditjondro (1991b) replies angrily, and Riwanto Tirtosudarmo (1991) wraps up the exchange by reminding readers of the weakness of all oppositional politics in New Order Indonesia.

↩ en
原页 290, 291

1990和1991年《Kritis》上的一系列文章，呈现了围绕 Kedung Ombo 运动的全国辩论风味。Aditjondro（1990）开篇批评这场动员忽视了大型水坝建设的“结构性”特征——如官僚集中化和绿色革命对农民农业的破坏——而偏向于为水坝受害者争取同情。他谈到长期“文化批评”的重要性，包括适用技术运动，并警告不要过早庆祝运动的成功。在后续文章中，Arief Budiman（1990）抓住最后一点，痛斥 Aditjondro 的冷嘲，并提出一种乐观论述：非政府组织与学生行动者可以合作。他说，学生行动者开辟议题，非政府组织则跟进。Aditjondro（1991b）愤怒回应，Riwanto Tirtosudarmo（1991）在总结这场交锋时提醒读者，新秩序印尼所有反对派政治都很软弱。

In the mid-1990s, for example, the organization Sejati published pamphlets by and about Indonesia’s cultural minorities, highlighting their strong traditions of customary law. To make them accessible to a wide audience, they made the publications beautiful with photographs and gave them Indonesian and sometimes English texts, augmented by fragments in the regional language. Sejati was particularly interested in convincing Indonesian elites that minority cultures were worth nurturing within the national plan. In one project, they worked jointly with a major bank, offering books to its customers to educate them about Indonesia’s rich but vulnerable cultural diversity (Brown 1994). Films also spread their message. Other activists, however, objected to Sejati’s culturalist and elitist objectives.

↩ en

My discussion of the incident with LPMA activists later was inconclusive. Certainly, they knew both stories well.

8
原页 293, 294

At one Ford-supported conference, Walter Coward, director of the Rural Poverty Alleviation Program, offered his reflections on the genesis of CBNRM during his tenure at Ford. His story stresses two conjunctures through which the idea became charismatic enough to travel. The first was his discovery of small-scale, “community-based” irrigation at precisely that moment when development agencies were obsessed with large-scale irrigation. Coward relates how Philippine villagers showed him sophisticated local systems of irrigation. International developers had ignored these small-scale systems; they wanted big dams. Small-scale irrigation could be the perfect symbol for the alternative: not Big Dams, but small dams; not Big Development, but community-based development. The political will to support local forms of resource management owes a great deal to the fact that small-scale irrigation was such an apt carrier for the idea of community (Coward forthcoming).

The second conjuncture was the extension of community-based irrigation to build the idea of community-based forestry. Coward told conference attendees how he arrived in Indonesia, as a Ford Foundation program officer, with ideas he had developed in the Philippines about small-scale irrigation. There he met foresters worried about forest destruction and the loss of rural livelihoods. Thinking together, they hatched a larger domain of “community-based natural resource management”: Community irrigation models could help reorganize forestry. Two kinds of charisma were gained in this articulation. First, CBNRM took off toward many resources, becoming a general resource-management model: Soon, for example, Ford was thinking about community-based fisheries. Second, a new set of allies was acquired. Conservationists were worried about forests; indigenous rights groups worried about forest communities. The Ford Foundation was not ready to endorse either conservation or indigenous rights; however, their programs gained momentum from the impetus of these overlapping causes.

↩ en
原页 293, 294

在一次福特基金会支持的会议上，农村减贫项目主任 Walter Coward 谈了他对 CBNRM 在其福特任职期间起源的反思。他的叙述强调两个契机，这一观念正是通过它们获得了足以传播的感召力。第一个契机是他在发展机构正痴迷于大规模灌溉之时，发现了小规模、“以社群为基础”的灌溉。Coward 讲述了菲律宾村民如何向他展示当地复杂的灌溉系统。国际开发者曾忽视这些小规模系统；他们想要大型水坝。小规模灌溉可以成为替代方案的完美象征：不是大坝，而是小坝；不是大发展，而是以社群为基础的发展。支持地方资源管理形式的政治意愿，很大程度上归功于小规模灌溉是如此适合承载社群观念（Coward forthcoming）。

第二个契机是，以社群为基础的灌溉被扩展，用以建构以社群为基础的林业观念。Coward 向与会者讲述了他作为福特基金会项目官员抵达印尼的经历，带着他在菲律宾形成的关于小规模灌溉的想法。在那里，他遇到了担忧森林破坏和乡村生计丧失的林务员。他们一起思考，构想出一个更大的“以社群为基础的自然资源管理”领域：社群灌溉模式可以帮助重组林业。这种接合获得了两种感召力。第一，CBNRM 向多种资源扩展，成为一种普遍的资源管理模式：例如，福特很快开始考虑以社群为基础的渔业。第二，获得了一批新的盟友。保护主义者担忧森林；原住民权利团体担忧森林社群。福特基金会尚未准备好为保护或原住民权利中的任何一方背书；然而，他们的项目从这些相互重叠事业的推动力中获得了势头。

↩ zh
9
原页 294, 295

Consider, for example, the influential Zimbabwean initiative called CAMPFIRE. CAMPFIRE offers rural communities a share of the income gained from international big game hunting if they conserve local wildlife. CAMPFIRE is a very different model of community-based conservation than that discussed so far. Rather than working to conserve resources for village use, this program offers villagers a quid pro quo: Put up with the wildlife, which compete with village cattle and destroy village crops, in exchange for a share in the sometimes considerable revenues of big game hunting. This striking arrangement brings us directly to the particularity of collaborative partners, which range from rich white hunters, willing to pay top dollars for trophies, to a national government unwilling to provide for rural citizens directly.

In a history of the program, CAMPFIRE’s founder, Marshall Murphree, portrays it as a set of strategic compromises in which the “congruent objectives” of allies could be tweaked into a practical arrangement (Murphree forthcoming). The compromises, he admitted, helped explain the failures of the program as well as its successes; for example, by allowing local government to count as “community,” the program became entwined with government's own corruption and inequality. Critics of CAMPFIRE have charged that the program is just too deeply intertwined with bad collaborators. Conservation for the benefit of big game hunters fits too neatly into the colonial legacy of native displacement in East Africa; government management objectives join too poorly with local empowerment (Neumann forthcoming; Matowanyika 1997). Questions about community resource management only open wider: When do contingent collaborations negate utopian hopes leaving only practical—and unworthy—solutions? When does CBNRM become a top-down management scheme?

One response to these questions assessed the influence of CAMPFIRE with a cautious optimism. Ken Wilson, a Ford Foundation program officer in Mozambique, found that the inspiration of CAMPFIRE encouraged national elites in Mozambique to support community resource management in the 1990s (Wilson forthcoming). At that time, the political climate in Mozambique differed sharply from that in Zimbabwe, in his assessment. Where Zimbabwe offered top-down management, Mozambique allowed models to “bubble up” from local sources. Community resource experiments could be worked out in relation to a more circumscribed and relevant set of players, from shamans to foresters. Communities could be negotiated closer to the ground. In Wilson’s story, CAMPFIRE facilitated a combination of local initiative and international backing.

↩ en
原页 294, 295

例如，考虑一下津巴布韦颇具影响力的 CAMPFIRE 计划。如果乡村社群保护当地野生动物，CAMPFIRE 就把国际大型猎物狩猎所得收入的一部分分给它们。CAMPFIRE 是一种与本篇迄今所讨论的模式非常不同的以社群为基础的保护模式。该计划不是努力保护资源供村庄使用，而是向村民提出一种交换条件：忍受与村庄牲畜竞争并毁坏村庄作物的野生动物，以换取有时相当可观的大型猎物狩猎收入的一部分。这种引人注目的安排把我们直接带到协作伙伴的特殊性：从愿意为战利品一掷千金的富有白人猎人，到不愿直接供养乡村公民的国家政府。

在该计划的一部历史中，CAMPFIRE 的创始人 Marshall Murphree 将其描绘为一系列战略妥协，在其中盟友的“一致目标”可以被调整成一种实际安排（Murphree forthcoming）。他承认，这些妥协既有助于解释该计划的失败，也有助于解释其成功；例如，由于允许地方政府算作“社群”，该计划与政府自身的腐败和不平等纠缠在一起。CAMPFIRE 的批评者指控，该计划与糟糕的合作者纠缠得过深。为大型猎物狩猎者利益服务的保护，过于契合东非原住民被驱逐的殖民遗产；政府管理目标与地方赋权的结合又过于糟糕（Neumann forthcoming; Matowanyika 1997）。关于社群资源管理的问题只会越发拓展：偶然的协作何时会否定乌托邦希望，只留下实用——却无价值——的解决方案？CBNRM 何时会变成自上而下的管理制度？

对这些问题的回应之一，以谨慎的乐观评估了 CAMPFIRE 的影响。福特基金会在莫桑比克的项目官员 Ken Wilson 发现，CAMPFIRE 的启发鼓励了莫桑比克的国家精英在1990年代支持社群资源管理（Wilson forthcoming）。据他评估，当时莫桑比克的政治气候与津巴布韦截然不同。津巴布韦提供的是自上而下的管理，而莫桑比克允许模式从地方源头“冒上来”。社群资源实验可以围绕一组更有限、也更相关的参与者来设计，从萨满到林务员。社群可以在更贴近地面的层面上被协商。在 Wilson 的叙述中，CAMPFIRE 促成了地方首创精神与国际支持的结合。

校注：原文称门德斯于1979年加入劳工党。劳工党及其历史档案机构记载，正式成立大会举行于1980年2月10日，筹组活动则已在1978—1979年展开。因此原文年份与正式建党时间不合，也可能涉及筹组时期；现有核验不足以确定门德斯个人加入的具体日期，故不擅改为另一年。

校注9 · 克朗代克的位置

校注：原文将克朗代克称作“阿拉斯加的”。美国国家公园管理局将1896年发现黄金的克朗代克河地区定位于加拿大育空；阿拉斯加是这场淘金潮的重要通道和相关活动地区。正文保留底本地理表述。

  • 美国国家公园管理局：What Was the Klondike Gold Rush?

校注10 · 美国与京都议定书的法律地位

校注：原文使用2001年“退出”的概括。联合国条约状态表列美国于1998年11月12日签署，但无批准记录；布什政府于2001年明确反对该议定书。因此此处应理解为放弃支持及参与落实的政治立场，不能等同于已批准的缔约方正式退约。

校注11 · 1997年谈判与2000年目标期限

校注：本注把1997年京都谈判与未兑现里约承诺相联系。1992年公约所述回到1990年排放水平的目标期限为2000年；1997年时期限尚未届满。因此不能把本注表述直接理解为所有国家已经在截止日违约。本次核验未逐国审核提前达标情况，原注文字予以保留。

    校注13 · ITTO“2000年目标”的形成时间

    校注：原文写1991年通过该目标，同时引用1990年的评论。ITTO自身资料存在不同阶段的记年：一份会议文集称1990年采纳，ITTO手册则称1991年理事会采纳。因此仅凭此处先后关系不能断定引文或年份错误；正文与引文年份均保留，读者应区分目标提出、承诺与正式采纳的过程。

    • ITTO会议文集：Opening Session
    • ITTO Handbook

    校注14 · 原木出口禁令与出口税

    校注：本注先说1992年禁令改为出口税，随后又称1998年取消禁令。世界银行资料确认1992年的替代；印尼1998年1月15日致IMF的政策备忘录第37段提出削减原木等出口税，7月备忘录列出调整后的分阶段税率安排。因此1998年这里宜理解为放松此前具有强限制作用的出口措施，而非首次撤销1992年已被替代的禁令。保留底本措辞；政策承诺不等于已按原定日期执行。

    • 世界银行：印尼经济报告，第3.14段
    • 印尼政策备忘录，1998-01-15
    • 印尼政策备忘录，1998-07-29
    返回相关段落

    校注15 · 自由港停产与保险事件的年份

    校注：底本将骚乱停产记为1995年，并将OPIC取消保险接在1996年事件之后。自由港公司截至1996年9月的10-Q季报记载，导致矿山和选矿厂停产约三天的骚乱发生于1996年3月。挪威政府养老基金伦理委员会2006年报告记载，OPIC于1995年10月撤销保险，1996年4月暂时恢复。这里保留底本记年；这项核对不代表认可公司的事件定性，也未独立核验该段全部诉讼及环境责任叙述。

    • Freeport-McMoRan，1996年第三季度10-Q（报告镜像）
    • 挪威政府养老基金伦理委员会2006年报，第47页
    返回相关段落

    校注：底本写A. elastica和A. champeden，正文照录。英国皇家植物园Kew的POWO数据库采用Artocarpus elasticus；并将Artocarpus champeden列为Artocarpus integer var. integer的异名。这里提供检索名称，不把异名一概视为误写，也不据此重新鉴定作者田野中的具体植物。

    • Kew：Artocarpus elasticus
    • Kew：Artocarpus champeden

    • Kew：Antiaris toxicaria

    校注18 · kaladan的暂定学名

    • Kew标本K001396019

    校注19 · 猩猩取食农作物的概括

    校注：此处“猩猩甚至不偷庄稼”是作者的概括。Orangutan Foundation于2013年发表的救援记录提到一只被报告取食农作物的成年雄性猩猩。因此这句话不宜理解为没有例外的物种行为断言。该记录晚于本书出版，且本项核查未验证同句关于攻击人的概括。
